### R-389: 404 pages ignore the visitor's stored theme: the not-found response is Next's error shell and the inline theme boot script never runs
- Severity: Low
- Category: Bug
- Status: CONFIRMED
- Location: src/app/layout.tsx:L50-L64; src/app/[locale]/[category]/page.tsx:L46; src/app/[locale]/[category]/[slug]/page.tsx:L38-L40
- Evidence:

  `src/app/layout.tsx:L54-L63`

  ```tsx
            dangerouslySetInnerHTML={{
              // Boot script, docs/design/identity.md §5.2: data-theme only for a stored choice (otherwise the CSS
              // media query follows the OS); data-motion="full" is the only flag that arms motion. data-intro marks the
              // first full-motion load of the browser session, for the brand mark intro (R3-V14, §5.5 M26).
              __html: `(function(){var d=document.documentElement,r=null;
  try{var t=localStorage.getItem('theme');if(t==='light'||t==='dark')d.setAttribute('data-theme',t)}catch(e){}
  ```

  Output of (command) curl -s http://127.0.0.1:3100/en/does-not-exist | head -c 120 (local production build):

  ```text
  status 404
  <!DOCTYPE html><html id="__next_error__"><head><meta charSet="utf-8"/>...
  ```

  Output of (command) Chromium probe, localStorage theme=dark, prefers-color-scheme light: MutationObserver on <html> from the first byte:

  ```text
  /en/does-not-exist
    15ms html element first seen data-theme=null
    20ms DOMContentLoaded data-theme=null
    102ms load data-theme=null
    130ms attr id: "__next_error__" -> null
    131ms attr lang: null -> "en"
    131ms attr class: null -> "textlatin_… displaygreek_…"
  /en/privacy
    2ms html element first seen data-theme=null
    24ms attr data-theme: null -> "dark"
    52ms DOMContentLoaded data-theme=dark
  ```

  Verification: Lead runtime check on the local production build (axe-themes.ts, shots.ts, probe-ui.ts); not from an agent.

- Problem: For a URL that ends in notFound() (an unknown category or item, e.g. /en/does-not-exist or /en/moments/no-such-item), the server answers 404 with Next's error document (<html id="__next_error__">), and the root layout is rendered on the client about 130 ms later. React does not execute a <script> whose content is set with dangerouslySetInnerHTML when it renders it on the client, so the theme boot script never runs on these pages: data-theme stays unset, while on every normal page the script sets it before DOMContentLoaded. The server log shows no error for these requests, so this is how the 404s are served, not a crash. Why Next chooses the error document here was not traced.
- Impact: A visitor who chose Night (dark) in the theme switch on a device whose OS is in light mode, or Day on a dark-mode device, sees every 404 page in the other theme. Seen in all 32 stored-theme 404 states of the lead's scans (en, el, 390 and 1440 px, both motion settings); every 200 page honoured the stored theme.
- Fix:

  Apply the stored choice from client code as well, so a client-rendered root gets it too. Minimal: a small client component rendered in the root layout next to the script (or the existing theme subscription in ThemeSwitch moved into it) that, in a layout effect, does what the boot script does when the attribute is missing:

  ```text
    useLayoutEffect(() => {
      if (document.documentElement.hasAttribute('data-theme')) return;
      try {
        const t = localStorage.getItem('theme');
        if (t === 'light' || t === 'dark') document.documentElement.setAttribute('data-theme', t);
      } catch {}
    }, []);
  ```

- Severity: Low

- Problem: The admin banner states a 12-hour threshold, while the flag it displays uses the 3-hour alert threshold (and is also true before any sync of a configured calendar). The text names the wrong constant and the component test locks it in.
- Impact: After the stale alert fires at about 3 h 05 min, the owner opens /admin/availability and reads that the calendar has not synced in the last 12 hours, while 'Last success' on the same card shows a time three hours ago. Right after AIRBNB_ICAL_URL is first configured the same sentence appears before any sync was due. Confusing, and it can lead the owner to misjudge how long the public calendar has been stale; no data is affected.

  and change tests/components/admin-availability.test.tsx L287 to expect '... in the last 3 hours.' (the JSX renders the number as a separate text node inside the same <p>, so getByText on the full sentence still matches the element's text content only if a function matcher or the exact rendered string is used; check the assertion).

### R-391: An open check-in page never picks up the Wi-Fi details when the disclosure time passes; the notice then shows a past time or 'Unavailable'
- Severity: Low
- Category: Bug
- Status: CONFIRMED
- Location: src/components/CheckInInfo.tsx:L460-L483; src/components/CheckInInfo.tsx:L637-L642; src/components/CheckInInfo.tsx:L709
- Evidence:

  `src/components/CheckInInfo.tsx:L460-L483`

  ```tsx
    useEffect(() => {
      const loadPreferences = async () => {
        try {
          const res = await internalFetch('/api/check-in/preferences');
          if (res.ok) {
  ...
              setWifiNetwork(data.data.wifi?.network || '');
              setWifiPassword(data.data.wifi?.password || '');
              setWifiAvailableAt(typeof data.data.wifiAvailableAt === 'string' ? data.data.wifiAvailableAt : null);
  ...
      loadPreferences();
    }, []);
  ```

  `src/components/CheckInInfo.tsx:L639-L642`

  ```tsx
    const wifiRevealAt = wifiAvailableAt ? new Date(wifiAvailableAt) : null;
    const wifiNotice = !wifiNetwork && wifiRevealAt && wifiRevealAt.getTime() > Date.now()
      ? `${ui.wifiAvailableFrom} ${new Intl.DateTimeFormat(...).format(wifiRevealAt)}`
      : null;
  ```

  `src/components/CheckInInfo.tsx:L709`

  ```tsx
                <dd className="checkin-mono">{wifiNetwork || wifiNotice || ui.unavailable}</dd>
  ```

  `src/app/api/check-in/preferences/route.ts:L90-L97`

  ```ts
        wifiAvailableAt = revealAt.toISOString();
        const now = new Date();
        if (now >= revealAt && now <= expiresAt) {
          wifi = {
            network: process.env.GUEST_WIFI_NETWORK || '',
            password: process.env.GUEST_WIFI_PASSWORD || '',
  ```

  Verification: Found by F8. Verifier: upheld (read-all-paths).

- Problem: The Wi-Fi details and wifiAvailableAt are fetched once when the page mounts. The server includes the credentials only after revealAt, and the client never fetches again: there is no timer at wifiAvailableAt, no visibilitychange handler and no refresh. A page opened before the window therefore never shows the Wi-Fi details. Its notice keeps the now-past 'Available from <time>' until some unrelated re-render, after which the summary and the Wi-Fi card show 'Unavailable'.
- Impact: A guest opens /check-in the evening before arrival and sees 'Available from 14 Oct 2026, 15:00'. They leave the tab open. At the door the next afternoon, the same tab, if the browser did not discard it, shows no network or password: either the stale 'Available from' or 'Unavailable'. Nothing prompts a reload. A manual reload fixes it, and the server guard renews an expired session through /portal/refresh. The guest is inconvenienced, nothing is lost, and the host may get a call.
- Fix:

  Reload the page shortly after the reveal time, unless the guest is typing an arrival request. The server guard then also handles the 2 h session expiry, which a client-only refetch would not. Insert after the two loaders:
  ```tsx
  useEffect(() => {
    if (wifiNetwork || !wifiAvailableAt || isRequestingArrival) return;
    const delay = new Date(wifiAvailableAt).getTime() - Date.now();
    if (!(delay > 0) || delay > 2_147_483_647) return;
    const timer = window.setTimeout(() => window.location.reload(), delay + 1_000);
    return () => window.clearTimeout(timer);
  }, [wifiAvailableAt, wifiNetwork, isRequestingArrival]);
  ```
- Fix risk: A reload while the arrival-request form is open would discard the guest's text, hence the isRequestingArrival guard. Timers in background or frozen tabs are delayed until the tab resumes, which is acceptable here. Test: a fake-timer component test that renders with wifiAvailableAt a few seconds ahead, advances past it and asserts window.location.reload was called (stub location), plus a test that it is not called when wifi is already present or the reveal time is in the past (the existing 'keeps Unavailable once the window has passed' test must still pass).
- Resolution: FIXED in follow-up task T13 (Check-in page shows the Wi-Fi details once the disclosure time passes); changes are uncommitted, patch .runtime/review-patches/R4-T13.patch. Regression tests: tests/components/checkin-wifi.test.tsx.

### R-392: build-workers.mjs output-directory guard admits the repository root (argument '' or '.'), so rm -rf runs on the whole checkout
- Severity: Low
- Category: Bug
- Status: CONFIRMED
- Location: scripts/build-workers.mjs:L11-L19
- Evidence:

  `scripts/build-workers.mjs:L11-L19`

  ```js
  const root = path.resolve(path.dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)), '..');
  const outdir = path.resolve(root, process.argv[2] ?? 'dist/workers');
  if (path.relative(root, outdir).startsWith('..')) {
    throw new Error('The output directory must stay inside the repository');
  }
  ...
  await rm(outdir, { recursive: true, force: true });
  ```

  `tests/unit/build-workers.test.ts:L6-L9`

  ```ts
  // Vitest runs with the repository root as cwd. The bundler refuses locations outside the
  // repository, and `dist/` is its default output, so use a sibling temporary directory.
  const outdir = mkdtempSync('tmp-build-workers-');
  ```

  `docker/Dockerfile.security:L25`

  ```text
  RUN npm run build:workers
  ```

  Verification: Found by T3. Verifier: upheld (executed).

- Problem: The guard only tests whether the relative path starts with '..'. It therefore accepts the repository root itself (relative path '' from an empty argument or '.') and every top-level directory (src, prisma, .git, scripts), and the following rm() deletes it recursively before esbuild runs. The same test wrongly rejects an in-repo directory whose name begins with '..'.
- Impact: Only an explicit, unusual argument triggers it: someone runs `node scripts/build-workers.mjs "$OUT"` with OUT unset, or passes '.' meaning 'build here'. No caller in the tree does (Dockerfile and npm script pass nothing; the test passes a mkdtemp name). If it happens on the owner's machine, the checkout is deleted including untracked files git cannot restore: .env.local (the CARTO key and dev peppers live only there, per O28), .runtime/ scratch data and node_modules. The script then fails inside esbuild because its entry points are gone. Tracked files can be restored from git.
- Fix:

  ```diff
  --- a/scripts/build-workers.mjs
  +++ b/scripts/build-workers.mjs
  -if (path.relative(root, outdir).startsWith('..')) {
  -  throw new Error('The output directory must stay inside the repository');
  -}
  +const relativeOutdir = path.relative(root, outdir);
  +if (
  +  relativeOutdir === ''
  +  || relativeOutdir === '..'
  +  || relativeOutdir.startsWith(`..${path.sep}`)
  +  || path.isAbsolute(relativeOutdir)
  +) {
  +  throw new Error('The output directory must be a subdirectory of the repository');
  +}
  ```

  (Verified on a scratch copy as described in the trace. It does not stop 'src' or 'scripts'; refusing an outdir that contains an entry point or a tracked directory would be a separate, optional hardening.)
- Fix risk: tests/unit/build-workers.test.ts passes 'tmp-build-workers-XXXXXX', which stays accepted; I did not run that test (forbidden, writes to the repo root). Do not add a regression test that calls the real script with '' or '.' against the checkout: if the guard ever regressed, the test would delete the repository. Test it on a temp copy of the script with a stub esbuild, as done here.
- Resolution: FIXED in follow-up task T14 (build-workers refuses the repository root as its output directory); changes are uncommitted, patch .runtime/review-patches/R4-T14.patch.

- Severity: Low

- Evidence:

  ```ts
      const { rule, season, cents } = climateFeeOnNight(night, feeSchedule);
  ```

  ```tsx
            <span key={`${group.season}-${group.cents}`}>
              {`${group.nights} × ${price(group.cents)} ${describeMonths(group.months, locale, 'short')}`}
            </span>
          ))}
  ```

  ```text
  $ TZ=Europe/Athens npx --no-install tsx --tsconfig tsconfig.json .../verify-D7/run.tsx S4   (CLIMATE_FEE_SCHEDULE + hypothetical rule from 2027-01-01: high 1000, low 200; stay 2026-12-28 to 2027-01-03; real StaySummary rendered with React DOM in jsdom)
  groups: [{"season":"low","months":[1,2,3,11,12],"cents":200,"nights":4,"amountCents":800},{"season":"low","months":[1,2,3,11,12],"cents":200,"nights":2,"amountCents":400}]
  detail: <span>4 × €2 Nov–Mar</span><span>2 × €2 Nov–Mar</span>

  fee total 1200 sum groups 1200
  ```

- Problem: The fee breakdown's React keys do not match the grouping: climateFeeGroups keeps nights of different fee rules apart even when season and amount are equal, and StaySummary keys the spans by season and cents only.
- Impact: Latent with the single rule in force. Once a dated rule is appended that changes only the April-October amount (the documented way to change the schedule), a stay across its effectiveFrom date shows '4 × €2 Nov–Mar' and '2 × €2 Nov–Mar' as two indistinguishable lines and React reports a duplicate key, which makes reconciliation of that list undefined on later selection changes. The total stays correct.

  Merging groups that look identical (keying climateFeeGroups by season, cents and months instead of effectiveFrom|season) would also remove the double line, but it changes the documented contract and the stay-quote test at L342; that is a lead decision.
- Fix risk: Index keys are safe for this static, order-stable list (no per-item state). Test: render StaySummary (or the planner with a mocked two-rule schedule) for a stay across the new rule's effectiveFrom where the low amount is unchanged; expect no console.error and the two detail lines.
- Resolution: DEFERRED to the owner by the decision agent (2026-10-09): The key collision only happens once a dated climate-fee rule exists, so it is fixed (index keys, O65) inside the deferred R3-L6/L7 fee-schedule task.

The spec requires no hover on a disabled Button. The hover rules and the ::after glint rule lack the disabled guard that the lift rule (L395), IconButton hover (L127) and the magnetic pull already have.
- Impact: A desktop guest on /{locale}/guest hovers the disabled Sign in submit (form not yet valid, or while loading): it darkens to primary-hover and the glint sweeps across it while the cursor shows not-allowed, so it reads as clickable. Same for the disabled Copy Wi-Fi button when the Wi-Fi data is missing, and for Save, Send request and Cancel while a request is saving in CheckInInfo.   -    :root[data-motion="full"] .ui-btn.ui-btn--primary:hover::after { ... }
  ```diff
  +    :root[data-motion="full"] .ui-btn.ui-btn--primary:hover:not(:disabled):not([aria-disabled="true"])::after { ... }
  ```

  Optionally add the same aria-disabled guard to L383 and L395 for consistency (no ui-btn uses aria-disabled today).
- Fix risk: The guarded hover selectors rise from (0,3,0) to (0,5,0) specificity; no other rule targets .ui-btn hover colours, so ordering is unaffected. Test: hover an enabled and a disabled primary, secondary and ghost button with a mouse in light and dark with data-motion=full and reduced; run tests/unit/motion-css-gate.test.ts and tests/components/stay-routes.test.tsx (both only parse ui.css). The `:not(a):not(b)` form is already used in this sheet.
- Resolution: DECLINED by the decision agent (2026-10-09): Hover styling on disabled buttons is cosmetic and desktop-only, and the click is already blocked.

- Problem: The only recovery action of both error boundaries is the legacy reset(), which clears the boundary state and re-renders the already received segment without a new request. For a Server Component failure the cached error is rendered again at once. Since Next 16.3.0 the documented recovery is the stable retry(), which refreshes the router inside a transition and then clears the state.
- Impact: The DB container restarts during a deploy (single VPS). A guest who is signed in opens /en/check-in, or the admin opens /admin: the page throws on the server and the localized error page appears. The DB is back seconds later, the person taps "Try again" and gets the same error page immediately with no network request; only Home or a manual reload helps. The label promises a retry that does not happen. No data is affected.
- Fix:

  Use the stable prop in both boundaries and the test:

  ```diff
  --- src/app/error.tsx
  -  reset: () => void;
  +  retry: () => void;
  -export default function GlobalError({ error, reset }: GlobalErrorProps) {
  +export default function GlobalError({ error, retry }: GlobalErrorProps) {
  -onClick={() => reset()}
  +onClick={() => retry()}
  --- src/app/[locale]/error.tsx
  -export default function LocaleError({ error, reset }: { ...; reset: () => void }) {
  +export default function LocaleError({ error, retry }: { ...; retry: () => void }) {
  -onClick={() => reset()}
  +onClick={() => retry()}
  ```

  Update the two comments that say "(reset)" (error.tsx L16, [locale]/error.tsx L10). In tests/components/locale-not-found.test.tsx L68-74 rename the spy to `retry`, pass `retry={retry}` and assert it is called once; L83 `reset={vi.fn()}` -> `retry={vi.fn()}`.
- Fix risk: retry() calls router.refresh(), so a deterministic server bug still shows the error page again (as with reset()). Needs: the updated tests/components/locale-not-found.test.tsx (the boundary test currently pins reset and passes at HEAD: 8 passed) and typecheck (the Greek test renders the component with the old prop). Optional manual check under next start: stop the DB, open /en/check-in with a valid guest session, restart the DB, click "Try again".
- Resolution: FIXED in follow-up task T15 (Error boundaries retry the server render and report locale errors); changes are uncommitted, patch .runtime/review-patches/R4-T15.patch. Regression tests: tests/components/locale-not-found.test.tsx.

### R-397: GR-origin claim stores 10-digit numbers starting with 0 that sign-in and the admin phone search can never resolve from the same input
- Severity: Low
- Category: Bug
- Status: CONFIRMED
- Location: src/lib/phone.ts:L18-L23; src/lib/phone.ts:L44-L49
- Evidence:

  `src/lib/phone.ts:L18-L23`

  ```ts
    // Greek local auto-prefix (+30) for 10-digit locals
    if (origin === 'GR' && /^\d{10}$/.test(raw)) {
      // Basic local sanity: leading 2 (landline) or 6/7/8/9 (mobiles vary); don't overfit
      const prefixed = `+30${raw}`;
      return isE164(prefixed) ? { e164: prefixed } : null;
    }
  ```

  `src/lib/phone.ts:L44-L48`

  ```ts
  export function phoneLookupCandidates(input: string): string[] {
    const primary = normalizePhone(input);
    if (!primary) return [];
  ```

  `src/lib/portalAuthService.ts:L315-L316`

  ```ts
    const phoneCandidates = phoneLookupCandidates(input.phone);
    if (phoneCandidates.length === 0) throw new PortalAuthError('INVALID_CREDENTIALS');
  ```

  `prisma/migrations/20260714150000_trustworthy_portal_and_operations/migration.sql:L61-L62`

  ```sql
    ADD CONSTRAINT "users_phone_e164_check"
    CHECK ("phone_e164" ~ '^\+[1-9][0-9]{7,14}$');
  ```

  Output of scratch/phone-and-dates.ts (real src/lib/phone.ts):

  ```text
  claim GR "0123456789" -> {"e164":"+300123456789"} | lookup []
  DB regex accepts +300123456789: true
  ```

  Verification: Found by S3.2. Verifier: upheld (executed). Refuter: upheld, severity Low.

- Problem: With origin GR, normalizePhone turns any 10-digit string into +30 followed by those digits, including strings with a leading 0. The comment promises a leading-digit sanity check that the code does not do. phoneLookupCandidates (sign-in and admin search) rejects the same input because its first reading '+0…' is invalid. Claim and lookup therefore disagree on exactly these inputs. R-265/R-351 fixed the lookup side only for valid Greek locals.
- Impact: A guest selects 'Greece' and types a 10-digit number with a leading trunk 0, for example a French mobile 06 12 34 56 78. The claim succeeds and stores +300612345678. Every later sign-in with the same typed number fails with 'Invalid phone number or password', and the host's phone search finds nothing. The guest gets back in only by typing '+30 0612…' or through a host access reset. The stored number is also not the guest's real number.
- Fix:

  ```diff
  -  if (origin === 'GR' && /^\d{10}$/.test(raw)) {
  +  if (origin === 'GR' && /^[1-9]\d{9}$/.test(raw)) {
  ```

  The leading-0 input then falls through to the international branch, where '+0…' is invalid, so the claim returns INVALID_CLAIM, consistent with sign-in.
- Fix risk: A GR-origin claim with a leading-0 10-digit input is now rejected with the generic claim error. Already stored +300… accounts are unaffected. Add '0123456789' to the rejects table in tests/unit/date-phone-validation.test.ts and check that sensitiveRateLimit.ts:25 (which calls normalizePhone with 'GR' for 10-digit inputs) still builds an identifier key for that input, or falls back as intended.
- Resolution: FIXED in follow-up task T02 (Phone numbers are normalized the same way for the limiter, the claim and sign-in); changes are uncommitted, patch .runtime/review-patches/R4-T02.patch. Regression tests: tests/security/rate-limit-persistence.test.ts, tests/unit/date-phone-validation.test.ts.

- Problem: (1) Every successful Locate-me answer creates a new L.marker and nothing keeps or removes the previous one, so the pins stack; after the guest walks and presses the button again, the old position stays on the map. (2) The pin is a regular 'service' phone-handset place pin with tabindex=0, role=button and no accessible name (no title, aria-label or alt). Keyboard and screen-reader users get an unnamed button, and sighted users cannot tell it from the Fire Department and Hospital pins on the check-in map. (3) After the map is unmounted, mapRef.current is null, setView is skipped by the ?. but addTo(mapRef.current!) still runs and throws.
- Impact: A guest on the check-in map presses Locate me twice while walking: the map ends with two identical unnamed phone pins (plus the data pins), the first at the old position. In the run below the count of service pins went 2, 3, 4. Separately, a guest on the guide map presses Locate me, the permission prompt is open, the guest switches to List (which unmounts the map), then taps Allow: the callback throws an uncaught TypeError. Run output: after 1st locate: service pins = 3; after 2nd locate: service pins = 4; the two added markers had tabindex=0 role=button title=null aria-label=null; the callback after unmount threw: TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'addLayer').

  ```diff
  -            L.marker([latitude, longitude], { icon: buildIcon({ markerType: 'service' }, mapLabels.home) }).addTo(mapRef.current!);
  +            const current = mapRef.current;
  +            if (!current) return;
  +            current.setView([latitude, longitude], 15);
  +            if (locationMarkerRef.current) locationMarkerRef.current.setLatLng([latitude, longitude]);
  +            else locationMarkerRef.current = L.marker([latitude, longitude], { icon: buildIcon({ markerType: 'service' }, mapLabels.home), interactive: false, keyboard: false }).addTo(current);
  ```

  and in the effect cleanup add `locationMarkerRef.current = null;`. Reusing mapLabels.locateMe as the pin title (the original proposal) would name the pin after the button, so I use interactive:false and keyboard:false instead. A distinct 'you are here' icon is a design decision for the lead. I applied this to a scratch copy and re-ran: service pins after the 1st and 2nd locate were 3 and 3; the user pin has tabindex=null role=null; the callback after unmount threw nothing.
- Fix risk: The cleanup line is needed: after a re-init (the effect re-runs when center, zoom, labels or the tile key change) a stale marker would belong to the removed map and setLatLng would not show it on the new one. interactive:false means the pin cannot open a popup (it has none today). Test: Locate twice and expect one user pin; unmount with a pending locate callback and expect no throw.

### R-399: M18 press feedback scale(.98) is overridden by the hover lift whenever a mouse presses a button
- Severity: Low
- Category: Bug
- Status: CONFIRMED
- Location: src/styles/components/ui.css:L383; src/styles/components/ui.css:L394-L395
- Evidence:

  `src/styles/components/ui.css:L383`

  ```css
  :root[data-motion="full"] .ui-btn:active:not(:disabled) { transform: scale(.98); }
  ```

  `src/styles/components/ui.css:L394-L395`

  ```css
  @media (hover: hover) and (pointer: fine) {
      :root[data-motion="full"] .ui-btn:not(.ui-btn--link-arrow):hover:not(:disabled) { transform: translateY(-2px); }
  ```

  `docs/design/identity.md:L770`

  ```md
  | M18 | Buttons | Hover (fine pointers): lift −2 px plus a warm glint sweep on primary (700 ms). Active: `scale(.98)` for 160 ms | Pointer | CSS | Colour change only |
  ```

  `docs/design/identity.md:L46`

  ```md
  14. **From playful (judge 1):** tactile button press: `scale(.98)` on active and a 2 px lift on hover (fine pointers only).
  ```

  Output of (scratch) agents/verify-F10/spec.mjs output:

  ```text
  [0,5,0] :root[data-motion="full"] .ui-btn:active:not(:disabled)
  [0,6,0] :root[data-motion="full"] .ui-btn:not(.ui-btn--link-arrow):hover:not(:disabled)
  ```

  Verification: Found by F10. Verifier: upheld (executed).

- Problem: With a mouse the lift rule (0,6,0) always out-specifies the press rule (0,5,0) and both set `transform`, so `scale(.98)` never applies on a fine-pointer device (except link-arrow buttons). M18 and graft 14 specify both a hover lift and a press scale on fine pointers.
- Impact: A desktop visitor who clicks Check dates or any primary/secondary Button with full motion sees the 2 px lift but no press scale. On phones the press works. Cosmetic: a documented micro-interaction is missing on the main desktop path.
- Fix:

  Inside the fine-pointer block, after L395, add a combined rule (specificity (0,7,0), verified with the same script):

  ```diff
  +    :root[data-motion="full"] .ui-btn:not(.ui-btn--link-arrow):hover:active:not(:disabled) { transform: translateY(-2px) scale(.98); }
  ```

  (Alternative: change L383 to the individual `scale: .98` property and add `scale var(--dur-micro) var(--ease-glide)` to the L380 transition list; it composes with the lift and the magnetic `translate`, but touches two lines.)
- Fix risk: Cosmetic only. Test: with a mouse and data-motion=full press a primary, secondary and ghost button (lift plus slight shrink, no jump on release); on a touch device the press still works; link-arrow unchanged; reduced motion unchanged. tests/unit/motion-css-gate.test.ts is unaffected (the new rule has no animation or transition declaration).
- Resolution: DECLINED by the decision agent (2026-10-09): A missing micro-interaction on fine pointers only, with no functional effect.

### R-402: Planner keeps the server render's today and nights: after midnight (Athens), or on a browser Back that reuses the cached page, it still offers and quotes yesterday as a check-in, and an open page never turns stale
- Severity: Low
- Category: Bug
- Status: CONFIRMED
- Location: src/components/availability/AvailabilityPlanner.tsx:L131-L142; src/app/[locale]/availability/page.tsx:L93-L97; src/lib/prisma-repositories/availabilityRepository.ts:L97-L104; src/lib/availability/stayQuote.ts:L121-L126

  `src/components/availability/AvailabilityPlanner.tsx:L131-L142`

  ```tsx
  export default function AvailabilityPlanner({ locale, availability }: AvailabilityPlannerProps) {

      () => ({ today, horizonEnd, blockedNights: bookedNights(today, nights), ratePeriods: rates }),
  ```

  `src/app/[locale]/availability/page.tsx:L93-L97`

  ```tsx
    const now = new Date();

    let availability: PublicAvailability | null = null;
    try {
      availability = await readPublicAvailability(now);
  ```

  `src/lib/prisma-repositories/availabilityRepository.ts:L97-L104`

  ```ts
    const lastSyncedAt = state.lastSuccessAt?.toISOString() ?? null;
    const fresh = state.lastSuccessAt !== null && now.getTime() - state.lastSuccessAt.getTime() <= STALE_AFTER_MS;
    return {
      today,
      horizonEnd,
      status: fresh ? 'fresh' : 'stale',
      lastSyncedAt,
      nights: encodeNights(today, horizonEnd, fresh ? state : null),
  ```

  `src/lib/availability/stayQuote.ts:L125`

  ```ts
    if (checkIn < context.today) return { ok: false, reason: 'past' };
  ```

  `node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/04-glossary.md:L47`

  ```md
  Pages are not cached by default but are reused during browser back/forward navigation.
  ```

  (1 further evidence excerpts omitted: (command))

  Verification: Found by D7. Verifier: upheld (executed). Refuter: upheld, severity Low.

- Problem: The planner's notion of today, of the booked nights and of calendar freshness is fixed at the server render. When the property date moves on while the page stays in memory (a tab left open past 00:00 Europe/Athens, or a browser Back that reuses the cached page payload), yesterday stays labelled 'Today', stays enabled as a check-in, and validateStay accepts it because it compares with the frozen today. The booked nights and the 12-hour fresh/stale decision are also those of the render, so a page kept open for days shows nights that were booked on Airbnb in the meantime as free, with no stale notice.
- Impact: A guest opens /en/availability late on 6 Oct, comes back after midnight and picks 6-8 Oct: the planner labels 6 Oct 'Today', quotes €176 for 2 nights and puts #checkin=2026-10-06&checkout=2026-10-08 into the WhatsApp text, a stay that already started. A tab left open for days offers nights that are now booked. Nothing is booked or paid on the site, so the result is a wrong request the host has to decline and a disappointed guest, not a wrong charge.
- Fix:

  Keep the server as the source of today and use the browser clock only to decide when the render is out of date. Reloading keeps the URL fragment, so applyFragment restores the selection. In AvailabilityPlanner.tsx:

  ```diff
  -import { CLIMATE_FEE_SCHEDULE } from '@/data/stayPolicy';
  +import { CLIMATE_FEE_SCHEDULE, PROPERTY_TIME_ZONE } from '@/data/stayPolicy';
  -import { eachNight, fromLocalDate, nightsBetween, toLocalDate, type IsoDate } from '@/lib/availability/calendarDate';
  +import { eachNight, fromLocalDate, nightsBetween, propertyToday, toLocalDate, type IsoDate } from '@/lib/availability/calendarDate';
  +  // The server decides today; the clock only says when that answer is out of date.
  +  useEffect(() => {
  +    const reloadIfOutOfDate = () => {
  +      if (document.visibilityState === 'visible' && propertyToday(PROPERTY_TIME_ZONE, new Date()) > today) window.location.reload();
  +    };
  +    reloadIfOutOfDate(); // a Back/Forward reuse of an old payload remounts the planner
  +    document.addEventListener('visibilitychange', reloadIfOutOfDate);
  +    window.addEventListener('pageshow', reloadIfOutOfDate); // bfcache restore
  +    return () => { document.removeEventListener('visibilitychange', reloadIfOutOfDate); window.removeEventListener('pageshow', reloadIfOutOfDate); };
  +  }, [today]);
  ```

  router.refresh() from next/navigation (the candidate's proposal) also works and keeps client state, but useRouter needs the App Router context, so every test in tests/components/availability-planner.test.tsx would then have to mock next/navigation.
- Fix risk: A reload loop is impossible only while the server's propertyToday and the browser's agree; a device clock set a day ahead would reload on every visibility change (the reload would bring the same today back). Guard against it with a once-per-today flag (for example, compare with the today of the last reload in sessionStorage), or accept it. Tests: vi.setSystemTime past midnight Athens with today=yesterday props expects one reload (stub location.reload); same-day props expect none; the existing planner tests must still pass with fake timers off.
- Resolution: DECLINED by the decision agent (2026-10-09): The planner books and sends nothing and a reload fixes the date, while the proposed reload logic depends on the device clock and can loop.

### R-403: Prisma's SIGTERM/SIGINT hooks call process.exit as soon as the pool drains, pre-empting Next's graceful shutdown and cutting in-flight requests
- Severity: Low
- Category: Bug
- Status: CONFIRMED
- Location: src/lib/prisma.ts:L142-L202
- Evidence:

  `src/lib/prisma.ts:L178-L189`

  ```ts
    process.once('beforeExit', () => {
      void cleanup('beforeExit');
    });

    for (const signal of signals) {
      process.once(signal, () => {
        void cleanup(signal).finally(() => {
          const exitCode = exitCodes[signal] ?? 0;
          process.exit(exitCode);
        });
      });
    }
  ```

  `src/lib/prisma.ts:L192-L201`

  ```ts
  if (!globalThisWithPrisma.__prismaShutdownHooksRegistered__) {
    ...
    if (hasClient) {
      registerPrismaShutdownHooks(prisma);
      globalThisWithPrisma.__prismaShutdownHooksRegistered__ = true;
    }
  ```

  `node_modules/next/dist/server/lib/start-server.js:L331-L389`

  ```js
  // first, stop accepting new connections and finish pending requests,
  ...
  server.close((err)=>{ ... res(); });
  ...
  case 'SIGTERM':
      process.exit(143);
  ...
  if (!process.env.NEXT_MANUAL_SIG_HANDLE) {
      process.on('SIGINT', cleanup);
      process.on('SIGTERM', cleanup);
  }
  ```

  `node_modules/next/dist/build/utils.js:L1133-L1143`

  ```js
  const { startServer } = require('next/dist/server/lib/start-server')
  ...
  startServer({
  ```

  `docker/Dockerfile.security:L143-L147`

  ```text
  STOPSIGNAL SIGTERM
  ...
  ENTRYPOINT ["/usr/bin/dumb-init", "--"]
  CMD ["node", "scripts/start-standalone.mjs", "server.js"]
  ```

  (2 further evidence excerpts omitted: node_modules/pg-pool/index.js:L133-L141; scratch: agents/verify-S9/sigterm.ts (http server, 1.5 s handler, Next-like SIGTERM handler doing server.close then exit 143))

  Verification: Found by S9. Verifier: upheld (executed). Refuter: upheld, severity Low. Lead: Re-read prisma.ts L142-L202 and the installed next/dist/server/lib/start-server.js L321-L389 (Next 16.3.6): on SIGTERM Next closes the server, waits for in-flight requests, then exits 143; the Prisma hook exits 143 as soon as $disconnect() resolves, which does not wait for requests that hold no database connection (e.g. one awaiting the inline webhook).

- Problem: src/lib/prisma.ts installs its own SIGINT/SIGTERM/SIGQUIT listeners that end in process.exit() right after $disconnect resolves. In the web process, Next's standalone server already handles the same signals by closing the listener and waiting for pending requests. Because pg-pool's end() resolves as soon as no client is checked out, the Prisma listener exits the process within milliseconds. Requests that are not inside a query at that moment (webhook fetch, rendering, streaming) are cut off. If a request is inside a query, the process exits as soon as that query releases its client, before the response is written.
- Impact: Every `docker compose up -d web` (release), `docker stop` or host reboot sends SIGTERM through dumb-init. A guest or admin request in flight at that moment gets a connection reset instead of finishing within the 10 s stop grace period. For example, a check-in arrival request waiting on the inline webhook delivery fails for the guest, although its outbox row is already committed and the worker retries the delivery later. No stored data is lost, but Next's graceful termination never takes effect. On a one-apartment site this is rare (only requests that overlap a restart).
- Fix:

  Remove the hooks: Next handles the web process's signals, and the workers disconnect explicitly.
  ```diff
  -type ExtendedGlobal = typeof globalThis & {
  -  __prisma__?: PrismaClient;
  -  __prismaShutdownHooksRegistered__?: boolean;
  -};
  +type ExtendedGlobal = typeof globalThis & { __prisma__?: PrismaClient };
  @@
  -function registerPrismaShutdownHooks(client: PrismaClient): void { ... }   // L142-L190
  -if (!globalThisWithPrisma.__prismaShutdownHooksRegistered__) { ... }      // L192-L202
  ```
  In tests/unit/prisma-lifecycle.test.ts, replace the first case (L56-L60) with an assertion that importing the module registers no SIGTERM/SIGINT listener, and drop the __prismaShutdownHooksRegistered__ cleanup lines (L22, L41, L52).
- Fix risk: A SIGTERM to a worker container (cron `timeout 55`/`280` or docker stop) then gets Node's default termination instead of waiting for checked-out connections. PostgreSQL rolls back any open transaction, and outbox leases expire and are reclaimed (src/lib/bookingOutbox.ts), so this needs no extra handling. Still, run the worker disconnect tests and tests/unit/prisma-lifecycle.test.ts. In dev, `next dev` and tsx scripts keep their own or default signal handling. An end-to-end check is `docker stop` on the web container during a slow request (needs Docker: the lead's or owner's call).
- Resolution: FIXED in follow-up task T16 (Prisma no longer exits the process on SIGTERM); changes are uncommitted, patch .runtime/review-patches/R4-T16.patch. Regression tests: tests/unit/prisma-lifecycle.test.ts.

### R-405: redactSensitiveText turns every named WebKit/Gecko stack frame ('fn@https://…') into [REDACTED_EMAIL], so Safari/iOS and Firefox error reports lose their stack
- Severity: Low
- Category: Bug
- Status: CONFIRMED
- Location: src/lib/redaction.ts:L38-L43; src/app/api/errors/route.ts:L58-L60; src/lib/errorReporting.ts:L123-L127
- Evidence:

  `src/lib/redaction.ts:L38-L43`

  ```ts
  function looksLikeEmail(token: string): boolean {
    const at = token.indexOf('@');
    if (at < 1 || at !== token.lastIndexOf('@')) return false;
    const dot = token.indexOf('.', at + 2);
    return dot > at + 1 && dot < token.length - 1;
  }
  ```

  `src/app/api/errors/route.ts:L58-L60`

  ```ts
    const stack = report.error.stack
      ? redact(report.error.stack.split('\n').slice(0, 5).join('\n')).slice(0, 2_000)
      : undefined;
  ```

  `src/lib/errorReporting.ts:L123-L127`

  ```ts
    private extractFileFromStack(stack?: string): string | undefined {
      if (!stack) return undefined;
      const match = stack.match(/at.*\((.+):\d+:\d+\)/);
      return match?.[1];
    }
  ```

  `src/lib/errorReporting.ts:L58-L61`

  ```ts
      window.addEventListener('unhandledrejection', (event) => {
        const error = event.reason instanceof Error ? event.reason : new Error(String(event.reason));
        void this.reportError(error, { category: 'unhandledRejection' });
      });
  ```

  Output of agents/verify-X10/redact.ts (scratch, calls the real src/lib/redaction.ts):

  ```text
  safari => "[REDACTED_EMAIL]\n[REDACTED_EMAIL]\n@https://example.gr/_next/static/chunks/main.js:1:10\nglobal [REDACTED_EMAIL]"
  chrome => "TypeError: x is undefined\n    at handleClick (https://example.gr/_next/static/chunks/app/page-abc123.js:1:2345)"
  ```

  Verification: Found by X10. Verifier: upheld (executed).

- Problem: WebKit and Gecko stack frames are single whitespace-free tokens of the form `functionName@https://host/path.js:line:col`. looksLikeEmail classifies them as e-mail addresses, so the stored client.error stack becomes a column of [REDACTED_EMAIL]. For unhandled rejections and route-boundary errors, extractFileFromStack also understands only V8 frames, so these reports keep no file, line or column at all.
- Impact: Guests mostly arrive by QR scan on phones, and every browser on iOS is WebKit. A JavaScript failure on /stay or the check-in page from an iPhone is stored with a stack that names no function and no file, and for promise rejections no location either. The host or developer cannot locate the failure from the report. No data is exposed. Chrome and Android Chrome reports are fine.
- Fix:

  ```
   function looksLikeEmail(token: string): boolean {
     const at = token.indexOf('@');
     if (at < 1 || at !== token.lastIndexOf('@')) return false;
  +  if (token.includes('://', at)) return false; // WebKit/Gecko stack frame `fn@https://…`
     const dot = token.indexOf('.', at + 2);
  ```
  Add a Safari-frame case to tests/security/security-boundaries.test.ts. I ran this change on a scratch copy: Safari frames are kept, 'guest@example.com', 'mailto:guest@example.com' and 'https://guest@example.com/x' are still redacted, and the existing test inputs give the same outputs.
- Fix risk: A token that is an e-mail directly followed by '://' (for example 'a@b.com://x') would no longer be redacted. That is unrealistic. Re-run tests/security/security-boundaries.test.ts and tests/security/redaction-claim-token.test.ts. security-monitoring.ts (CSP report details) uses the same function and benefits the same way.
- Resolution: FIXED in follow-up task T34 (Redaction keeps stack frames, catches embedded tokens, and logs no contact data); changes are uncommitted, patch .runtime/review-patches/R4-T34.patch. Regression tests: tests/security/security-boundaries.test.ts, tests/unit/logger-enterprise.test.ts.

### R-406: The body is decoded as strict UTF-8 before unfolding: a line fold inside a multi-byte character fails the whole sync with invalid_encoding
- Severity: Low
- Category: Bug
- Status: CONFIRMED
- Location: src/lib/availability/icalFetch.ts:L81-L85; src/lib/availability/icalParser.ts:L71-L86
- Evidence:

  `src/lib/availability/icalFetch.ts:L81-L85`

  ```ts
    try {
      return new TextDecoder('utf-8', { fatal: true }).decode(body);
    } catch {
      throw new CalendarFetchError('invalid_encoding');
    }
  ```

  `src/lib/availability/icalParser.ts:L79-L81`

  ```ts
      // Unfolding: a line end followed by one space or tab continues the previous line.
      if (previous !== undefined && (raw.startsWith(' ') || raw.startsWith('\t'))) {
        previous.text += raw.slice(1);
  ```

  Output of agents/verify-D1/parse.ts (scratch; SUMMARY:Κράτηση with CRLF+SP inserted between the two bytes of the last character):

  ```text
  fold-in-char strict decode throws TypeError
  fold-in-char lenient -> [{"start":"2026-11-01","end":"2026-11-05"}]
  FFFD in date -> throws invalid_date line 5
  FFFD in name -> throws malformed_line line 5
  ```

  `tests/unit/ical-fetch.test.ts:L345-L352`

  ```ts
    it('rejects a body that is not valid UTF-8', async () => {
      mocks.fetch.mockResolvedValue(new Response(new Uint8Array([0x42, 0x45, 0xff, 0xfe]), { status: 200 }));
      ...
      expect(error.code).toBe('invalid_encoding');
  ```

  Verification: Found by D1, S6.2 (independent reports: D1-02, S6.2-01). Verifier: upheld (executed).

- Problem: Folding is defined on octets (RFC 5545 section 3.1, which also notes that simple producers may fold inside a UTF-8 multi-octet sequence and that readers must unfold so as to restore it; quoted from memory, the RFC could not be re-read without network). The code decodes strictly before unfolding, so such a feed, valid iCalendar, is rejected as a whole even though the affected text property is discarded unread.
- Impact: Only if the Airbnb export carries a non-ASCII character on a folded line and folds inside it: every sync fails with invalid_encoding while that event remains in the feed, the snapshot goes stale, the alert opens after 3 h and after 12 h the public calendar shows every night as unknown. The fixtures are ASCII-only and were written from memory, so whether the real feed contains non-ASCII text on long lines is not established; the trigger is unlikely.
- Fix:

  Decode leniently; the parser's own validation already rejects U+FFFD in names and dates.

  ```diff
  -  try {
  -    return new TextDecoder('utf-8', { fatal: true }).decode(body);
  -  } catch {
  -    throw new CalendarFetchError('invalid_encoding');
  -  }
  +  // Not fatal: a fold inside a multi-byte character (RFC 5545 section 3.1) decodes to U+FFFD
  +  // in a text property the parser drops; U+FFFD in a name or a date still fails the parse.
  +  return new TextDecoder('utf-8').decode(body);
  ```

  then drop 'invalid_encoding' from CalendarFetchErrorCode.
- Fix risk: tests/unit/ical-fetch.test.ts L345-352 pins invalid_encoding and must be replaced by a test that a body with a fold inside a multi-byte SUMMARY character parses, plus one that U+FFFD in DTSTART still fails with invalid_date. A non-UTF-8 (e.g. Latin-1) feed would then be accepted as long as names and dates are ASCII, which is harmless for this dates-only parser.
- Resolution: DECLINED by the decision agent (2026-10-09): It needs a folded non-ASCII character in the Airbnb export, which in practice carries ASCII text; reopen if the first real sync reports invalid_encoding.

### R-407: The check-in map's loading placeholder is a fixed 260px while the map is clamp(240px, 35vw, 420px), so the section jumps when Leaflet's chunk loads; mapConstants.ts now exists only for that value
- Severity: Low
- Category: Bug
- Status: CONFIRMED
- Location: src/components/CheckInInfo.tsx:L67-L71; src/components/CheckInInfo.tsx:L1049-L1056; src/lib/mapConstants.ts:L1-L8
- Evidence:

  `src/components/CheckInInfo.tsx:L67-L71`

  ```tsx
  const MAP_HEIGHT = 'clamp(240px, 35vw, 420px)';
  const DynamicApartmentLocationMap = dynamic(() => import('@/components/ApartmentLocationMap'), {
    ssr: false,
    loading: () => <MapLoadingSkeleton height={MAP_DEFAULTS.HEIGHT.COMPACT} />,
  });
  ```

  `src/lib/mapConstants.ts:L3-L8`

  ```ts
  export const MAP_DEFAULTS = {
    // Standard map heights for different contexts
    HEIGHT: {
      COMPACT: '260px',
    },
  } as const;
  ```

  `src/components/CheckInInfo.tsx:L1049-L1051`

  ```tsx
                <DynamicApartmentLocationMap
                  locale={locale}
                  height={MAP_HEIGHT}
  ```

  `src/components/InteractiveMap.tsx:L86`

  ```tsx
      <div ref={containerRef} className={`relative ${className}`} style={{ height }}>
  ```

  `src/components/MapLoadingSkeleton.tsx:L20`

  ```tsx
      <div className="map-placeholder" style={{ height }}>
  ```

  (1 further evidence excerpts omitted: src/styles/components/stay.css:L535-L538)

  Verification: Found by F8, F6 (independent reports: F8-03, F6-06). Verifier: upheld (read-all-paths).

- Problem: The dynamic-import placeholder of the check-in neighbourhood map is a fixed 260px (MAP_DEFAULTS.HEIGHT.COMPACT), while the map that replaces it is clamp(240px, 35vw, 420px). The section therefore changes height when the Leaflet chunk arrives: +160px at viewports of 1200px and wider, -20px at about 686px and narrower. Below 1280px the highlights stack under the map, so they jump. MAP_DEFAULTS has this single reader and holds only this mismatched value.
- Impact: A guest on a laptop scrolls to the neighbourhood section while the chunk loads. The highlight cards under the map jump down by up to 160px, a visible layout shift. The effect is small: it is the last section of the page, often below the fold when the chunk arrives, and nothing is lost.
- Fix:

  ```diff
  -import { MAP_DEFAULTS } from '@/lib/mapConstants';
  ...
  -  loading: () => <MapLoadingSkeleton height={MAP_DEFAULTS.HEIGHT.COMPACT} />,
  +  loading: () => <MapLoadingSkeleton height={MAP_HEIGHT} />,
  ```
  MAP_HEIGHT is a module-level const declared on L67, before the dynamic() call, so it can be referenced there. Then delete src/lib/mapConstants.ts, which has no other reference.
- Fix risk: Purely visual. Check the check-in page at 390, 768, 1280 and 1440px that the placeholder and the map have the same height. tests/components/checkin-location-highlights.test.tsx and checkin-wifi.test.tsx mock next/dynamic, so they are unaffected. knip (check:dead-code) must stay clean after the deletion.
- Resolution: DECLINED by the decision agent (2026-10-09): A cosmetic layout shift at the bottom of the check-in page while the map loads.

### R-408: The fixed QuoteBar has no footer clearance and no scroll-padding-bottom (unlike the BookBar), so below lg it covers the bottom of the footer and can hide keyboard-focused controls
- Severity: Low
- Category: Bug
- Status: CONFIRMED
- Location: src/styles/components/calendar.css:L333-L357; src/styles/components/shell.css:L311-L315; src/styles/components/shell.css:L498-L505; src/components/availability/AvailabilityPlanner.tsx:L441-L443
- Evidence:

  ```css
  .site-footer {
    position: relative;
    margin-top: var(--space-section);
    padding: 0 0 calc(48px + env(safe-area-inset-bottom));
  }
  ```

  `src/styles/components/shell.css:L498-L505`

  ```css
  /* The footer clears the bar (§8 SiteFooter). */
  @media (max-width: 1023.98px) {
    :root:has(.bookbar) .site-footer.site-footer { padding-bottom: calc(96px + env(safe-area-inset-bottom)); }
    /* Keyboard focus scrolls a control above the shown bar, not under it (WCAG 2.4.11; R3-V13 keyboard pass
       found the footer controls fully covered on home and apartment). */
    :root:has(.bookbar.is-shown) { scroll-padding-bottom: calc(96px + env(safe-area-inset-bottom)); }
  }
  ```

  `src/styles/components/shell.css:L363-L367`

  ```css
  .site-footer .site-footer__link {
    display: inline-flex;
    align-items: center;
    gap: 8px;
    min-height: 36px;
  ```

  (1 further evidence excerpts omitted: git grep output)

  Lead runtime probe (390x844, /en/availability, stay selected, scrolled to the end):

  ```text
  {"barClass":"quote-bar","bar":{"top":776,"bottom":832},"viewport":844,"covered":[{"text":"Privacy","top":760,"bottom":796,"overlapPx":20,"height":36}],"scrollPaddingBottom":"56px"}
  ```

  Verification: Found by F7. Verifier: upheld (read-all-paths). Refuter: upheld, severity Medium. Lead: Reproduced at 390x844 with the stay 15-18 Oct selected and the page scrolled to the end: the QuoteBar spans y 776-832 and covers 20 px of the 36 px "Privacy" footer link (16 px left), which cannot be scrolled clear. Correction to the finding: the root does have scroll-padding-bottom: 56px on phones (stay.css L670, the network-status rule), so keyboard focus scrolls a control to within 12 px of the bar rather than fully under it; partial obscuring does not fail WCAG 2.4.11 (Minimum). Severity set to Low by the lead.

- Problem: The QuoteBar is a fixed bottom bar like the BookBar, but neither of the BookBar's two mitigations covers it: footer clearance (footer padding-bottom 96 px) and scroll-padding-bottom for keyboard focus. The footer's 48 px bottom padding is less than the bar's 68 px footprint.
- Impact: On a phone, a guest with a complete stay selected scrolls to the end of /en/availability. The footer legal links (privacy and the other legal pages) are half under the glass bar, with about 16 px of their 36 px tap height left. A keyboard user (tablet with keyboard, or a switch device) tabbing down through the page's contact links and the footer can land on a link drawn entirely behind the bar, which fails WCAG 2.4.11 Focus Not Obscured (Minimum). The project already treats this as a defect for the BookBar.
- Fix:

  Mirror the BookBar rules for the QuoteBar in calendar.css, next to the .quote-bar block. The bar is only in the DOM while shown, so :has(.quote-bar) is enough:

  ```diff
  +/* The footer and keyboard focus clear the shown QuoteBar (as the BookBar, shell.css; WCAG 2.4.11). */
  +@media (max-width: 1023.98px) {
  +  :root:has(.quote-bar) .site-footer.site-footer { padding-bottom: calc(96px + env(safe-area-inset-bottom)); }
  +  :root:has(.quote-bar) { scroll-padding-bottom: calc(96px + env(safe-area-inset-bottom)); }
  +}
  ```
- Fix risk: Low and CSS-only. The footer gets taller at the bottom only while the bar is shown. When the bar appears or disappears near the page end the document height changes by 48 px, which can shift the scroll position slightly. Check at 390 px and 768 px with a complete stay: the footer legal row should clear the bar at the bottom, Tab through the footer and the page links should keep focus above the bar, and the bar and the extra padding should disappear at >= 1024 px.
- Resolution: FIXED in follow-up tasks T27 (The availability page's fixed bars clear the header, the footer and the network pill), T61 (The QuoteBar's scroll padding also wins below 640 px); changes are uncommitted, patches .runtime/review-patches/R4-T27.patch, R4-T61.patch.

  Verification: Found by F4. Verifier: upheld (executed).

- Problem: The 200 ms fade-in is meant only as the fallback when no morph runs, so `:not([data-vt="photo"])` switches it off during the morph. When the morph finishes, clear() removes data-vt while the dialog is still open. The fade selector then starts to match the open dialog, and its computed animation-name changes from none to lightbox-fade-in. Under CSS Animations semantics, adding a name to animation-name starts that animation. The open dialog therefore drops to opacity 0 and fades back in right after the morph.
- Impact: Conditions: data-motion="full" and a browser with document.startViewTransition. A visitor taps a tile on /{l}/apartment, and the photo morphs into the viewer. Then the dialog (photo, caption bar, controls) blinks to transparent and fades back in over 200 ms. This happens on every open. The PROGRESS watch item says the morph was checked in Chrome only, and this rule has no history before HEAD that could show whether that check saw it.
- Fix:

  Apply the fade only where morphPhoto falls back for lack of the API, so data-vt no longer has to switch it off. In src/styles/components/lightbox.css:

  ```diff
  -  :root[data-motion="full"]:not([data-vt="photo"]) .lightbox[open] {
  -    animation: lightbox-fade-in 200ms var(--ease-glide);
  -  }
  +  @supports not (view-transition-name: none) {
  +    :root[data-motion="full"] .lightbox[open] {
  +      animation: lightbox-fade-in 200ms var(--ease-glide);
  +    }
  +  }
  ```

  Also update the comment at L99-L100. tests/unit/motion-css-gate.test.ts collects nested at-rules (walk(body, [...atRules, prelude])), so the rule stays inside the reduced-motion media query and under :root[data-motion="full"], and the gate should still pass.
- Fix risk: This assumes that browsers with the view-transition-name CSS property also have document.startViewTransition. Same-document View Transitions ship both together, but this was not checked per browser. If a View Transition is skipped (hidden document, or another transition already running), the dialog appears instantly instead of fading. Run tests/unit/motion-css-gate.test.ts. In Chrome, open and close a tile with motion set to full and with reduced motion, and check that getAnimations() on the dialog is empty after the morph.
- Resolution: FIXED in follow-up task T33 (The lightbox fades in only once); changes are uncommitted, patch .runtime/review-patches/R4-T33.patch. Regression tests: tests/unit/motion-css-gate.test.ts.


  ```text
  exit=1

  exit=0   (no output)

  exit=0   (no output)

  SECRET SCAN FAILED. GITLEAKS_BIN must identify the checksum-locked Gitleaks binary ...

  ```

  Verification: Found by T2. Verifier: upheld (executed).

- Problem: A security gate that fails open silently (no output, exit 0) for an unusual but legitimate way of starting it: an absolute path that contains a symlink, for example /tmp/<checkout> on macOS where /tmp is a symlink to private/tmp (confirmed with ls -ld /tmp on this machine).
- Impact: An operator checking a clean checkout in /tmp (or any symlinked directory) with `node /tmp/release-checkout/scripts/check-secrets.mjs artifacts` sees no output and exit code 0 and takes it as a pass. The documented entry points (npm scripts with relative paths, verify:release) are not affected, so the normal release flow works; the trigger is an undocumented manual invocation.
- Fix:

  ```diff

  +import { readFileSync, realpathSync } from 'node:fs';
  ...
  -  ? pathToFileURL(path.resolve(process.argv[1])).href
  +  ? pathToFileURL(realpathSync(process.argv[1])).href
  ```

  Safer variant that also keeps odd argv[1] values importable: wrap in try/catch and return '' when realpathSync throws. The same one-line change applies to scripts/verify-release.mjs:245 if the owner wants the guard fixed there too (separate decision).
- Fix risk: Low. Re-run the secret-scanning node tests (they import the module, argv[1] is the test file and exists) and `npm run check:secrets:sources`. `node --preserve-symlinks-main` would make import.meta.url keep the link path and the fixed guard would then skip main; that flag is not used anywhere in this repository. The try/catch variant avoids the ENOENT-on-import edge.
- Resolution: DECLINED by the decision agent (2026-10-09): The documented entry points (npm scripts and verify:release) are not affected; only an absolute path through a symlinked directory is.

For a mandatory release gate the failure mode is silent success.

The supported `npm run verify:release` is not affected. An operator or an agent that uses such a path sees an empty run and exit 0, but the output lacks the 'RELEASE VERIFICATION PASSED: 30/30' line that docs/release-verification.md describes, so only careless reading would take it as a pass. Low.
- Fix:

  Compare real paths.

  verify-release.mjs:

  ```diff
  +import { realpathSync } from 'node:fs';  (merge into the existing node:fs import)
  -const invokedPath = process.argv[1]
  -  ? pathToFileURL(path.resolve(process.argv[1])).href

  +  ? pathToFileURL(realpathSync(process.argv[1])).href
  +  : '';
  ```

  validate-security.ts:

  ```diff
  +const isMain = process.argv[1] ? fileURLToPath(import.meta.url) === realpathSync(process.argv[1]) : false;
  ```

  (import realpathSync from 'fs').
- Fix risk: realpathSync throws if argv[1] does not exist; it always exists when a file is run as the main script, and the `process.argv[1] ?` guard keeps `node -e` and REPL safe. When the module is imported by tests (scripts/tests/release-policy.test.mjs imports runReleaseVerification) argv[1] is the test runner, so the guard stays false. Test: run gate 3/4 (release-policy tests and validate:release-policy) and `npm run verify:release` once; both files are inside release-policy's source checks, so confirm validateVerifyImplementation still passes (the markers are untouched).
- Resolution: DECLINED by the decision agent (2026-10-09): Same cause as R-410: `npm run verify:release` and `npm run validate:security` resolve their paths correctly.


  `node_modules/@prisma/client/runtime/client.d.ts:L638-L642`

  ```ts
      $transaction<P extends PrismaPromise<any>[]>(arg: [...P], options?: {
          maxWait?: number;
  ```

  Output of (command):

  ```text
  git grep -n -i "trigger\|default_transaction_isolation\|isolation" -- prisma src scripts docker  -> no default_transaction_isolation setting; isolationLevel is set only in portalAuthService.ts:299, checkInRequestRepository.ts:228, ratePeriodRepository.ts:108, refreshTokenRepository.ts:498/562, privacyService.ts:204
  ```

  (1 further evidence excerpts omitted: tests/integration/operations/outbox-dead-lifecycle.test.ts:L108-L119)

  Verification: Found by X2, D2, D3 (independent reports: X2-02, D2-04, D3-03). Verifier: upheld (read-all-paths).

- Problem: The metric is a difference of two counts that must come from one snapshot, but the batch transaction runs at READ COMMITTED, so a retention commit between the statements makes the difference positive without any real delivery failure.
- Impact: On the operations run right after a guest erasure that cancelled undelivered events, a critical 'Dead outbox events' alert can open and notify the alert webhook with value = number of cancelled events; the next run (5 minutes later) resolves it. The window is one database round-trip, so it is rare, and the effect is one false page to the host.
- Fix:

  Read both counts from one snapshot:

  ```diff
         const [dead, cancelled] = await prisma.$transaction([
           prisma.outboxEvent.count({ where: { status: 'DEAD' } }),
           prisma.outboxEvent.count({ where: ERASURE_CANCELLED_OUTBOX }),
  -      ]);
  +      ], { isolationLevel: 'RepeatableRead' });
  ```
  A read-only REPEATABLE READ transaction cannot fail with a serialization error, so no retry is needed.
- Fix risk: Minimal. Unit tests that mock prisma.$transaction with a strict argument check may need the second argument accepted. The integration test outbox-dead-lifecycle must still pass.
- Resolution: DECLINED by the decision agent (2026-10-09): It needs a retention commit to land between two counts in one round trip, and the false alert resolves on the next run.

- Severity: Low

  `scripts/drain-outbox.ts:L21-L25`

  ```ts
  // Wait for every step to settle before failing, so disconnect() never races a
  // step that is still running and the results of the other steps are still logged.
  async function main() {
    const steps = await Promise.allSettled([
  ```

  `node_modules/@prisma/client/runtime/client.js`

  ```js
  async#n(){switch(this.#t.type){case"disconnected":{let t=this.tracingHelper.runInChildSpan("connect",async()=>{...});return this.#t={type:"connecting",promise:t},await t}case"connecting":return await this.#t.promise;case"connected":return this.#t.engine;case"disconnecting":return await this.#t.promise,await this.#n()}} (v7.10.0; every request calls await this.#n(), so a query after $disconnect reconnects)
  ```

  (2 further evidence excerpts omitted: node_modules/@prisma/adapter-pg/dist/index.js:L811-L812; /private/tmp/claude-503/-Users-pvasilakis-site/82bdc617-08bf-4706-9396-218b0b8840f7/scratchpad/review4/agents/verify-S5/drain-race.mts)

  Verification: Found by S5. Verifier: upheld (executed).

- Problem: deliverWithConcurrency uses Promise.all, so drainOutbox rejects as soon as one delivery rejects, while the other worker loops are still delivering. The outbox worker then calls prisma.$disconnect() under those in-flight deliveries. The operations worker avoids exactly this race with Promise.allSettled (R-206).
- Impact: Several events are due, for example after a receiver outage, and one claim hits a transient database error. The run logs 'failed' and disconnects while the other deliveries are still waiting for the webhook. Their final updates then lazily reconnect a fresh pool (as read in the installed Prisma 7.10.0 runtime). The new idle connections can keep the process alive until 'timeout 55' kills it, and 'flock -n' then skips the next minute's run. If instead the final update fails during the disconnect, a delivered webhook stays LEASED and is sent again after the 5-minute lease (same Idempotency-Key). The trigger is rare on a single host, and the consequences are a delayed run or a deduplicable duplicate.
- Fix:

  Let every delivery settle before failing, as the operations worker does:

  ```diff
     const results = new Array<boolean>(eventIds.length);
  +  const failures: unknown[] = [];
     let index = 0;
     const worker = async () => {
       while (index < eventIds.length) {
         const current = index;
         index += 1;
  -      results[current] = await deliverOutboxEvent(eventIds[current]);
  +      try {
  +        results[current] = await deliverOutboxEvent(eventIds[current]);
  +      } catch (error) {
  +        results[current] = false;
  +        failures.push(error);
  +      }
       }
     };
     await Promise.all(...);
  +  if (failures.length > 0) throw new AggregateError(failures, `${failures.length} outbox deliveries failed`);
     return results;
  ```
- Fix risk: Semantics change slightly: after one failure the worker loop keeps claiming further events instead of stopping. That is the intended outcome, but if the database is really down, every remaining event fails fast as well. The worker's 'failed' log then carries an AggregateError message. Tests: a unit test in tests/unit/booking-outbox.test.ts where one claim rejects and another delivery resolves later; drainOutbox must reject only after the other delivery's final update was called.
- Resolution: FIXED in follow-up task T17 (Outbox deliveries stay best-effort and all settle before the worker fails); changes are uncommitted, patch .runtime/review-patches/R4-T17.patch. Regression tests: tests/unit/booking-outbox.test.ts, tests/routes/arrival-request.test.ts, tests/routes/admin-dead-outbox-actions.test.ts.


  `src/lib/privacyService.ts:L109-L117`

  ```ts
        if (!stillExpired) {
          // Skipped: drop the request this call created so no VERIFIED request is left behind.

  ```

  `src/lib/privacyService.ts:L204`

  ```ts
    }, { isolationLevel: 'Serializable' });
  ```

  `src/lib/portalAuthService.ts:L301-L307`

  ```ts
    for (let attempt = 1; attempt <= SERIALIZABLE_ATTEMPTS; attempt += 1) {
      try {
        return await consume();
      } catch (error) {
        if (!isSerializationConflict(error) || attempt === SERIALIZABLE_ATTEMPTS) throw error;
      }
    }
  ```

  (3 further evidence excerpts omitted: src/lib/operationalMonitor.ts:L283-L291; node_modules/@prisma/adapter-pg/dist/index.js:L539-L543; scratch: agents/verify-D3/d3-01.mts (real privacyService.ts, fake prisma via globalThis.__prisma__, $transaction rejects with a P2034 PrismaClientKnownRequestError on run 1, then the guard sees a new booking on run 2))

  Verification: Found by D3, X2, S7, X9a (independent reports: D3-01, X2-03, S7-04, X9a-03). Verifier: upheld (executed). Refuter: upheld, severity Low.

- Problem: eraseGuestForRetention commits a VERIFIED erasure request (with the retention note) before the Serializable erasure transaction starts, and completeErasureRequest is the only Serializable transaction in src/ that is not retried on P2034. The 'no VERIFIED request left behind' cleanup runs only on the in-transaction skip path and only for a row created by the same call. If the transaction throws (P2034, ERASURE_BLOCKED_BY_ACTIVE_DELIVERY, a killed run) and the guest then stops being expired, the next call finds the row as existing (created: false), skips, and keeps it. ensureVerified (L78-85) has the same pre-transaction side effect: it upgrades a legacy PENDING request and overwrites its note before the guard decides.
- Impact: Realistic only in a narrow race: a returning guest claims a new booking while the operations run (every 5 minutes) is inside the erasure transaction for that guest on the first run after the 12-month mark. Under Serializable the claim's committed booking write is expected to abort the erasure with SQLSTATE 40001, which adapter-pg 7.10.0 maps to TransactionWriteConflict (P2034). Nothing retries: that run exits 1 with '1 retention guest erasure(s) failed: ...', and privacy_requests keeps an open VERIFIED request with the automatic-retention note for a guest who now has a current booking. No guest data is lost (the account and the new booking survive). The stale row is reused, with its old requestedAt, when the guest is erased later. For the admin route the same conflict gives the host a generic 500 and a second click. Low: rare trigger, no data loss, the run log shows the failure.
- Fix:

  Retry only the transaction (not the request creation) on P2034, as the other Serializable writers do. On the retry the guard sees the new booking and deletes the row this call created:

  ```diff
  --- a/src/lib/privacyService.ts
  +++ b/src/lib/privacyService.ts
  @@ export async function eraseGuestForRetention(
     const { request, created } = await createVerifiedErasureRequest(userId, auditNote);
  -  const completed = await completeErasureRequest(request.id, auditNote, { bookingsEndedBefore, createdRequest: created });
  -  return completed !== null;
  +  for (let attempt = 1; ; attempt += 1) {
  +    try {
  +      const completed = await completeErasureRequest(request.id, auditNote, { bookingsEndedBefore, createdRequest: created });
  +      return completed !== null;
  +    } catch (error) {
  +      const conflict = error instanceof Prisma.PrismaClientKnownRequestError && error.code === 'P2034';
  +      if (!conflict || attempt === 3) throw error;
  +    }
  +  }
  ```

  (Prisma is already imported at L2.) Optionally, the same loop around the call in eraseGuestByAdmin (L19) removes the 500 for the host.
- Fix risk: Low. The retry wraps only completeErasureRequest, so no second request row is created. Tests: a unit case where $transaction rejects once with a P2034-coded PrismaClientKnownRequestError and then the guard skips (expects privacyRequest.delete with the created id and result false); a case where it rejects 3 times (expects the error); the existing 9 cases in tests/unit/privacy-erasure.test.ts must stay green.
- Resolution: FIXED in follow-up task T18 (Guest erasure retries serialization conflicts); changes are uncommitted, patch .runtime/review-patches/R4-T18.patch. Regression tests: tests/unit/privacy-erasure.test.ts.

  ```ts
    ...
    const session = await prisma.session.create({
      data: {
        id: crypto.randomUUID(),
        userId,
        bookingId,
        expiresAt,
      },
    });
  ```

  `src/lib/prisma-repositories/refreshTokenRepository.ts:L226-L237`

  ```ts
        if (!(await lockUser(tx, userId))) {
          throw new Error('Refresh authorization user does not exist');
        }
        ...
        const session = await tx.session.findUnique({ where: { id: tokenId } });
        if (!session
          || session.userId !== userId
          || session.revokedAt
          || session.expiresAt <= now) {
  ```

  (2 further evidence excerpts omitted: src/lib/guestSession.ts:L151-L158; (command))

  Verification: Found by X2. Verifier: upheld (read-all-paths).

- Problem: Session issuance is not bound to the credential that was just verified. authenticatePortalUser verifies the password against a hash read without a lock, and issueGuestSession inserts the Session row without re-reading users.password_hash under a lock that conflicts with the reset's UPDATE. resetGuestAccess can only revoke rows that exist when its UPDATE statements run, so a session inserted after the reset commits stays valid, and refreshTokenRepository.create accepts it as the anchor of a new 30-day family because the session is not revoked.
- Impact: Someone who knows the old password must have a sign-in in flight (between hash read and session insert, roughly the bcrypt time) at the moment the host's reset commits. They then keep a 2-hour session, or a rotating refresh family with remember-me, after a reset meant to lock them out. The attacker cannot see when the host clicks reset, and the per-IP limit (5 per 15 minutes) bounds how often a sign-in can be in flight, so the trigger is unlikely on a one-apartment site; the consequence is an authorization bypass of the reset, hence Low rather than Nit.
- Fix:

  Make the session insert take the user row lock and refuse a password-less account (resetGuestAccess always sets passwordHash = null, and a reclaim that sets a new hash cannot happen within the bcrypt window):
  ```diff
  -  const session = await prisma.session.create({
  -    data: { id: crypto.randomUUID(), userId, bookingId, expiresAt },
  -  });
  +  const session = await prisma.$transaction(async (tx) => {
  +    const rows = await tx.$queryRaw<Array<{ password_hash: string | null }>>`
  +      SELECT "password_hash" FROM "users" WHERE "id" = ${userId}::uuid FOR UPDATE`;
  +    if (!rows[0]?.password_hash) throw new PortalAuthError('INVALID_CREDENTIALS');
  +    return tx.session.create({ data: { id: crypto.randomUUID(), userId, bookingId, expiresAt } });
  +  });
  ```
  If the session transaction locks first, the reset's user UPDATE waits and its later session/family UPDATE statements (new READ COMMITTED snapshots) see and revoke the new rows; if the reset commits first, the session transaction reads NULL and fails. The family insert is then covered by create()'s existing revoked-session check. Comparing against the exact verified hash (as the candidate proposed) is stricter but needs a signature change through attachPortalAuthCookies and both routes; it is not needed for the realistic case.
- Fix risk: issueGuestSession is called directly by integration tests (logout-characterization, refresh-revoked-session-regression) whose fixture users may have no password hash; check the fixtures before adding the NOT NULL check. tests/security/auth-session.test.ts mocks prisma for issueGuestSession and must mock $transaction/$queryRaw. The sign-in route must map the new PortalAuthError to 401 (it currently only wraps authenticatePortalUser), otherwise the race outcome is a 500. Add an integration test with a barrier between authenticatePortalUser and issueGuestSession that commits resetGuestAccess and expects no unrevoked session.
- Resolution: DECLINED by the decision agent (2026-10-09): It needs a sign-in in flight at the exact moment the host resets access, and the fix would rework session issuance in the security core and its integration fixtures.

- Severity: Low
- Category: Concurrency

- Evidence:

  ```ts
      evaluateOperationalAlerts(),
  ```
