### R-625: The documented logrotate rule does not bound the Nginx error log to 14 days: notifempty stops rotation (and with it ageing) on every quiet day
- Severity: Low
- Category: Security
- Status: SUSPECTED
- Location: docs/deployment/origin-ingress-runbook.md:L89-L111
- Evidence:

  ````text
  docs/deployment/origin-ingress-runbook.md:L94-L107
    The log is kept for 14 days, as the privacy notice states. Rotate it daily on
    the host with a logrotate rule in `/etc/logrotate.d/`:
    <host-log-dir>/error.log {
        daily
        rotate 14
        missingok
        notifempty
        postrotate
            docker kill -s USR1 origin-nginx
        endscript
    }
  src/i18n/domains/legal.ts:L186 (el: L319): "The web server's error log, which can contain your IP address and the address of the requested page: 14 days."
  deploy/nginx/nginx.conf.template:L20: error_log /var/log/nginx/error.log warn;
  ````

  Verification: found by the QA finder of unit Environment validation, logging and redaction, scripts, Docker and ingress, dependencies, runbook (follow-up task T59); re-derived by an independent verifier (upheld, SUSPECTED, severity Medium) and an adversarial refuter (upheld, SUSPECTED, severity Low): VERDICT: upheld, but the severity should be Low, not Medium. Status stays SUSPECTED because I could neither run nor read logrotate here. What I tried to refute and why it failed. (a) A guard in the rule: none. The rule has daily + rotate 14 + notifempty and no maxage/ifempty. With notifempty, an empty error.log means the run does nothing (no shift, no removal), and maxage is only evaluated when a rotation happens, so adding maxage does not fix it (both my model and the verifier's show the burst staying on disk). The mechanism is sound under the documented logrotate semantics. (b) Another control elsewhere: none (grep in evidence item 3). The Nginx container is not in docker/docker-compose.pr

- Problem: Per logrotate(8), a rotated file only ages when a rotation takes place. notifempty ("Do not rotate the log if it is empty") skips the rotation on every day on which error.log is empty, and maxage is likewise "only checked if the log file is to be rotated". At level warn on a small site, error.log gets lines only for dry-run rate-limit hits and upstream refusals (for example while the web container is restarted), so most days it is empty. Then error.log.1 .. error.log.14 are never shifted or deleted. Even on busy days, rotate 14 keeps 14 rotated files plus the current one, so the oldest lines are up to about 15 days old, not 14.
- Impact: A host configured exactly as the runbook says keeps client IP addresses and request lines longer than the 14 days that decision O62 and the published privacy notice (en and el) promise. After one incident (a burst of lines, rotated once), that file stays on disk until 14 later non-empty rotations push it out, which can be months on a quiet site. This is the one control that makes the privacy line true.
- Fix: Drop notifempty so that logrotate's default ifempty rotates an empty log and every daily run ages the kept files; use rotate 13 if 14 days is a hard maximum:
<host-log-dir>/error.log {
    daily
    rotate 13
    missingok
    postrotate
        docker kill -s USR1 origin-nginx
    endscript
}
- Fix risk: Documentation only. The host then keeps up to 13 mostly empty rotated files. Keep the postrotate USR1 so Nginx reopens the file, and check the rule on the host with logrotate -d.
- To confirm (SUSPECTED only): On the Linux host (logrotate is not installed on this macOS machine and there is no network, so it was not run): leave error.log empty across a daily boundary and run logrotate -d against the rule; with notifempty the debug output reports that the log does not need rotating because it is empty. Then compare the age of the oldest rotated file after several quiet days.
- Resolution: FIXED in follow-up tasks T67 (Operator and security documentation state what the code does), T71 (The documented error-log rule keeps at most 14 days: rotate 13); changes are uncommitted, patches .runtime/review-patches/R4-T67.patch, R4-T71.patch.

### R-626: Address redaction still misses decomposed (NFD) non-ASCII letters and a special character before the @ when the address is glued to a URL; the \p{N} part of the T65 class is not pinned by a test
- Severity: Low
- Category: Security
- Status: CONFIRMED
- Location: src/lib/redaction.ts:L82-L84; tests/security/security-boundaries.test.ts:L428-L436
- Evidence:

  ````text
  src/lib/redaction.ts L82-L84 (after T65):
    // An address may hold non-ASCII letters or digits (an internationalised local part or domain); tokens stay ASCII.
    const addressRuns = token.split(/[^\p{L}\p{N}_.@+-]+/u);
    output += looksLikeEmail(token) || runs.some(looksLikeEmail) || addressRuns.some(looksLikeEmail)

  Run on 2026-10-10 with `npx --no-install tsx` (probe in the scratchpad, redactSensitiveText from src/lib/redaction.ts):
    NFC Greek local part                 => "[REDACTED_EMAIL]"
    NFD Greek local part                 => "Ζωή@example.com,https://x.example/z"
    NFC Greek domain                     => "[REDACTED_EMAIL]"
    NFD Greek domain                     => "user@παράδειγμα.gr;https://x.example/z"
    ASCII with special char before @     => "obrien'@example.com,https://x.example/z"
    non-ASCII digit in domain            => "[REDACTED_EMAIL]"
  ````

  Verification: found by the T65 implementer (probe-marks.log, probe B) and re-run by the lead on the tree after batch W6C1. The implementer also measured that adding \p{M} to the class redacts both NFD cases and leaves 300000 random ASCII inputs unchanged, and that a mutant without \p{N} passes both new T65 cases.

- Problem: T65 (R-614) made the address check Unicode-aware with the class [\p{L}\p{N}_.@+-], which does not contain combining marks (\p{M}). A decomposed letter (a base letter plus a combining accent) therefore splits the token, and an address next to a URL is left unredacted, although the code before T34 redacted it. Separately, an RFC-valid local part that ends in a special character right before the @ (for example an apostrophe or an exclamation mark) glued to a URL is left unredacted by the T34 rule that a following "://" means "not an address"; and the two decided T65 test inputs do not contain a non-ASCII digit, so removing \p{N} from the class would not fail any test.
- Impact: A guest address typed in decomposed form (rare: keyboards produce precomposed letters; macOS file names and some copy-paste sources are decomposed) or with a trailing special character, written without a space before a URL in a stored error report, security event or erasure note, is stored in clear text. These stores are access-controlled and the case is rare, so the exposure is small.
- Fix: Add \p{M} to the class: `/[^\p{L}\p{M}\p{N}_.@+-]+/u`, with one test for each NFD case (the two inputs above, built with `.normalize('NFD')`), and one assertion for 'user@παράδειγμα1.gr;https://x.example/z' to pin \p{N}. The special-character case needs no code change unless the owner wants it. Decision O94 (round 5): parts (a) and (b) are fixed by T70 with a second, mark-aware split added as one more operand (the T65 class is not widened, because widening lost redactions on synthetic tokens with two or more @ in the decision agent's probe); part (c) is accepted, not fixed: its inputs are ASCII, so any fix would change ASCII output, and a split on the RFC 5322 special characters would also mask address-free URLs such as 'https://social.example/@anna/post.html?u=https://x.example/z' (decision agent's probe).
- Fix risk: The class only widens the address check, so ASCII input cannot change (the implementer's 300000-input comparison); the existing redaction tests must still pass.
- Resolution: FIXED in follow-up task T70 (Address redaction also handles combining marks next to a URL; the digit part of the address class is pinned); changes are uncommitted, patch .runtime/review-patches/R4-T70.patch. Regression tests: tests/security/security-boundaries.test.ts.

### R-560: npm@11.18.0 is installed in the builder and migrate stages by version only, without an integrity pin
- Severity: Nit
- Category: Dependencies
- Status: SUSPECTED
- Location: docker/Dockerfile.security:L18; docker/Dockerfile.security:L85-L86
- Evidence:

  `docker/Dockerfile.security:L18-L19`

  ```text
  RUN npm install --global npm@11.18.0
  COPY package.json package-lock.json ./
  ```

  `docker/Dockerfile.security:L85-L86`

  ```text
  RUN npm install --global npm@11.18.0 \
    && npm ci --omit=dev --strict-allow-scripts --audit=false --fund=false \
  ```

  `package.json:L6`

  ```json
    "packageManager": "npm@11.18.0",
  ```

  `docker/migrate/package.json:L13-L16`

  ```json
    "allowScripts": {
      "@prisma/engines@7.10.0": true,
      "prisma@7.10.0": true
    },
  ```

  Verification: Found by T5. Verifier: upheld (reasoned).

- Problem: Every npm package of the app and the migrate image is covered by a lockfile with integrity hashes, and the base image by a digest, but the npm CLI that performs those installs is fetched by version only, with no repository-side hash.
- Impact: Only an attacker who can alter the registry response (registry compromise, or an interposed mirror/proxy trusted by the build host) could substitute a modified npm, which would then run `npm ci` and the allow-listed install scripts of the release build. Not realistic for this project; the practical result is an unrecorded trust assumption.
- Fix: Smallest: record the accepted residual risk (npm CLI and Prisma engine binary are fetched without a repository-side hash) in docs/release-verification.md. A hash pin (ARG with a sha512 checked before `npm install --global ./npm-11.18.0.tgz`) is possible but adds a per-bump maintenance step; I do not recommend it for this site.
- Fix risk: Documentation only. A hash-pin variant would change two RUN lines of Dockerfile.security and needs a docker:build and smoke:image run.
- To confirm: Compare the registry's dist.integrity for npm@11.18.0 with a value obtained from an independent trusted network (npm view is forbidden in this task).
- Resolution: DECLINED by the decision agent (2026-10-09): Not a realistic threat for this site, as the finding itself concludes.

Realistic cost: negligible, as the owner's setup (Docker Desktop on macOS) has the v2 plugin. If the branch also serves a standalone v2 binary, removing it would be a regression for such machines.

AdminAvailabilityClient.tsx L4 and L192: `FormEvent` -> `SubmitEvent`. admin/guests/page.tsx L209 and AdminLoginClient.tsx L13: `React.FormEvent` -> `React.SubmitEvent`.

(2) In errors/route.ts the `clientIp === 'unknown'` branch can never be taken, because the limiter has already required a canonical address. (3) clientIdentity.ts L110 reports 'sentinel' (meaning a literal 'unknown' value) when the client-IP header is absent, where 'missing' is the accurate reason. - Problem: (1) The cutoff is computed by setUTCMonth, which overflows at month ends; the result is correct for today's 12 months but would select bookings 1-3 days early for a period such as 6 or 18 months. Unit tests use only one date (2030-07-14). (2) When any guest erasure fails, runRetention throws after the loop and the worker log for that run shows only the error string, not the counts of work already committed.
- Impact: (1) No effect with GUEST_DATA_RETENTION_MONTHS = 12. It becomes an early deletion of 1-3 days only if the retention period changes to a value that is not a multiple of 12 (the period is the owner/accountant's deferred decision). (2) After a failed run the operator cannot see in syslog how many rows were deleted or check-in requests redacted in that run.
- Fix:

### R-565: Retention erasure re-check compares booking end dates with the full cutoff instant in JS, while the SQL selection compares them with the cutoff's UTC date
- Severity: Nit
- Category: Logic
- Status: CONFIRMED

- Evidence:

  `src/lib/operationalMonitor.ts:L230-L231`

  ```ts
  const guestDataCutoff = new Date(now);
    guestDataCutoff.setUTCMonth(guestDataCutoff.getUTCMonth() - GUEST_DATA_RETENTION_MONTHS);
  ```

  `src/lib/operationalMonitor.ts:L268-L269`

  ```ts
  const expiredGuests = await prisma.user.findMany({
      where: { bookings: { some: {}, every: { endDate: { lt: guestDataCutoff } } } },
  ```

  `src/lib/privacyService.ts:L109-L111`

  ```ts
  if (guard) {
        const stillExpired = user !== null && user.bookings.length > 0
          && user.bookings.every((booking) => booking.endDate < guard.bookingsEndedBefore);
  ```

  `prisma/schema.prisma:L32-L33`

  ```prisma
  startDate         DateTime            @map("start_date") @db.Date
    endDate           DateTime            @map("end_date") @db.Date
  ```

  Verification: Found by X4. Verifier: upheld (executed).

- Problem: The comment says the in-transaction guard re-checks the retention predicate, but on the cutoff's anniversary date the guard is looser than the SQL selection: it accepts end_date equal to the cutoff's UTC date, which the SQL rejects.
- Impact: None today. If eraseGuestForRetention gets another caller, or the selection moves to JS, a guest whose last booking ended exactly 12 months ago would be erased one day earlier than the check-in-request redaction (which uses the SQL date predicate) treats the same booking.
- Fix:

  Truncate the cutoff to a UTC date once, so both predicates agree:

  ```diff
  --- a/src/lib/operationalMonitor.ts
     guestDataCutoff.setUTCMonth(guestDataCutoff.getUTCMonth() - GUEST_DATA_RETENTION_MONTHS);
  +  guestDataCutoff.setUTCHours(0, 0, 0, 0);
  ```
- Fix risk: Very low. The SQL parameters are unchanged (the adapter already sends only the date), so selection and redaction behave the same. tests/unit/operational-retention.test.ts may assert the exact cutoff passed to the mocked eraseGuestForRetention and must be checked and run. The integration guest-data-retention test passes its own cutoff and is unaffected.
- Resolution: DECLINED by the decision agent (2026-10-09): No effect with the single current caller.

  (c) tests/security/proxy-page-headers.test.ts L10: drop the headers argument (`proxy(new NextRequest(`${ORIGIN}${path}`))`), or use `cookie: 'lang=en'` if a cookie is wanted.

  (d) security-monitoring.ts L80-L81 and ready/route.ts L17:

  ```diff
  +    await tx.$executeRaw`SET LOCAL statement_timeout = '1800ms'`;
  ```

  (same for lock_timeout), and rename the tx mock key `$executeRawUnsafe` to `$executeRaw` in tests/routes/csp-report.test.ts L7/L48 and tests/security/client-identity-route-regression.test.ts L176.
- Fix risk: (b) none while defaultLocale is 'en'; run tests/security/proxy-page-headers.test.ts. (c) with lang=en the proxy would stop setting a lang response cookie on /en paths; no current assertion reads it; run the same test file. (d) the transaction mocks in csp-report.test.ts and client-identity-route-regression.test.ts expose only $executeRawUnsafe, so without renaming them tx.$executeRaw is undefined and the audit write throws inside the transaction; update the mocks and run both files. That the tagged form with no interpolations sends the same SQL rests on the existing use at refreshTokenRepository.ts L161 (not re-checked in Prisma source); the readiness path is covered by tests/integration (npm run test:integration, lead-run).

### R-575: Nits (grouped): SPDX OR evaluated as AND, hostile DB constants duplicated in verify-release.mjs, EVIDENCE_CAPTURE_FAILED hides its cause (sub-item 2, rounded duration sum, is not a defect and is dropped)
- Severity: Nit
- Category: Maintainability
- Status: CONFIRMED
- Location: scripts/check-licenses.ts:L248-L276; scripts/verify-release.mjs:L96-L106; scripts/lib/release-gates.mjs:L6-L19; scripts/lib/npm-audit-evidence.ts:L319-L328
- Evidence:

  ```ts
    | {

        right: SpdxExpressionNode;
        conjunction: 'and' | 'or';
      };
  ```

  `scripts/check-licenses.ts:L275`

  ```ts
  return isAllowedSpdxExpression(node.left) && isAllowedSpdxExpression(node.right);
  ```

  `scripts/verify-release.mjs:L96-L106`

  ```js
  DATABASE_URL: 'postgresql://«redacted»',
  DIRECT_URL: 'postgresql://«redacted»',
  SHADOW_DATABASE_URL: 'postgresql://«redacted»',
  PGHOST: 'hostile.invalid',
  ... PGPORT, PGDATABASE, PGUSER, PGPASSWORD, POSTGRES_DB, POSTGRES_USER, POSTGRES_PASSWORD: 'hostile' ...
  ```

  `scripts/lib/release-gates.mjs:L6-L19`

  ```js
  export const HOSTILE_INTEGRATION_ENVIRONMENT = Object.freeze({
    INTEGRATION_POSTGRES_IMAGE: APPROVED_POSTGRES_IMAGE,
    DATABASE_URL: 'postgresql://«redacted»',
    ... the same eleven keys with the same values ...
  ```

  `scripts/lib/release-policy.mjs:L286-L288`

  ```js
  if (JSON.stringify(HOSTILE_INTEGRATION_ENVIRONMENT)
    !== JSON.stringify(EXPECTED_HOSTILE_INTEGRATION_ENVIRONMENT)) {
    errors.push('the integration gate must use only the exact hostile DB/PG environment');
  ```

  (4 further evidence excerpts omitted: scripts/tests/release-policy.test.mjs:L1067; scripts/lib/npm-audit-evidence.ts:L32-L42; scripts/lib/npm-audit-evidence.ts:L323-L327; scripts/check-licenses.ts:L128)

  Verification: Found by T1b. Verifier: upheld (executed).

- Problem: (1) isAllowedSpdxExpression ignores the `conjunction` field that the type declares (L71) and requires both sides for OR as well as AND (L275), so a dual-licensed package with one allowed alternative is rejected (executed, see trace). (3) The eleven hostile DB/PG values exist in verify-release.mjs L96-L106 (applies to every gate) and again in release-gates.mjs L8-L18 (integration profile); the policy compares only the second. (4) runNpmAuditEvidenceCheck prints a failure reason that is not in the NpmAuditFailureReason union, and its catch drops the error, so the outside-repository guard, an unwritable or missing temp dir and any filesystem error print the same line.
- Impact: (1) False positive only (safe direction): a future dual-licensed dependency such as '(MIT OR GPL-3.0-only)' fails the license gate and forces an exception entry although the MIT alternative is usable. No current dependency triggers it (the gate passes at HEAD). (3) A change to one block but not the other is not caught by validate:release-policy. Low probability, no current mismatch. (4) If TMPDIR points inside the repository (TMPDIR is passed through by verify-release.mjs L30), gate 24 fails with EVIDENCE_CAPTURE_FAILED and the operator cannot tell why without a debugger.
- Fix:

  (1) scripts/check-licenses.ts L275:

  ```diff
  -  return isAllowedSpdxExpression(node.left) && isAllowedSpdxExpression(node.right);
  +  const left = isAllowedSpdxExpression(node.left);
  +  const right = isAllowedSpdxExpression(node.right);
  +  return node.conjunction === 'or' ? left || right : left && right;
  ```

  and add the OR and AND cases to tests/unit/check-licenses.test.ts.

  (3) Export a database-only constant from release-gates.mjs and spread it into both the base environment and HOSTILE_INTEGRATION_ENVIRONMENT (`{ INTEGRATION_POSTGRES_IMAGE: ..., ...HOSTILE_DATABASE_ENVIRONMENT }`, keeping the key order because the policy compares JSON.stringify). Do not spread the whole integration object into the base environment: that would add INTEGRATION_POSTGRES_IMAGE to every gate.

  (4) In the catch of runNpmAuditEvidenceCheck: `catch (error) { ...; writeLine(`NPM_AUDIT_FAILURE_DETAIL=${(error as NodeJS.ErrnoException)?.code ?? (error instanceof Error ? error.message : 'unknown')}`);` Use the code for fs errors (their messages contain paths); the guard's Error has no code but a fixed message, which is safe to print. The proposed `error.code` alone would print nothing for the guard.
- Fix risk: (1) OR semantics is a policy decision (the licensee may choose the allowed alternative); confirm with the owner. tests/unit/check-licenses.test.ts is one of the five files that write to fixed directories, so the lead must run it. (3) release-policy compares JSON.stringify, so key order must be preserved; run `npm run validate:release-policy` and `npm run test:release-policy`; knip must see the new export used. (4) The tests use arrayContaining, so an extra line is compatible; check that nothing parses the NPM_AUDIT_* lines (none found in this review: only validate-security consumes the boolean).
- Resolution: DECLINED by the decision agent (2026-10-09): No current dependency triggers part (1), and parts (3) and (4) only affect diagnostics.

  (6 further evidence excerpts omitted: src/components/shell/SiteFooter.tsx:L42; src/app/admin/layout.tsx:L27-L28; src/data/brand.ts:L1-L2; src/components/Toast.tsx:L19-L37; src/app/[locale]/layout.tsx:L31-L38; tests/components/toast.test.tsx:L45-L59)

  Verification: Found by F1. Verifier: upheld (executed).

- Problem: (1) The locale layout has an orphan comment (L14) and a comment (L33) that says the route stays fully static, but the root layout awaits headers() and every route builds as dynamic (ƒ). (2) The wordmark 'Dolce Far Niente' is written out in SiteHeader (module const), SiteFooter and the admin layout, while src/data/brand.ts holds only BRAND_NAME. (3) ToastProvider works out the locale again from the pathname instead of taking the `eff` its parent already has. (4) The toast GC interval runs every 400 ms even when no toast is on screen.

(2) A wordmark change must touch three components plus the manifest short_name; the footer copy is the only one no test pins. (3) Adding a third locale would show the toast dismiss label in English with no error. (4) A no-op timer callback every 400 ms on every localized page; negligible.

Change L33 to: `// Session state is fetched client-side; this layout reads no cookies.` (2) In src/data/brand.ts add `export const WORDMARK = 'Dolce Far Niente';`, remove the local const in SiteHeader.tsx:23 and import it there, and use `{WORDMARK}` in SiteFooter.tsx:42 and admin/layout.tsx:28. (3) Optional, lowest value: `export function ToastProvider({ children, locale }: { children: React.ReactNode; locale: Locale })`, drop usePathname and the derived locale, and pass `<ToastProvider locale={eff}>` in the locale layout. This also means updating the 25 `<ToastProvider>` render sites in 9 test files, or the test files will fail to type-check. (4) `const hasToasts = toasts.length > 0; useEffect(() => { if (!hasToasts) return; const t = setInterval(/* unchanged body */, 400); return () => clearInterval(t); }, [hasToasts]);`
- Fix risk: (1) and (2) do not change behaviour; run site-shell.test.tsx, admin-layout-header.test.tsx and brand.test.ts. (3) changes ToastProvider's props, so every test that renders it needs the new prop; run typecheck and the checkin-*, i18n-copy, stay-routes, guide-* and toast component tests. (4) Run tests/components/toast.test.tsx: a toast must still auto-dismiss after about 5 s, and the no-re-render case must still pass. The interval restarts each time the toast count goes from 0 to 1, which can delay expiry by up to 400 ms (well within the test's 5600 ms window).
- Resolution: DECLINED by the decision agent (2026-10-09): Comments and literals with no behaviour change.

### R-578: Nits: formatDistance prints "1,000 m" for 0.995-0.999 km; getItem's slug fallback can never run
- Severity: Nit
- Category: Maintainability
- Status: CONFIRMED
- Location: src/components/guide/guideEntries.ts:L59-L66; src/lib/data.ts:L50; src/lib/data.ts:L74
- Evidence:

  `src/components/guide/guideEntries.ts:L59-L66`

  ```ts
  /** "1.5 km" from 1 km up (one decimal), "650 m" below (to 10 m), in the locale's unit style. */
  export function formatDistance(km: number, locale: Locale): string {
    if (km < 1) {
      const metres = Math.max(10, Math.round(km * 100) * 10);
      return new Intl.NumberFormat(locale, { style: 'unit', unit: 'meter', maximumFractionDigits: 0 }).format(metres);
    }
    return new Intl.NumberFormat(locale, { style: 'unit', unit: 'kilometer', maximumFractionDigits: 1 }).format(km);
  }
  ```

  `src/lib/data.ts:L50`

  ```ts
      const result = ItemSchema.safeParse({ ...(obj as object), slug: toSlug(name) });
  ```

  `src/lib/data.ts:L73-L74`

  ```ts
    const items = getItemsByCategory(categoryId);
    return items.find((i) => (i.slug ?? toSlug(i.name)) === slug) ?? null;
  ```

  `src/data/schemas.ts:L49`

  ```ts
    slug: z.string().optional(),
  ```

  Verification: Found by F5. Verifier: upheld (executed).

- Problem: (1) The metre branch of formatDistance does not handle rounding up to 1000 m, so it prints '1,000 m' instead of '1 km'. (2) getItem has a slug fallback that the data loader makes unreachable.
- Impact: (1) A future place 995-999 m from the apartment would show '1,000 m' on its card while a place 1.0 km away shows '1 km'; nothing affected today. (2) A reader may wrongly infer that slugs can be missing or set in the JSON; no runtime effect.
- Fix: (1) guideEntries.ts L61: `if (km < 0.995) {` (values from 0.995 then format as '1 km'); add `expect(formatDistance(0.996, 'en')).toBe('1 km')` to tests/unit/guide-entries.test.ts. (2) data.ts L74: `return items.find((i) => i.slug === slug) ?? null;`
- Fix risk: (1) Distances in 0.995-0.999 km change from '1,000 m' to '1 km'; run tests/unit/guide-entries.test.ts. (2) None while getItemsByCategory sets slug; run tests/unit/data-map-navigation.test.ts.
- Resolution: DECLINED by the decision agent (2026-10-09): No place is 0.995-0.999 km away today, and the slug fallback cannot run.

### R-581: The parser's BOM check uses an invisible raw U+FEFF literal (the test does too), and in production the fatal TextDecoder already strips a leading BOM
- Severity: Nit
- Category: Maintainability
- Status: CONFIRMED
- Location: src/lib/availability/icalParser.ts:L211; tests/unit/ical-parser.test.ts:L85-L87
- Evidence:

  `src/lib/availability/icalParser.ts:L211`

  ```ts
    const body = text.startsWith('<U+FEFF, invisible>') ? text.slice(1) : text;
  (xxd of the line: ...7374 6172 7473 5769 7468 2827 efbb bf27 29... = startsWith('EF BB BF'))
  ```

  `tests/unit/ical-parser.test.ts:L85-L87`

  ```ts
    it('strips a UTF-8 byte order mark', () => {
      expect(parseBlockedRanges(`<U+FEFF, invisible>${calendar(NOT_AVAILABLE_EVENT)}`)).toEqual([expected[1]]);
    });
  (xxd of L86: ...6765 7328 60ef bbbf 247b... = backtick EF BB BF ${)
  ```

  `src/lib/availability/icalFetch.ts:L82`

  ```ts
      return new TextDecoder('utf-8', { fatal: true }).decode(body);
  ```

  Verification: Found by S6.2, D1, S6 (independent reports: S6.2-03, D1-05, S6-06). Verifier: upheld (executed).

- Problem: The BOM check compares against an invisible character literal, so a reader cannot see what is compared. If a tool stripped the character, the check would become startsWith(''), which is always true, and the parser would drop the first character of every calendar. In the production fetch path the branch is also redundant, because TextDecoder with the default ignoreBOM: false already removes a leading BOM. That was observed by running it.
- Impact: Readability only. A tool that silently stripped the character would break parsing of every calendar, but the parser tests would catch it.
- Fix:

  ```diff
  -  const body = text.startsWith('<raw U+FEFF>') ? text.slice(1) : text;
  +  const body = text.startsWith('﻿') ? text.slice(1) : text;
  ```

  Make the same change in tests/unit/ical-parser.test.ts:86 (`﻿${calendar(NOT_AVAILABLE_EVENT)}`). Keep the branch, because direct callers of the pure parser use it. (The proposed diff showed the same invisible literal on both sides; the escape sequence ﻿ is the intended replacement.)
- Fix risk: None functionally: '﻿' is the same code unit. Run tests/unit/ical-parser.test.ts.
- Resolution: DECLINED by the decision agent (2026-10-09): Readability only; the parser tests would catch a stripped character.

- Problem: About 40 lines of URL parsing and a URL rewrite (prismaPgConfig.ts L14-24, L26-30, L45-70) plus three of four tests support Prisma 6 query-engine URL parameters that the project never sets. Without these parameters the module only applies fixed defaults.
- Impact: No runtime defect. Reading and maintenance cost only: a reader sees a nine-name compatibility layer and a debug log hint (visible only with PRISMA_LOG_LIFECYCLE=1) that advertises it, although nothing uses it. Counter-consideration: the shim is also the only way to change the pool size (connection_limit -> pg max) without a code change, and it is documented nowhere, so removal trades a hidden lever for less code; and the owner declined the analogous 'unused knob' item R-348 for security-config (O39), a different module, so the owner may prefer to keep it. - Fix risk: Option B: if production DATABASE_URL carries '?connection_limit=N' the pool silently reverts to the pg default of 10; a '?schema=x' would no longer set the adapter schema option and would reach pg unchanged (pg does not use it). Test: tests/unit/prisma-adapter-config.test.ts, tests/unit/prisma-lifecycle.test.ts (mocks the module, unaffected), the coverage gate (prismaPgConfig.ts is in the explicit include at vitest.config.ts L71; thresholds must still hold), and the integration suite as a smoke of the default pool settings.
- Resolution: DECLINED by the decision agent (2026-10-09): Keep the shim: it is the only lever for the pool size, the same reasoning as the earlier decision O39.

  Verification: Found by X1. Verifier: upheld (read-all-paths).

- Problem: (1) MetricCard declares `icon` and `valueClassName` (default 'admin-accent'), but neither of its 2 callers passes them, so the icon slot and the class override are dead. (2) In the admin guests page, issueClaimGrant takes a `channel` parameter with default 'REMOTE', and its only call never sets it. The parameter suggests the UI can issue ONSITE grants, but it cannot. ONSITE grants come only from direct API calls (the smoke script and an integration test), and the channel is used only as stored and audit metadata. (3) These exports have no importer in the repo: POSTGRES_IMAGE_POLICY_STAGES and POSTGRES_IMAGE_POLICY_FAILURE_CLASSES (used in-file only, for `typeof` types), GUIDE_FILTER_KEYS (used in-file only), and the types GalleryRoom, NightState, PriceGroup, PrivacyCookieName, PrivacyLocalStorageKey, PrivacySessionStorageKey and LegalItem.
- Impact: No runtime effect. A reader may think MetricCard supports icons or tone overrides, or that the admin UI can issue on-site claim grants, when neither is the case.

MetricCard.tsx: remove `icon?` and `valueClassName?` from the props, change the signature to `({ label, value }: MetricCardProps)`, hardcode `className="mt-2 text-3xl font-semibold admin-accent"` and drop the L19 icon line. guests/page.tsx:179: `const issueClaimGrant = async (bookingId: string) => {` and at L186 `body: JSON.stringify({ channel: 'REMOTE', ttlMinutes: 30 })`. Leave the API's ONSITE enum alone, because the smoke script and the integration test use it. Remove the `export` keyword from POSTGRES_IMAGE_POLICY_STAGES, POSTGRES_IMAGE_POLICY_FAILURE_CLASSES, GUIDE_FILTER_KEYS, GalleryRoom, NightState, PriceGroup, PrivacyCookieName, PrivacyLocalStorageKey, PrivacySessionStorageKey and LegalItem. Do NOT remove `export` from straightLineKm, formatDistance or reliefPoint, because unit tests import them.
- Fix risk: Low. Every change is type-level or affects props no caller passes. Rerun typecheck, tests/unit/admin-css-tokens.test.ts, tests/components/admin-guests.test.tsx, tests/unit/postgres-image-policy-command.test.ts and knip. Removing an export can surface a TypeScript 'exported type uses private name' error if an exported signature references the type. The exported PostgresImagePolicyStage and FailureClass types use `typeof` on the constants, which is allowed for non-exported consts, but typecheck must confirm it.
- Resolution: DECLINED by the decision agent (2026-10-09): Dead props and exports with no runtime effect.

- Location: src/app/[locale]/error.tsx:L13; src/app/[locale]/not-found.tsx:L11; src/app/error.tsx:L20; src/components/Toast.tsx:L22; src/lib/security-middleware-edge.ts:L36-L37
- Evidence:


  `src/app/[locale]/not-found.tsx:L11`

  ```tsx

  ```

  `src/app/error.tsx:L20`

  ```tsx
    const locale: Locale = pathname?.startsWith('/el') ? 'el' : 'en';
  ```

  `src/components/Toast.tsx:L22`

  ```tsx
    const locale: Locale = pathname?.startsWith('/el') ? 'el' : 'en';
  ```

  `src/lib/security-middleware-edge.ts:L36-L37`

  ```ts
      const pathLocale = locales.find((l) => pathname === `/${l}` || pathname.startsWith(`/${l}/`));
      requestHeaders.set('x-locale', pathLocale ?? 'en');
  ```

  (3 further evidence excerpts omitted: src/app/layout.tsx:L43; src/i18n/config.ts:L1-L3; tests/security/proxy-page-headers.test.ts:L30-L31)

  Verification: Found by X8. Verifier: upheld (read-all-paths).

- Problem: The client error, 404 and toast components each re-implement 'which locale does this path use' with a hard-coded '/el' literal instead of the single definition in src/i18n/config.ts, and the edge middleware falls back to a literal 'en' instead of defaultLocale.
- Impact: No current defect. If a third locale is added or the default flips to 'el', the 404, both error pages and the toast dismiss label stay English/Greek-only and the x-locale header for non-localized routes (/admin, /offline) stays 'en' until those five lines are found by hand.
- Fix: Add `export function localeFromPathname(pathname: string | null | undefined): Locale` to src/i18n/config.ts (exact `/${l}` or `/${l}/` prefix match over `locales`, else defaultLocale), use it in the four client files, and use it (or just omit the fallback literal) in security-middleware-edge.ts line 37. Do not widen to proxy.ts or shellLinks.ts.
- Fix risk: Must keep '/elx' -> 'en' (tests/security/proxy-page-headers.test.ts) and the client tests that set a pathname (tests/components/locale-not-found.test.tsx uses '/el/moments/nope'). config.ts is imported by the edge runtime already (proxy.ts), so the helper must stay dependency-free.
- Resolution: DECLINED by the decision agent (2026-10-09): No defect with two locales, and no third locale is planned.

(b) Check that the guide map and the check-in map still swap the placeholder for Leaflet when scrolled into view. (c) and (d) carry no behaviour change and are covered by typecheck and the existing map tests.

- Severity: Nit
- Category: Redundant
- Status: CONFIRMED
- Location: src/lib/prisma.ts:L108-L140
- Evidence:

  `src/lib/prisma.ts:L7-L10`

  ```ts
  type ExtendedGlobal = typeof globalThis & {
    __prisma__?: PrismaClient;
    __prismaShutdownHooksRegistered__?: boolean;
  };
  ```

  `src/lib/prisma.ts:L111-L114`

  ```ts
    } else {
      // Leave undefined during build/time when no DATABASE_URL is configured.
      globalThisWithPrisma.__prisma__ = undefined as unknown as PrismaClient;
    }
  ```

  `src/lib/prisma.ts:L129-L140`

  ```ts
  export const prisma: PrismaClient = new Proxy({} as PrismaClient, {
    get(_target, prop, receiver) {
      const client = getActivePrismaClient();
      const value = Reflect.get(client as unknown as object, prop, receiver);
      return typeof value === 'function' ? value.bind(client) : value;
    },
    set(_target, prop, value) {
      const client = getActivePrismaClient();
      Reflect.set(client as unknown as object, prop, value);
      return true;
    },
  });
  ```

  Output of scratch: agents/verify-S9/settrap.ts (real prisma.ts; Reflect.set wrapped to count calls whose target is the real client, while touching model delegates, $transaction, $queryRaw, $on, $extends and running a query and an interactive transaction):

  ```text
  query error (expected): PrismaClientKnownRequestError
  tx error (expected): PrismaClientKnownRequestError
  Reflect.set calls from proxy set trap: 0
  ```

  Verification: Found by S9. Verifier: upheld (executed).

- Problem: (a) L111-L114 cast undefined to PrismaClient through unknown and assign it to an optional property that is already falsy, which is a no-op. (b) L132 and L137 cast `client as unknown as object` although PrismaClient is already an object type. (c) The `set` trap has no caller in the repo or in the Prisma paths exercised, and it ignores Reflect.set's result and always returns true.
- Impact: No runtime effect. The double casts suggest a type problem that does not exist and would hide a real one if the global's type changed.
- Fix: Drop the else branch at L111-L114 (keep the `if (process.env.DATABASE_URL)` assignment), use `Reflect.get(client, prop, receiver)`, and delete the `set` trap (L135-L139). If the S9-01 fix lands, the `possiblePrisma as unknown` cast at L196-L197 disappears with the hooks.
- Fix risk: Without the set trap, an assignment through `prisma.x = ...` would land on the empty proxy target instead of the client; no such assignment exists today (searches above). Run typecheck and tests/unit/prisma-lifecycle.test.ts.
- Resolution: DECLINED by the decision agent (2026-10-09): No runtime effect.

- Severity: Nit
- Category: Security
- Status: CONFIRMED

  ```ts
      const existingUser = await tx.user.findUnique({ where: { phoneE164: normalized.e164 } });

        if (existingUser.passwordHash) {
          const matches = await bcrypt.compare(input.password, existingUser.passwordHash);
          if (!matches) throw new PortalAuthError('INVALID_CREDENTIALS');
  ```

  `src/lib/portalAuthService.ts:L241-L243`

  ```ts
      if (grant.booking.userId && grant.booking.userId !== userId) {
        throw new PortalAuthError('BOOKING_ALREADY_CLAIMED');
      }
  ```

  `src/app/api/portal/claims/route.ts:L57-L61`

  ```ts
      if (error instanceof PortalAuthError) {
        if (error.code === 'BOOKING_ALREADY_CLAIMED') {
          throw new ApiError(ApiErrorCode.CONFLICT, 'This booking is already linked to another account');
        }
        throw new ApiError(ApiErrorCode.UNAUTHORIZED, 'The claim token or account credentials are invalid');
  ```

  `src/lib/portalAuthService.ts:L112-L113`

  ```ts
   * Claiming it with the same phone sets a new password (null-hash branch of
   * consumeBookingClaimGrant); a different phone is refused as already claimed.
  ```

  Output of agents/verify-AT/at.mts (scratch, real consumeBookingClaimGrant, grant for booking owned by u1, phone of u3 with a password):

  ```text
  wrong-guess-1 -> INVALID_CREDENTIALS
  victim-password -> BOOKING_ALREADY_CLAIMED
  grant consume updateMany calls: 0
  ```

  Verification: Found by AT.2. Verifier: upheld (executed). Refuter: upheld, severity Nit.

- Problem: For a grant whose booking already has an owner (only access-reset grants), the claim transaction verifies the password of the account named by the submitted phone before checking ownership: wrong password gives 401, right password gives 409, and the grant stays open. The code comment and docs/security/claim-token-transport.md say a different phone is simply refused as already claimed.
- Impact: A guest who received an access-reset token can, until it expires (30 min default, up to 24 h), confirm guesses of another guest's password, including past guests for whom sign-in always answers 401. Budget: claims limiter 5/h per address (per-phone part bypassable as in AT-01) and the exchange limiter 20/h per address. The marginal gain over the by-design oracle of any open grant is small.
- Fix:

  In consumeBookingClaimGrant, check ownership before credentials:

  ```diff
       const existingUser = await tx.user.findUnique({ where: { phoneE164: normalized.e164 } });
  +    // Ownership first: for a booking that already has an owner, another phone gets the same answer
  +    // whether or not it knows that account's password.
  +    if (grant.booking.userId && grant.booking.userId !== existingUser?.id) {
  +      throw new PortalAuthError('BOOKING_ALREADY_CLAIMED');
  +    }
       let userId: string;
  ```
- Fix risk: Same final status for every case except 'other phone with existing account and wrong password on an owned booking' (401 -> 409). The L223 check for password-less accounts on unowned bookings is still needed and unchanged. Run tests/unit/guest-access-reset.test.ts and add a case: owned booking, other phone with a password, wrong password -> BOOKING_ALREADY_CLAIMED and bcrypt.compare not called.
- Resolution: FIXED in follow-up task T10 (Portal auth reveals neither which accounts exist nor other guests' passwords); changes are uncommitted, patch .runtime/review-patches/R4-T10.patch. Regression tests: tests/unit/portal-sign-in-timing.test.ts, tests/unit/guest-access-reset.test.ts.

Seen only by a guest when a new version is detected or on the iOS tip.

(b) in MetricCard.tsx drop `icon`/`valueClassName` from the props and the destructuring, hard-code `admin-accent` on the value <p>, and delete the L19 branch. (c) change the Callout.tsx:19 sentence to say that success/danger are styled in ui.css but used as raw classes in CheckInInfo and ErrorSummary (comment-only change); routing those sites through <Callout> is a separate behaviour change (adds an icon, changes <p> to <div>) and should be its own task. (d) either reword the six strings without the arrow (e.g. 'Update available: {old} to {new}', 'Share, then Add to Home Screen' and the Greek equivalents) or keep the arrows and note the exception in identity.md §2.3; do not add U+2192 to the unicode-range because the shipped woff2 does not contain the glyph.

(b) typecheck must pass (neither caller passes the removed props); tests/unit/admin-css-tokens.test.ts reads MetricCard.tsx for palette/legacy colour classes only and 'admin-accent' is a token class. (c) none. (d) guest-facing copy change: owner approval is needed (copy approvals C1/C2 in PROGRESS decisions); rerun the i18n/NFC tests and any test that pins the banner strings (git grep over tests for the arrow found no pinned string), and check the Greek text.
- Resolution: DECLINED by the decision agent (2026-10-09): Owner decision O76: dead CSS and props and a stale comment, and the arrow copy stays.

(3) ClientLogger.info has no caller, so the `case 'info'` branch in log() at L59-61 is also unreachable. (4) apartmentData.location and the `location` field that getApartmentContent returns are never read.

### R-600: Nits (grouped): two CSS custom properties nothing consumes, and the motion-ok variant with no uses
- Severity: Nit
- Category: Unused
- Status: CONFIRMED
- Location: src/styles/base.css:L15; src/styles/tokens.css:L114; src/styles/motion.css:L10-L16
- Evidence:

  `src/styles/base.css:L13-L15`

  ```css
  /* §2.5/§2.6 Greek display line-heights and label tracking */
  :lang(el) {
    --lh-display-extra: .06;
  ```

  `src/styles/tokens.css:L113-L114`

  ```css
  --text-micro: .75rem;
  --text-micro--line-height: 1.2;
  ```

  `src/styles/motion.css:L10-L16`

  ```css
  @custom-variant motion-ok {
    @media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference) {
      &:where(:root[data-motion="full"] *) {
        @slot;
      }
    }
  }
  ```

  Output of command output:

  ```text
  git grep -n lh-display-extra -> docs/design/identity.md:311, src/styles/base.css:15 (2 hits, no var())
  git grep -n text-micro--line-height -> src/styles/tokens.css:114 (1 hit)
  git grep -n text-micro -- src -> only `font-size: var(--text-micro)` in guide.css/home.css/map.css plus tokens.css; no `text-micro` class in any .tsx
  git grep -n motion-ok -> motion.css:4 (comment), motion.css:10 (definition), docs/design/identity.md:705
  var() consumers of tokens.css text companions: every --text-*--line-height/letter-spacing has >=1 var() use except --text-micro--line-height (0)
  ```

  Verification: Found by X1. Verifier: upheld (read-all-paths).

- Problem: --lh-display-extra (base.css:15) and --text-micro--line-height (tokens.css:114) are declared, but nothing consumes them. The motion-ok custom variant (motion.css:10-16) is defined, but no class uses it.
- Impact: Dead declarations with no visual effect. Someone could tune --lh-display-extra expecting Greek display line-heights to change, and nothing would happen.
- Fix: Delete base.css:15 and tokens.css:114, and update identity.md:311 so it no longer prescribes --lh-display-extra. Keeping or removing the motion-ok variant is the lead's call: it is the documented utility gate in identity §5.2, and tests/unit/motion-css-gate.test.ts should be checked before removing it.
- Fix risk: Very low. Since nothing reads either property, removing them changes no computed style. If motion-ok is removed, re-run tests/unit/motion-css-gate.test.ts and tests/unit/design-tokens.test.ts.
- Resolution: DECLINED by the decision agent (2026-10-09): Unused custom properties; the motion-ok variant stays as the utility gate documented in identity §5.2.

### R-627: Guide filter block is wider than a phone viewport: the List/Map toggle and the last category chips sit off-screen and cannot be reached at 360-700 px (outside the unit's files, found while testing the shell with reduced motion)
- Severity: High
- Category: Bug
- Status: CONFIRMED
- Location: src/styles/components/guide.css:L75-L79
- Evidence:
  ```
  .guide-filters {
    display: grid;
    gap: 14px;
    margin-bottom: 24px;
  }
  ```
  Independent verifier (W2a): Reproduced by the LEAD in headless Chrome (puppeteer 25, Node 22.19.0, loopback only, script .runtime/review5/wave2/guide-filters-check.mjs) BEFORE any verifier ran, and re-measured after the fix. Before: /en/moments at 390x844 (isMobile): .guide-filters 351 px wide with computed grid-template-columns 632.141px, .guide-search 20-580, .guide-view (List/Map) x 488-652 (viewport 390), .guide-chips 16-480; with full motion main {overflow-x: clip} hides it (document overflow 0), with prefers-reduced-motion the page scrolls sideways (262 px at 390 px; /el/moments at 360 px: 346 px, viewport 706). 768 px and 1280 px fine. A screenshot at 390 px showed the search field without its right border and no List/Map toggle. After the fix (grid-template-columns: minmax(0, 1fr)): columns 351 px (324 px at 360), search 20-371, .guide-view 207-371 (146-342 at 360 px), document overflow 0 in both motion modes, screenshot shows the toggle under the chips.
- Problem: `.guide-filters` is a grid with no `grid-template-columns`, so its implicit `auto` column takes the min-content contribution of `.guide-filters__row` (a flex-wrap row whose `.guide-chips` child holds 640 px of chips). The column grows to 632 px inside a 351 px container, so the search label is 560 px wide and the row, chips and the `.guide-view` List/Map toggle are laid out past the viewport edge. In the default full-motion mode `:root[data-motion="full"] .site-main { overflow-x: clip; }` (src/styles/motion.css L535) hides the excess, so nothing scrolls and nothing reveals it; with prefers-reduced-motion: reduce the document scrolls sideways. Executed in the repo's puppeteer on http://localhost:3000/en/moments at 390x844 with isMobile and full motion: `.guide-view` x 488-652 (List 492-567, Map 569-648) against a 390 px viewport; chips 'Taygetos' 461-565 and 'Sites' 573-652; `.guide-search` 20-580; `.guide-chips` scrollWidth 640 / clientWidth 465, so scrolling the chip box does not bring them into the viewport; `.guide-filters` computed grid-template-columns '632.141px'. Document overflow with reduced motion on /el/moments: 360 px 346, 390 px 317, 430 px 279, 600 px 118, 700 px 23, 768 px 0 (search 560 px against containers 324/351/387/540/630). Screenshot at 390 px shows the search field without its right border and no List/Map toggle. guide.css and GuideList.tsx are unchanged since f7958fa and REVIEW.md/PROGRESS.md do not mention 'guide-filters' or 'guide-search' (grep), so this is a latent defect that the clip masks in the overflow audits.
- Impact: On phones, the main device for the QR guide, the Map view toggle is unreachable (not visible, and a clipped overflow cannot be scrolled or focused into view), two of six category chips are hidden, and the search field is cut off. With reduced motion the whole page can be dragged sideways by up to 346 px.
- Fix: Add one declaration to the rule: `.guide-filters { display: grid; grid-template-columns: minmax(0, 1fr); gap: 14px; margin-bottom: 24px; }`. Verified by injecting `.guide-filters { grid-template-columns: minmax(0, 1fr); }` into the live page at 390 px: computed columns '351px', search 20-371, `.guide-view` 207-371 (inside the viewport), document overflow 0 with reduced motion, and a screenshot shows search, chips and the List/Map toggle fully visible. Verifier on the fix: Applied as task F0-T1: one declaration plus a unit test that pins it (red run: 1 failed; green: 1 passed).
- Fix risk: Low: the grid keeps one column, and from 768 px the auto track already stretched to the container, so the desktop layout does not change. Check 360-768 px in both motion modes and both locales (chip scroller still scrolls inside its box); jsdom cannot lay this out, so cover it in the browser audit (npm run audit:responsive:ux) and run that audit with prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, because overflow-x: clip hides this class of defect in full motion.
- Found by: R5-U11 (W2a); candidate D-010
- Resolution: FIXED by fast-track task F0-T1 (batch F0B1, the lead reproduced the defect and measured the fix in Chrome before the verifier round; patch .runtime/review-patches/R5-F0-T1.patch, test tests/unit/guide-filters-css.test.ts with a saved red and green run). Not yet committed.

### R-628: The worker stores a page only when it is loaded by a full navigation: pages the guest opens by tapping Next links are never stored, so most visited pages are missing offline although the offline page says 'Pages you opened before are still here'
- Severity: Medium
- Category: Logic
- Status: CONFIRMED
- Location: public/sw.js:L197-L200
- Evidence:
  ```
  if (request.mode === 'navigate') {
      event.respondWith(networkFirstPage(request, url.pathname));
      return;
    }
  ```
  Independent verifier (W1b): Read public/sw.js L190-210: the only branch that stores HTML is `if (request.mode === 'navigate') { event.respondWith(networkFirstPage(request, url.pathname)); return; }`; every other non-asset request falls through with no respondWith. Real Chromium 25.12 puppeteer against http://localhost:3000, real public/sw.js registered as /sw.js?v=0.1.1&build=probe-a (PwaManager's dev-only unregister/cache-delete neutralised in the page; offline emulated on page and worker target like scripts/smoke-production-image.ts): (1) after full load of /en/stay the cache pages were [/offline,/el/offline,/en/offline,/en/stay]. (2) header link click to /en/moments and then a place link were soft navigations (window marker survived: 'alive'); the page requests were `GET /en/moments?_rsc=... nav:false rsc:1` and `GET /en/moments/viktoria-karelia-greek-costumes-collection?_rsc=... nav:false rsc:1`; cache pages unchanged after both. (3) offline: /en/stay -> 200 'Welcome home.', /en/moments -> 200 "You're offline", the place page -> 200 "You're offline". (4) after one online FULL load of the place page it was stored and offline showed 'Viktoria Karelia Greek Costumes Collection'. Copy it contradicts: src/i18n/domains/stay.ts L103 lead 'Pages you opened before are still here.' and tip 'open the pages you need while you are online'; legal.ts L228 'the public pages you visited'. All site links are next/link (the header and place links produced _rsc fetches). Existing tests only use mode:'navigate' (tests/unit/service-worker.test.ts) and page.goto in the smoke, so no gate sees it. Vary header of a public page is 'rsc, next-router-state-tree, next-router-prefetch, next-router-segment-prefetch, Accept-Encoding' (no Accept), so a worker-made synthetic Request would still match a later navigation. Not [...]
  Refuter (REF-UI): not refuted, survives as CONFIRMED; severity Medium. No refutation; I reproduced it independently and then attacked the impact. Real Chromium (puppeteer 25.12.0) against http://localhost:3000 with the real public/sw.js registered as /sw.js?v=0.1.1&build=refute-ui, dev-only unregister/cache-delete neutralised in the page, offline emulated on the page and on the worker target (scratchpad review5/REF-UI/b010.cjs). (1) after the full load of /en/stay the cache pages are [/offline, /el/offline, /en/offline, /en/stay]. (2) The header or stay-hub next/link to /en/phones was a soft navigation (window marker survived); the page requested 'GET /en/phones?_rsc=bR_FSF nav=false rsc=1'; a fetch listener I injected in the worker target saw it as mode 'cors' (log: 'cors /en/phones?_rsc=bR_F'), so the worker's request.mode === 'navigate' branch (public/sw.js L197-200) never runs and no respondWith/cache.put happens; cache pages unchanged. (3) offline: [...] On the fix: The CACHE_PAGE message fix is workable and I verified its key premise: from the worker target I fetched new Request('/en/phones') (type basic, ok, not redirected, Vary 'rsc, next-router-state-tree, next-router-prefetch, next-router-segment-prefetch, Accept-Encoding'), put it under the URL, went offline and a full navigation to /en/phones then returned 'Important phones' (Vary does not block the match). Additions to the fixRisk: (1) PwaManager is not mounted directly: DeferredRuntimeManagers imports it after scheduleIdle (src/components/DeferredRuntimeManagers.tsx), so 'skip the first run' of [...]
- Problem: HTML is written to the cache only in networkFirstPage, which runs only for request.mode === 'navigate'. The site's own links are next/link (SiteHeader, guide cards), so a tap is a client-side navigation: Next fetches an RSC payload (?_rsc=, mode cors) which the fetch handler ignores (no respondWith; the RSC response is not stored either). Evidence (real Chromium against the dev server with the real public/sw.js; offline emulated on the page and on the worker target as scripts/smoke-production-image.ts does; PwaManager's dev-only unregister/cache-delete disabled in the page so the worker can be observed; scratch script browser-softnav3.cjs): (1) full load of /en/stay -> pages in cache ["/el/offline","/en/offline","/en/stay"]; (2) two soft navigations in the same document (a window marker survived) to /en/moments and /en/moments/viktoria-karelia-greek-costumes-collection -> pages in cache unchanged; (3) a full reload of the place page -> it is now stored; (4) offline: /en/stay -> 200 "Welcome home.", /en/moments -> 200 "You're offline", the place page -> its content (only because of the reload in 3). The offline path itself behaves as designed: tapping a link to a cached page falls back to a full navigation and the worker answers (/phones loaded earlier -> "Important phones"; unvisited /moments -> offline page). The copy promises more: src/i18n/domains/stay.ts L103 lead "Pages you opened before are still here." and the tip "open the pages you need while you are online, so they are ready later"; the privacy notice (src/i18n/domains/legal.ts L228) says the public pages you visited are kept.
- Impact: A guest scans the QR code (/en/stay, a full load), opens the Kalamata guide and a place by tapping, then loses data. /en/stay opens offline, but the guide and the place show "You're offline" although the guest opened them minutes earlier. Only entry pages (QR landing, reload, typed or shared URL) are kept. The 5xx stand-in of R-425 has the same gap. tests/unit/service-worker.test.ts (mode: 'navigate' requests only) and the smoke step 'offline: visited page' (page.goto) use full navigations, so no gate can see this.
- Fix: Store the page the guest lands on after a client-side route change. PwaManager (mounted in the locale layout, so it survives soft navigations) posts { type: 'CACHE_PAGE', url: location.href } to navigator.serviceWorker.controller from a usePathname() effect (skip the first run). In sw.js's message handler: `if (event.data.type === 'CACHE_PAGE') event.waitUntil(storePage(event.data.url));` where storePage requires the same origin, not /api/, !isNetworkOnlyPage(pathname), then `const r = await fetchInternal(new Request(url.href)).catch(() => undefined); if (isStorable(r)) await (await caches.open(CACHE_NAME)).put(url.href, r);`. Alternative if the owner prefers no extra requests: change the offline copy and the notice to say that only pages opened by a full page load are kept. Verifier on the fix: The CACHE_PAGE message fix is workable: PwaManager is mounted in the locale layout and survives soft navigations, and a worker-side storePage with the same-origin, /api/ and isNetworkOnlyPage guards plus isStorable reuses the existing rules (the cached copy keeps its own CSP header/nonce, Vary has no Accept so match works). It touches PwaManager.tsx, sw.js, two test files and the smoke, so it is more than a one-liner; the fixRisk (one extra ~50 KB request per route change, URL taken from page script so keep the guards) is fair. The alternative 'change the copy' includes legal.ts, which [...]
- Fix risk: One extra HTML request (about 50 KB) per route change on mobile data (consider requestIdleCallback and navigator.connection.saveData). The message handler takes a URL from page script, so keep the same-origin and network-only guards in the worker. The worker's fetch carries cookies like a navigation to the same URL, so the lang cookie cannot flip. Needs new cases in tests/unit/service-worker.test.ts and tests/components/pwa-manager.test.tsx and a smoke step that soft-navigates, goes offline and reopens the page.
- Found by: R5-U16 (W1b); candidate B-010
- Resolution: FIXED by T-F02 (batch B1, 2026-10-13): PwaManager posts CACHE_PAGE (URL without hash) on every pathname change after mount, on mount when the URL differs from the document's navigation entry, and once after controllerchange when the page loaded uncontrolled; the worker stores the page only if same-origin, not /api/, not network-only, not an offline page and the answer isStorable. Evidence: RED 7 failed / 36 passed (fix/logs/T-F02-red.log), GREEN 43/43; lead check in real Chromium against the production standalone build (fix/logs/B1-lead-sw-prod.log): /en/phones, /en/moments and a place page are stored after soft navigations and open offline with their own h1; no /api/ or private entry; B1 verifier PASS-WITH-NOTES (mutants of every guard killed; one survivor, R-793). Patch R5-T-F02.patch. Note: the dev server does not exercise the new code (the effects are production-only); the check ran on `.next/standalone`.

### R-629: Horizontal-overflow metric is blind on every phone preset: the reference width is window.innerWidth, which Chrome mobile emulation grows to the content width
- Severity: Medium
- Category: Bug
- Status: CONFIRMED
- Location: scripts/responsive-ux-audit.ts:L525-L526
- Evidence:
  ```
  const docWidth = Math.max((root && root.scrollWidth) || 0, (body && body.scrollWidth) || 0);
        const viewportWidth = window.innerWidth;
  ```
  Independent verifier (W34): Code: scripts/responsive-ux-audit.ts:525-526 `const docWidth = Math.max(root.scrollWidth, body.scrollWidth); const viewportWidth = window.innerWidth;`; phone presets at lines 143-231 all have isMobile: true (5 presets: 320, 360, 390, 414, 768). Executed on the REAL pages (Puppeteer 25.12.0, Node 22.19.0, localhost:3000, the audit's own collectMetrics script string extracted from the file and evaluated). Real page meta is `width=device-width, initial-scale=1`. (1) /en, 390x844 isMobile, probe div 900px wide appended to body: `inner:900, client:390, rootScroll:900` -> metrics horizontalOverflowPx=0 (should be 510). Same page with isMobile:false: `inner:390, rootScroll:900` -> horizontalOverflowPx=510. (2) Real defect reproduced by re-adding the pre-fix rule `.guide-filters{grid-template-columns:none}` on /en/moments at 390 px, reduced motion, isMobile: `inner:652, client:390, rootScroll:652` -> horizontalOverflowPx=0; isMobile:false gives 262 (matches the 262 px the lead recorded for R5-F0). (3) Replacing only the reference with `root.clientWidth`: mobile+reduced gives 262, body probe gives 510; clean pages stay 0. Corroboration from the repo's own stored reports (reports/responsive-ux/*.json): the only cells with horizontalOverflowPx>0 ever are desktop-1024x768 (22 and 61 px, run 2026-10-05); no phone cell in any of 4 reports. Nuance: the audit never emulates reduced motion, so in a default run data-motion=full and `.site-main{overflow-x:clip}` (motion.css:535) already keeps scrollWidth at 390 for anything inside main; the practical gain of this fix alone is overflow outside main (header/footer/overlays) and reduced-motion runs. The element scan (line 534) uses the same innerWidth, so it is blind in the same way.
  Refuter (REF-TOOLING): not refuted, survives as CONFIRMED; severity Medium. No refutation. I extracted the audit's own script string from scripts/responsive-ux-audit.ts (collectMetrics, lines 502-612) and ran it unchanged against the real dev server (Puppeteer 25.12.0, Node 22.19.0, localhost:3000, page meta 'width=device-width, initial-scale=1'). 390x844, isMobile:true, probe div 900px wide appended to body: {inner:900, vv:390, client:390, rootScroll:900} -> original horizontalOverflowPx=0, with 'const viewportWidth = root.clientWidth' -> 510. Same page isMobile:false: inner 390 -> original 510. Real defect re-created by injecting the pre-fix rule '.guide-filters{grid-template-columns:none !important}' on /en/moments, mobile + prefers-reduced-motion:reduce: {inner:652, client:390, rootScroll:652} -> original overflow 0 AND overflowingElementCount 0 (the element scan is blind too), clientWidth variant 262 (the same 262 px recorded for R5-F0 in PROGRESS.md:302) [...] On the fix: Correct and minimal: replacing window.innerWidth by root.clientWidth (line 526) gave the right value in every combination I ran (clientWidth stayed 390 while innerWidth grew to 652 or 900; headless Puppeteer hides scrollbars so no desktop false positive). Fix risk is fair; add that the same change also repairs the per-element scan (line 534), and that phone cells will start reporting overflow outside main or in reduced motion, so the 81-cell baseline must be re-taken. Schedule together with H-002 and H-004 (same function, interdependent).
- Problem: collectMetrics computes horizontalOverflowPx as docWidth - window.innerWidth, and the per-element edge scan also compares against window.innerWidth. All five phone presets use isMobile: true, and the site emits `<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">` (Next default; read in .next/server/app/_global-error.html and node_modules/next/dist/lib/metadata/default-metadata.js:27; src/app/layout.tsx only sets themeColor). With that meta, Chrome mobile emulation widens the layout viewport to fit overflowing content, so innerWidth equals the content width and the overflow is 0. Executed evidence: I copied the repo's own collectMetrics/evaluateIssues unchanged into a scratch file and ran it in Puppeteer 25.12.0 headless Chrome (Node 22.19.0) on a synthetic page (360 px viewport, isMobile true, same meta, a 900 px wide grid child, no clip). Output: `{"inner":900,"vv":360,"root":900,"body":900,"client":360} overflowPx= 0 elements= 0`. With non-mobile emulation, or with minimum-scale=1, the same page gives overflowPx= 540. After changing only the reference to root.clientWidth: `overflowPx= 540 elements= 7`.
- Impact: Visible horizontal overflow on the phone presets (320, 360, 390, 414, 768 px) is reported as 0 whenever main is not clipped (reduced motion, or any overflow from header/footer outside .site-main). Together with .site-main { overflow-x: clip } in full motion (src/styles/motion.css:535), which keeps innerWidth at 360 and scrollWidth at 360, the audit has no way to report the class of defect it exists for (the guide List/Map toggle pushed off a phone screen, R5-F0). I did not run the real site: the mechanism is proven on a page with the same viewport meta, not on the production pages.
- Fix: In the evaluated script use the layout width of the root element instead of innerWidth: replace `const viewportWidth = window.innerWidth;` by `const viewportWidth = root.clientWidth;` (clientWidth stayed 360 in all 8 combinations I ran). Verifier on the fix: Correct: `const viewportWidth = root.clientWidth;` gave the right value in every combination I ran (390 stays 390; 510 and 262 are detected). Fix risk is fair. Add one sentence: after the change phone cells with overflow outside main can turn minor/major; and because the audit runs in full motion (clip), H-002 is needed for the main-content case, so schedule H-001 and H-002 together.
- Fix risk: clientWidth excludes a classic vertical scrollbar on desktop presets, but scrollWidth equals clientWidth when nothing overflows, so no false positive is expected there. Hidden minor overflows may appear on phones after the change; re-run the audit and re-baseline the 81-cell summary.
- Found by: R5-U27 (W34); candidate H-001
- Resolution: FIXED by T-F03 (batch B1, 2026-10-13): the horizontal-overflow metric measures against documentElement.clientWidth (not window.innerWidth), and the element-edge scan is turned into issues. Evidence: jsdom harness RED 14/27, GREEN 27/27 (fix/logs/T-F03-red.log, T-F03-green.log); lead fault probe in real Chrome on a loopback fixture (main.site-main with overflow-x: clip and a 900 px child): MAJOR 'element_beyond_viewport' (div.wide), the clean fixture PASS; B1 verifier PASS. Patch R5-T-F03.patch.

### R-632: Orchestrator migrates the database named by DIRECT_URL, not the one it checked or switched to (prisma.config.ts prefers DIRECT_URL)
- Severity: Medium
- Category: Bug
- Status: CONFIRMED
- Location: scripts/system-orchestrator.sh:L488-L499
- Evidence:
  `flock -x "$MIGRATION_LOCK_FILE" bash -lc "cd '$REPO_ROOT' && npm run prisma:migrate:deploy"`
  Independent verifier (W34): prisma.config.ts:17 `const datasourceUrl = process.env.DIRECT_URL ?? process.env.DATABASE_URL;`. `grep -c DIRECT_URL scripts/system-orchestrator.sh` = 0. run_migration_once (L488-499) runs `npm run prisma:migrate:deploy` (package.json:14 `prisma migrate deploy`) after prepare_database, which decides only on DATABASE_URL (L396-425; fallback `export DATABASE_URL="$DB_LOCAL_URL"` at L391); load_environment (L262-285) exports every dotenv key, and inherited shell variables pass through. cmd_up, cmd_bootstrap and cmd_migrate (so system:up, system:bootstrap, system:migrate, db:migrate) all reach run_migrations_with_retry. Executed in a scratch copy of prisma.config.ts and schema (Node 22.19.0, prisma 7.10.0, CHECKPOINT_DISABLE=1, closed loopback ports): DATABASE_URL=...127.0.0.1:2/database_marker plus DIRECT_URL=...127.0.0.1:1/direct_marker printed `Datasource "db": PostgreSQL database "direct_marker", schema "public" at "127.0.0.1:1"` and `P1001 ... 127.0.0.1:1`; with DATABASE_URL only it printed `database_marker ... 127.0.0.1:2`. .env.example:7 documents DIRECT_URL as supported; docs/testing.md:62 and scripts/verify-release.mjs:97 show the repo already treats an inherited DIRECT_URL as hazardous. No existing REVIEW.md finding covers it (R-477 cites the orchestrator lines for the upgrade-path documentation only).
  Refuter (REF-TOOLING): not refuted, survives as CONFIRMED; severity Medium. No refutation of the mechanism. Re-executed in a scratch copy of prisma.config.ts + schema (Node 22.19.0, prisma from the repo's node_modules, CHECKPOINT_DISABLE=1, closed loopback ports only, scratch cwd so no repo .env file was read): DATABASE_URL=...127.0.0.1:2/database_marker plus DIRECT_URL=...127.0.0.1:1/direct_marker printed 'Datasource "db": PostgreSQL database "direct_marker" ... at "127.0.0.1:1"' and 'Error: P1001'; DATABASE_URL only printed 'database_marker ... 127.0.0.1:2'. prisma.config.ts:17 is 'process.env.DIRECT_URL ?? process.env.DATABASE_URL'. grep for DIRECT_URL in the repo (excluding node_modules, .runtime, REVIEW/PROGRESS): only prisma.config.ts, .env.example:7, docs/testing.md:62, test/gate scripts; none in scripts/system-orchestrator.sh. Flow verified: cmd_up/cmd_bootstrap/cmd_migrate -> run_preflight (load_environment exports every key of the four dotenv files, [...] On the fix: Primary fix is correct in substance: compare in the shell after prepare_database (so the Docker-fallback switch is already applied) and die with code 14 when DIRECT_URL is non-empty and differs from DATABASE_URL. Place it after the SKIP_MIGRATE early return in run_migrations_with_retry (otherwise 'up --skip-migrate' and db:start would be rejected without migrating). Drop the 'unset DIRECT_URL' alternative (proved ineffective, prisma.config.ts reloads it from .env.local/.env). Fix risk: also blocks a deliberate setup with a pooled DATABASE_URL and a direct DIRECT_URL to the same dev database, [...]
- Problem: Every reachability, mode and fallback decision of the script is made on DATABASE_URL only (validate_database_url L303-311, prepare_database L396-425, start_fallback_database L391 `export DATABASE_URL="$DB_LOCAL_URL"`). The migration step then runs `npm run prisma:migrate:deploy`, and prisma.config.ts:17 reads `const datasourceUrl = process.env.DIRECT_URL ?? process.env.DATABASE_URL;`. `grep -n DIRECT_URL scripts/system-orchestrator.sh` finds nothing, so nothing unsets, compares or reports DIRECT_URL. load_environment (L262-285) exports every key of the four dotenv files, and inherited shell variables are kept, so a DIRECT_URL from the shell, .env.local or .env reaches Prisma. .env.example:7 documents DIRECT_URL as a supported optional variable. Execution proof (scratch copy of prisma.config.ts + schema, Node 22.19.0, CHECKPOINT_DISABLE=1, closed loopback ports only): with DATABASE_URL=postgresql://a:a@127.0.0.1:2/database_marker and DIRECT_URL=postgresql://d:d@127.0.0.1:1/direct_marker, `prisma migrate deploy` printed `Datasource "db": PostgreSQL database "direct_marker", schema "public" at "127.0.0.1:1"` / `Error: P1001: Can't reach database server at `127.0.0.1:1``; with only DATABASE_URL set it targeted `database_marker` at 127.0.0.1:2. The repo already treats this variable as hazardous elsewhere: scripts/verify-release.mjs:97 injects a hostile DIRECT_URL and docs/testing.md:62 says the integration config 'cannot prefer an inherited DIRECT_URL'.
- Impact: A developer who has DIRECT_URL set (for example exported for another Prisma project, or kept in .env for a hosted database) runs `npm run system:up`, `system:migrate`, `db:migrate` or `system:bootstrap`. The log says `DATABASE_URL is reachable (local)` (or the script switches to the local Docker fallback), yet `migrate deploy` is applied to the DIRECT_URL database, which can be a remote or non-dev database. The release migrations include guarded destructive steps (column and table drops; scripts/README.md L235-L252). When the script fell back to Docker, the app (DATABASE_URL, local) and the migrated database (DIRECT_URL) also differ, so /api/health/ready fails with a confusing 'migration not applied'.
- Fix: Before the migration step (start of run_migrations_with_retry, after prepare_database so the fallback switch is already applied) refuse a divergent DIRECT_URL: + if [[ -n "${DIRECT_URL:-}" && "${DIRECT_URL}" != "${DATABASE_URL}" ]]; then + die "DIRECT_URL is set and differs from DATABASE_URL; prisma migrate deploy would use DIRECT_URL. Unset it for local development." 14 + fi Alternative: in DB_MODE=local, `unset DIRECT_URL`. Verifier on the fix: Correct in substance (die when DIRECT_URL is non-empty and differs from DATABASE_URL, after prepare_database so the fallback switch is applied). Place the check AFTER the SKIP_MIGRATE early return in run_migrations_with_retry; at the very start it would also reject `up --skip-migrate` although no migration runs. Fix risk is fair: a developer who deliberately keeps a separate non-pooled DIRECT_URL must unset it for orchestrator runs. Severity Medium is acceptable (dev-only, needs DIRECT_URL set, but a guarded-destructive migration chain would hit an unintended database).
- Fix risk: A developer who deliberately uses a separate non-pooled DIRECT_URL with a managed development database must unset it for orchestrator runs (or the alternative must be limited to DB_MODE=local). Test `system:migrate` with DIRECT_URL unset, equal and different (use closed loopback ports; no real database needed).
- Found by: R5-U26 (W34); candidate H-012
- Resolution: FIXED by T-F01 (batch B1, 2026-10-13): after the SKIP_MIGRATE return, run_migrations_with_retry exits 14 when DIRECT_URL is non-empty and differs from DATABASE_URL, naming the rule; up/bootstrap --skip-migrate still pass. Evidence: scratch probe with stub docker/npm/curl and a fake .env.local, RED 16 pass / 21 fail on the HEAD copy (fix/logs/T-F01-red.log), GREEN 37/37 (T-F01-green.log), re-run by the lead and by the B1 verifier on the repo script (sha256 6e9cb97c): 37/37; patch .runtime/review-patches/R5-T-F01.patch. Residue found while fixing: R-790 (an env-file key can flip the opt-in variable), R-791 (db:studio and db:generate do not reach the guard).

### R-634: A nested .DS_Store in public/ is not excluded from the Docker context, ships in the runner image and is served
- Severity: Low
- Category: Security
- Status: CONFIRMED
- Location: .dockerignore:L27-L28
- Evidence:
  ```
  *.log
  .DS_Store
  ```
  Independent verifier (W2): .dockerignore:28 is a bare `.DS_Store`. Docker docs (https://docs.docker.com/build/concepts/context/): '*.md' excludes files 'right under the context directory ... Note that markdown files under subdirectories are still included', and only `**/` reaches any depth ('**/*.go excludes all files that end with .go found anywhere'). moby/patternmatcher (fetched, main): non-wildcard patterns are compiled as exactMatch and compared by `return path == p.cleanedPattern, nil`; the parent-path loop only tests the first len(pattern.dirs) directories of the parent, so a root-name pattern does not match public/house/.DS_Store. .gitignore:27 has `.DS_Store` (any depth), so git status and the `-dirty` suffix of scripts/image-tag.sh (`git status --porcelain`) never see a nested one. scripts/docker-build.sh builds with context `.`; docker/Dockerfile.security L23 `COPY . .` and L125 `COPY --from=builder ... /app/public ./public` ship all of public/. I ran Next's own recursiveReadDir (node_modules/next/dist/lib/recursive-readdir.js, as used at router-utils/filesystem.js L195) on a scratch public dir: ['/house/.DS_Store','/house/a.jpg'], so the file would be a served public item. src/proxy.ts L145 matcher `/((?!_next|.*\..*).*)` skips dotted paths, and scripts/lib/release-policy.mjs L767-771 checks only the three root .env lines. `find public -name '.*'` is empty at HEAD (only ./.DS_Store at the repo root, which the root rule excludes), so nothing is exposed today. R-493 (FIXED) concerned .env/*.pem and R-574 concerns legacy entries; neither mentions .DS_Store.
- Problem: .dockerignore:28 lists .DS_Store without '**/'. BuildKit's pattern matcher (moby/patternmatcher) compares a pattern without wildcards by exact equality with the whole relative path ('exactMatch: path == p.cleanedPattern'), so only a root-level .DS_Store is excluded and 'public/house/.DS_Store' is not (docs.docker.com/build/concepts/context says the same for '*.md': files under subdirectories are still included). .gitignore:27 ignores .DS_Store at every depth, so git status, the '-dirty' suffix of scripts/image-tag.sh and the source secret scan never see a nested one. docker/Dockerfile.security:23 'COPY . .' sends it to the builder and docker/Dockerfile.security:125 'COPY --from=builder ... /app/public ./public' ships all of public/ into the runner image. The installed Next 16.3.8 lists every file below public/ with no dotfile filter (node_modules/next/dist/server/lib/router-utils/filesystem.js:195 recursiveReadDir(publicFolderPath), default options); I ran that function on a scratch directory and it printed: public items as Next lists them (default options, as in filesystem.js:195): ['/house/.DS_Store','/house/a.jpg']. The matcher in src/proxy.ts:145 skips every path that contains a dot, deploy/nginx/nginx.conf.template has one 'location /' and no dotfile deny, scripts/check-image-assets.ts inspects only raster files and ENV_FILE_PATTERN in check-secrets.mjs names only .env, so no gate sees such a file. R-493's fix made .env and *.pem any-depth but left this third any-depth .gitignore entry root-only. `find public -name '.*'` finds nothing at HEAD, so nothing is exposed today. The Docker rule rests on the Docker docs and the matcher source (docker not run).
- Impact: The owner works on macOS and keeps adding photos below public/house/ (public/house/parking/ is new and untracked). Opening such a folder in Finder creates a .DS_Store there; the next `npm run docker:build` bakes it into the runner image and `/house/.DS_Store` can be downloaded by anyone. It lists the file names of that folder, including files already deleted (for example original IMG_* camera names). Information disclosure only, no credential, but invisible to git and to every release gate.
- Fix: Add `**/.DS_Store` to .dockerignore next to the existing root line (the root line may stay). Verifier on the fix: Adding `**/.DS_Store` next to the existing line is correct and minimal (the docs say `**/` also matches at depth zero, so the root line may stay). Fix risk is fair: the file is never needed in a build, and validate:release-policy only regex-checks `.env`, `.env.*` and `!.env.example`. I did not run docker build; the matching rule rests on the Docker docs and the patternmatcher source quoted above.
- Fix risk: None for the build, the file is never needed. Run `npm run validate:release-policy`; it only looks at the three root .env lines.
- Found by: R5-U18 (W2); candidate D-017
- Resolution: FIXED by T-F19 (batch B4, 2026-10-13): `**/.DS_Store` is excluded from the Docker context in .dockerignore, so a nested public/.DS_Store no longer ships in the runner image. The policy does not pin this line (deleting it in a tidy-up would reopen the finding without a failing gate); decision D13 asked for the line only.
