Evidence as R-658. `**/.DS_Store` is added to .dockerignore (R-634) but not pinned by the policy (decision D13 asked for the line only).

### R-636: Dev DB healthcheck uses pg_isready on the unix socket, which can pass during first-start initialisation; the orchestrator then probes TCP once and aborts
- Severity: Low
- Category: Bug
- Status: CONFIRMED
- Location: docker-compose.yml:L13-L17
- Evidence:
  `test: ["CMD-SHELL", "pg_isready -U ${POSTGRES_USER:-devuser} -d ${POSTGRES_DB:-site_dev}"]`
  Independent verifier (W34): LEAD REPRODUCTION (2026-10-13, executed by the lead on a throwaway container from the local postgres:16-alpine image, no network, script .runtime/review5/w0/health-probe2.sh): sampling every 50 ms inside the container during its first start gave 9 samples socket=no tcp=no, then 2 samples socket=yes tcp=no (the entrypoint's temporary server listens on the unix socket only), then 2 samples socket=no tcp=no (the restart gap), then 187 samples socket=yes tcp=yes. So a health command that asks over the unix socket can report ready before the real server accepts TCP connections. The window is about 0.1-0.25 s wide: a first run with the real health command at a 1 s interval (.runtime/review5/w0/health-probe.sh) saw health turn healthy together with TCP, so the effect is a rare flake, not a constant failure. Verifier: Verified from the repo: docker-compose.yml:13-17 healthcheck `pg_isready -U ${POSTGRES_USER:-devuser} -d ${POSTGRES_DB:-site_dev}` (no -h), interval 5s, no start_period; the image is postgres:16-alpine pinned by digest sha256:721873c3...6080ea; wait_for_container_ready (L357-379) accepts `healthy`; prepare_database then makes exactly one database_reachable TCP probe (L421-423, connectionTimeoutMillis 3000, no retry) and dies 17 on failure. docker/docker-compose.prod.yml:42 and tests/integration/support/database-lifecycle.ts:234 use the same no -h pattern (the lifecycle uses a 1 s interval). The central premise, that the official image's first-start init server listens only on the unix socket (`listen_addresses=''`) while pg_isready without -h probes that socket, is not in the repo and cannot be read from node_modules; I did not fetch it (no network in this round) and cannot run Docker, so the race is unproven. Circumstantial: the production-image smoke runs fresh [...]
- Problem: pg_isready is called without -h, so it checks the default unix socket. The official image's docker_temp_server_start (docker-library/postgres docker-entrypoint.sh, fetched from raw.githubusercontent.com) starts the initialisation server with `-c listen_addresses=''` ('does not listen on external TCP/IP'), reachable only through that socket, so on an empty volume the container can turn healthy before the real server listens on TCP. wait_for_container_ready (orchestrator L357-379) accepts healthy, then L421-423 performs one database_reachable probe over TCP (3 s timeout, no retry) and dies with 'Fallback database started but DATABASE_URL is still unreachable' (exit 17). docker/docker-compose.prod.yml:42 and tests/integration/support/database-lifecycle.ts:234 use the same pg_isready pattern without -h.
- Impact: First `npm run system:up` after the volume was created or removed may fail with exit 17 while the database finishes initialising; a second run works. Same pattern in the production compose could let `up -d --wait db` return before TCP is available on the very first deploy (not analysed here, other unit).
- Fix: Make the healthcheck test the TCP listener: `pg_isready -h 127.0.0.1 -U ... -d ...` (same in docker/docker-compose.prod.yml, which needs release-policy fixtures updated), and/or retry database_reachable a few times after the container is healthy. Verifier on the fix: Both proposed remedies are sound if the race is real: `pg_isready -h 127.0.0.1` in the healthcheck and/or a short retry loop around the post-healthy database_reachable probe (the retry is the smaller, lower-risk change and is confined to the dev script). Touching docker/docker-compose.prod.yml means release-policy fixtures and `validate:release-policy` / `test:release-policy`, so keep the prod compose out of the first task. Decide only after the probe below.
- Fix risk: docker-compose files are read by scripts/lib/release-policy.mjs and fixtures; run validate:release-policy and test:release-policy after any compose change.
- Found by: R5-U26 (W34); candidate H-021
- Resolution: FIXED by T-F11 (batch B2, 2026-10-13): docker-compose.yml's dev database healthcheck is `pg_isready -h 127.0.0.1 -U ... -d ...` (TCP, not the unix socket). Evidence: lead throwaway-container probe on the digest-pinned image (fix/logs/B2-lead-health-probe.log): 3 samples (150 ms) with the old socket form ready while TCP was closed, the new healthcheck says ready only from the sample where TCP is open (222 samples), never before; static RED/GREEN logs T-F11-red.log/green.log; B2 verifier PASS. docker/docker-compose.prod.yml and the integration harness keep the old form as decided (D13); R-727 covers the harness (T-F37).

### R-637: docker-compose.prod.yml sets no log rotation for the long-running web and db containers; Docker's default json-file driver keeps logs without a size limit
- Severity: Low
- Category: Performance
- Status: SUSPECTED
- Location: docker/docker-compose.prod.yml:L47-L49
- Evidence:
  ```
  web:
      <<: *hardened
      image: ${APP_IMAGE:?APP_IMAGE is required (npm run docker:build prints it)}
  ```
  Independent verifier (W2): docker/docker-compose.prod.yml has no `logging:` key: db (L25-45), web (L47-60) and the x-hardened anchor (L15-22) have none; `git grep -i -E 'max-size|json-file|log-opt|daemon.json|logging:' -- docs scripts docker deploy README.md` returns nothing, and docs/architecture/deployment-target.md and scripts/README.md never mention container logs. Docker docs (https://docs.docker.com/engine/logging/drivers/json-file/, fetched): max-size 'Defaults to -1 (unlimited)', max-file 'Defaults to 1', 'Only effective when max-size is also set'. The app logs to stdout by default (src/lib/logger-enterprise.ts L80-82: production level 'info', enableConsole unless LOG_CONSOLE=false) and web has `restart: unless-stopped`. The only log-rotation finding on record, R-503, concerns the Nginx container (the runbook now has a logrotate rule for error.log), not web/db. What I cannot see is the host's /etc/docker/daemon.json, which could set log-opts globally, hence SUSPECTED.
- Problem: Neither web (lines 47-60) nor db (lines 25-45) has a `logging:` key, and the shared `x-hardened` anchor (lines 15-22) has none either. `git grep -n -i -E 'max-size|json-file|log-opt|daemon.json'` over docs, scripts/README.md, docker and deploy finds no daemon-level setting either (the only rotation guidance is for the Nginx files in docs/deployment/origin-ingress-runbook.md, which says access.log still 'needs its own rotation rule before go-live'). The application logs to stdout by default (src/lib/logger-enterprise.ts: enableConsole is true unless LOG_CONSOLE=false) and the web container is long-running (restart: unless-stopped). From the Docker documentation as I remember it, the json-file driver has max-size -1 (unlimited) unless the daemon is configured; I could not check that offline.
- Impact: Client-triggerable error/warn lines (apiErrorHandler, rate-limit, readiness warnings) and the Postgres log accumulate in /var/lib/docker/containers/<id>/<id>-json.log until the container is recreated; on a small VPS this can fill the disk. The privacy notice in src/i18n/domains/legal.ts states a 14-day retention only for the web server's error log, so application logs have no stated retention either.
- Fix: Add one shared logging anchor and use it for web and db, for example `x-logging: &logging { driver: json-file, options: { max-size: "10m", max-file: "5" } }` and `logging: *logging` in both services, or document the equivalent /etc/docker/daemon.json setting in scripts/README.md 'Host layout'. This is an operations decision (retention), so it goes to the decision agent/owner. Verifier on the fix: Adding a shared `x-logging` anchor with json-file max-size/max-file to web and db (or documenting the daemon.json setting) is a correct minimal change; it is an operations/retention decision for the decision agent or owner. Fix risk is fair; scripts/lib/release-policy.mjs only inspects published ports and a few markers of the prod compose file, so a new key does not trip it. Rotation shortens how long `docker logs` can be inspected after an incident.
- Fix risk: Run `npm run validate:release-policy` and `npm run test:release-policy` (compose structure checks), and `docker compose -f docker/docker-compose.prod.yml --profile ops config -q` via the smoke. Rotation also shortens how long `docker logs` can be inspected after an incident.
- To confirm: On the VPS: `docker info --format '{{.LoggingDriver}}'` and the log-opts in /etc/docker/daemon.json, then `docker inspect <web> --format '{{.HostConfig.LogConfig}}'` (an empty Config map means unlimited). Run request: On the production host (owner): docker info --format '{{.LoggingDriver}}'; cat /etc/docker/daemon.json; docker inspect <web-container> --format '{{json .HostConfig.LogConfig}}'
- Found by: R5-U19 (W2); candidate D-008
- Resolution: DEFERRED-OWNER (decision D13): On the production host, run docker info --format '{{.LoggingDriver}}', read the log-opts in /etc/docker/daemon.json, and run docker inspect <web container> --format '{{json .HostConfig.LogConfig}}'. If nothing rotates, choose json-file max-size and max-file (for example 10m x 5), either as an x-logging anchor for web and db in docker/docker-compose.prod.yml or in daemon.json, together with the retention that implies. If no answer: No repository change; the item stays under 'Needs the production host or database'.

### R-643: layered-rate-limiting.md promises 'bounded route/status counters' for admin login; no counter exists at HEAD

### R-644: Secret-scanner lock supports only darwin-arm64, but the release docs never say so; verify:release gate 1 throws on any other platform
- Severity: Low
- Category: Maintainability
- Status: CONFIRMED
- Location: docs/security/secret-scanning.md:L28-L30
- Evidence:
  ```
  The gate uses Gitleaks 8.30.1. Download the exact official release artifact
  listed in `config/secret-scanning/tool.lock.json`, verify the upstream checksum
  file and archive hashes, extract it into a user-protected directory, and set:
  ```
  Independent verifier (W34): config/secret-scanning/tool.lock.json: `node -e` printed top-level keys [schemaVersion,name,version,releaseUrl,checksumsUrl,checksumsFileSha256,artifacts] and artifacts keys ['darwin-arm64'] only. scripts/check-secrets.mjs:L51-L52 `function platformKey() { return `${process.platform}-${process.arch}`; }`; L69-L74 `const artifact = lock.artifacts?.[platformKey()]; if (!artifact) { throw new Error(`No locked scanner artifact exists for ${platformKey()}.`); }`; L365-L366 verifyScanner(binaryPath) runs on every scan, and release-gates.mjs L58 and L98 make 'secret-sources' (gate 1) and 'secret-artifacts' (gate 25) call check:secrets:sources/artifacts. Docs: docs/security/secret-scanning.md:L28-L30 says 'Download the exact official release artifact listed in config/secret-scanning/tool.lock.json' with no platform statement; docs/release-verification.md:L18-L20 prerequisite says only 'the checksum-locked Gitleaks 8.30.1 binary selected through GITLEAKS_BIN'; grep -i 'darwin|arm64|Apple|macOS|platform' over secret-scanning.md, release-verification.md, scripts/README.md, README.md, CLAUDE.md finds no scanner-platform statement. The docs even suggest other hosts work: scripts/README.md:L8 'macOS or Linux shell' and release-verification.md:L21-L22 'Unix or Windows named-pipe socket'. Not in REVIEW.md (only R-5xx hit for 'darwin' is the license-check note at L6604, which states the release host is macOS arm64). On the owner's own host (darwin-arm64) the gate works, so the practical impact today is small.
- Problem: config/secret-scanning/tool.lock.json has `artifacts: { 'darwin-arm64': ... }` and no other entry (checked with `node -e`: keys = ['darwin-arm64'], 'linux-x64' and 'darwin-x64' undefined). scripts/check-secrets.mjs:51-52 and :69-74 build the key as `${process.platform}-${process.arch}` and throw `No locked scanner artifact exists for <key>.` when it is missing. verifyScanner runs on every scan (check-secrets.mjs:365-366), so gates 1 and 25 of verify:release fail on every other platform. Neither secret-scanning.md nor release-verification.md:18-20 (prerequisites) nor scripts/README.md mentions this. The documents speak of 'the' official release artifact as if it were platform-independent.
- Impact: The mandatory release gate can be run only on an Apple-silicon Mac. On an Intel Mac, a Linux release host (the ADR names a 'trusted release host' and the VPS runs Linux) or a Windows machine, an operator downloads a valid official Gitleaks archive, sets GITLEAKS_BIN, and the gate stops with an error that the docs do not explain. Adding the entries themselves needs the owner (download and hash of official artifacts) and is a separate task. Verifier on the fix: Correct: one sentence in secret-scanning.md plus the prerequisite bullet is the minimal change; adding linux/darwin-x64 lock entries is a separate owner task (official archive and binary hashes), as the finder says. fixRisk is fair; run npm run validate:release-policy once after editing, since release-policy pins parts of the secret-scanning setup.
- Fix risk: Documentation only for the sentence. Adding platform entries touches scripts/lib/release-policy.mjs expectations and the secret-scanning tests, so it needs its own task and a run of `npm run test:secret-scanning` with GITLEAKS_BIN set.
- Found by: R5-U29a (W34); candidate N-003
- Resolution: DEFERRED-OWNER: the documentation part (task T-F55) is not done (economy instruction of 2026-10-13); the owner part is the gitleaks tool lock, which holds darwin-arm64 only: if verify:release must run on another platform, download the official gitleaks 8.30.1 archive for it and approve adding its checksums to tool.lock.json as a separate task.

### R-647: Install accepts any failure of the offline pages and their scripts, and activation then deletes the previous complete cache: a flaky install leaves the build without an offline page and nothing retries
- Severity: Low
- Category: Error handling
- Status: CONFIRMED
- Location: public/sw.js:L117-L124
- Evidence:
  ```
  const cache = await caches.open(CACHE_NAME);
      // No cookies: /en/offline and /el/offline must not rewrite the visitor's `lang` cookie (src/proxy.ts).
      await Promise.allSettled(OFFLINE_ASSETS.map((url) => cache.add(new Request(url, { credentials: 'omit' }))));
      await precacheOfflineSubresources(cache).catch(() => {});
  ```
  Independent verifier (W1b): Read sw.js L117-124: `await Promise.allSettled(OFFLINE_ASSETS.map((url) => cache.add(new Request(url, { credentials: 'omit' }))));` and `await precacheOfflineSubresources(cache).catch(() => {});` (and L106/L112/L114 use allSettled inside), so install never rejects; L126-136 activate deletes every other guest-guide-* cache. The only other writers are the fetch handlers (networkFirstPage/cacheFirst/staleWhileRevalidate), which store /en/offline only if a guest visits it online. Executed in a node vm with the real public/sw.js and a fake cache holding a complete guest-guide-build-1: P1 (only /en/offline fails): install rejected null, new cache has /offline,/el/offline + assets, caches after activate ['guest-guide-build-2'], unvisited page offline -> 200 'precached /offline' (root page); P1b (every request fails): install rejected null, new cache entries [], caches ['guest-guide-build-2'], offline navigation -> 503 text/plain 'Offline'. PwaManager registers the versioned URL on every load (PwaManager.tsx L26-42), so a rejected install would be retried. Field frequency of an install request failing was not measured (not claimed by me either). No earlier finding (R-380/R-381 are the context).
- Problem: The three offline pages, the icons, the CSS, six fonts and (since T05) the 14-20 build scripts the offline page needs to hydrate are all fetched best-effort: allSettled and a swallowed catch. The install event never rejects, so the worker installs and activates with whatever arrived, and activate (L126-L136) deletes every other guest-guide-* cache, including the older complete one. The only writers of the cache are install and the fetch handlers, so a missing offline page is never re-added (PwaManager's register() does not reinstall the same script URL). Executed with the real sw.js in a VM (scratch vm-probes.mjs, an old complete cache guest-guide-build-1 present): (P1, only /en/offline fails) install rejected? null, caches after activate ["guest-guide-build-2"], an unvisited page offline -> 200 "precached /offline" (degraded to the root page); (P1b, every precache request fails) install rejected? null, entries in the new cache 0, caches after activate ["guest-guide-build-2"], offline navigation -> 503 text/plain "Offline". How often an install request fails in the field was not measured.
- Impact: First visit on a weak mobile connection: the install fires about 40 requests (pages, assets, CSS, fonts, scripts); if the signal drops during it, that build keeps no branded offline page, or an offline page whose Retry stays inert (the exact symptom of R-381), until the next deploy. T05 raised the number of requests the offline page depends on, so the chance that at least one fails per install is higher than before.
- Fix: Make the three offline pages (and ideally their scripts) required so that a failure fails the install: `await Promise.all(OFFLINE_PAGES.map((url) => cache.add(new Request(url, { credentials: 'omit' }))));` and `await precacheOfflineSubresources(cache);` for the scripts, keeping allSettled for icons and fonts. A rejected install keeps the old worker and cache, and PwaManager registers at every page load, so the install is retried. Add a test with a rejecting cache.add. Verifier on the fix: Correct in principle: Promise.all for the three offline pages (and for the scripts inside precacheOfflineSubresources, whose L114 allSettled must also change; the finder's text is slightly loose on that) makes a failed install keep the old worker and cache and be retried on the next page load. Note a rejected install leaves a partial guest-guide-<build> cache until the next activation; harmless. The fixRisk (a permanently broken offline route would block all updates, first install can need a second page load) is fair; add a test with a rejecting cache.add as proposed. Severity Low agreed.
- Fix risk: A permanently broken offline route would then block every worker update (visible only in the browser console); the first install on a bad connection does not complete until a later page load. Existing tests use a fake cache.add that never rejects, so they are unaffected; re-run the smoke check 'service worker installs and caches the build'.
- Found by: R5-U16 (W1b); candidate B-013
- Resolution: FIXED by T-F15 (batch B3, 2026-10-13): the install adds the three offline pages with Promise.all (credentials 'omit'), so one failing page fails the install and the previous worker and cache stay; the manifest, favicon and icons stay allSettled; precacheOfflineSubresources requires the module scripts (Promise.all, no swallowing catch) while CSS and fonts stay allSettled. Evidence: RED 5 failed / 27 passed (fix/logs/T-F15-red.log), GREEN 32/32; lead check in real Chromium on the production build (fix/logs/B3-lead-precache.log): the worker installs and activates, /offline, /en/offline and /el/offline are precached and every one of the 13 module scripts of the built /en/offline page is cached; B3 verifier PASS (mutants killed). Accepted consequence (D13): a permanently broken offline route or script now blocks every worker update (visible in the console only). Patch R5-T-F15.patch.

### R-648: The offline fallback is served under the requested URL, so every localized fallback hydrates with a different layout: hydration error, an error-report attempt, a header and footer switch, and on /en a 66 px jump with the brand mark sliding under the header
- Severity: Low
- Category: Bug
- Status: CONFIRMED
- Location: public/sw.js:L159-L166
- Evidence:
  ```
  const locale = pathname.split('/')[1];
      return (await cache.match(`/${locale}/offline`))
        || (await cache.match('/offline'))
        || new Response('Offline', { status: 503, statusText: 'Offline', headers: { 'content-type': 'text/plain' } });
  ```
  Independent verifier (W1b): Read sw.js L159-166: on a failed navigation the cached `/${locale}/offline` page is returned under the requested URL; network-only pages (/en, /el, /apartment, /availability, private) always take it (L160). shellLinks.ts L38-43 shellVariantFor + L26 STAY_ROUTES: usePathname() decides stay vs marketing vs guide shell. Chromium run on the dev server: real worker, then the worker's own fetch of ONE URL failed via CDP Fetch.failRequest on the worker target. /el/moments (1280x720): JS-off server HTML header 'site-header site-header--stay', brand /el/stay, nav [/el/stay,/el/moments]; JS on, early same, after hydration 'site-header--guide', brand /el, nav [apartment, availability, moments, #contact, stay], footer stay -> marketing; pageerror "Hydration failed because the server rendered text didn't match the client. As a result this tree will be regenerated on the client"; 1 POST to /api/errors observed. /en at 390x844 light: header 'site-header--stay' margin-bottom 0 -> 'site-header--marketing site-header--overlay' margin-bottom -66px, h1 top 186 -> 120; at 1280x720 dark h1 top 242 -> 176. src/lib/errorReporting.ts L48 window 'error' listener is what posts to /api/errors. Not in REVIEW.md: R-381 (offline scripts) is the cause of the page now hydrating, but no finding covers the mismatch. Limits: verified on the dev server; the production build was not run (same shellVariantFor and nav code; the structure mismatch of 2 vs 5 nav links makes React fall back to client render in production too, but I did not execute that).
- Problem: A failed navigation to any localized URL is answered with the cached /{locale}/offline page under the requested URL. SiteHeader and SiteFooter take their variant from usePathname() (shellVariantFor, src/components/shell/shellLinks.ts L38-L43: 'offline' is a stay route, '' a marketing route, the rest guide). The server HTML therefore carries the stay shell, and since R-381 (T05) the page hydrates, so React meets the shell of the requested URL. Real Chromium against the dev server, a fresh browser per case, the worker's own fetch of one URL failed through CDP Fetch on the worker target (scratch scripts browser-fallback-url.cjs, browser-fallback-header.cjs, browser-fallback-home3.cjs): (a) /el/moments: pageerror "Hydration failed because the server rendered text didn't match the client. As a result this tree will be regenerated on the client" with the diff site-header--stay vs --guide and brand href="/el/stay" vs "/el"; at DOMContentLoaded header "site-header site-header--stay", brand /el/stay, nav [/el/stay, /el/moments]; after hydration "site-header--guide", brand /el, nav [/el/apartment, /el/availability, /el/moments*, /el#contact, /el/stay]. (b) The page POSTs the error to /api/errors (observed). (c) /en (390x844 light and dark, 768x1024, 1280x720): header becomes "site-header--marketing site-header--overlay" with margin-bottom -66px; h1 top 186->120 (390), 207->141 (768), 242->176 (1280); brand mark top 106->40 at 390, so it overlaps the header (bottom 66) by 26 px (5 px at 768, none at 1280). Control: the start URL "/" offline gets the root /offline page, which has no header: hydrated=true, no page error. Retry still works (reload returns the real page). Since T26 (O59, R-460) /en, /el, /apartment and /availability always take this path when offline.
- Impact: A guest offline taps a link to a page that is not cached (Next falls back to a full navigation), or the offline page's own Home link (/en): the offline page paints in its server layout, then React discards it and rebuilds it with another header and footer; on /en the content jumps up 66 px and on phones the brand mark slips under the glass header. Every occurrence also attempts an error report; offline it fails, on a flaky connection it can reach the rate-limited /api/errors (audit table). The smoke reads innerText right after load (scripts/smoke-production-image.ts L331-L334) and lead check LC-12 looked at text and Retry only, so neither could see it. Run on the dev server; the production build was not run (same shellVariantFor and nav code).
- Fix: Let the fallback hydrate at its own URL: answer a failed localized navigation with Response.redirect(`/${locale}/offline?from=${encodeURIComponent(path)}`, 302) (look the offline pages up with ignoreSearch), and make OfflineActions' Retry go to `from` after validating it with safeLocalPath. Then add an offline smoke step that waits for hydration and asserts no pageerror and an unchanged header class. If the owner prefers to accept the recoverable error, record that decision next to the fallback code. Verifier on the fix: The redirect-to-/{locale}/offline?from= fix removes the cause (the page hydrates at its own URL), but it is not minimal: sw.js, OfflineActions (Retry to a validated `from`, safeLocalPath), tests and the smoke change, the address bar changes, and the offline lookup needs ignoreSearch. The fixRisk (open-redirect surface, updated test expectations) is fair. A smaller option to weigh is accepting the recoverable error and recording that decision. Severity Low agreed: the content stays usable, the visible effect is a header/footer switch and a layout jump on offline fallbacks.
- Fix risk: The address bar shows /{locale}/offline instead of the requested URL; `from` is an open-redirect surface and must be validated; expectations in tests/unit/service-worker.test.ts that read the fallback body (the unvisited and live-page cases) change to the redirect; OfflineActions tests and the offline smoke step need updating.
- Found by: R5-U16 (W1b); candidate B-011
- Resolution: FIXED by T-F09 (batch B2, 2026-10-13): a failed en/el navigation without a cached copy is answered with a 302 to /{l}/offline?from=<path+query>; the offline pages are answered from the precache by pathname (no loop) and never stored by the navigation branch; Retry goes to a toSafeLocalPath-validated `from` (also refusing a `//` result and offline pages) and reloads otherwise. Evidence: RED service-worker 5 failed + offline-actions 7 failed (fix/logs/T-F09-red.log), GREEN 54/54; lead check in real Chromium on the production build (fix/logs/B2-lead-offline.log): unvisited /en/moments offline lands on /en/offline?from=%2Fen%2Fmoments with the 302 chain, no hydration error, header and Retry present, Retry online returns to the guide, /en/offline opens offline without a redirect, unsafe `from` values (//evil.example, /.//evil.example, https://evil.example/, /en/offline) never leave the site; B2 verifier PASS (mutants killed). Residue: R-796 (each offline Retry adds a history entry), R-795 (toSafeLocalPath root cause). The smoke assertions follow in T-F41. Patch R5-T-F09.patch.

### R-649: Fallback branch for axe source uses `require` in an ES module and would throw ReferenceError; it is also unreachable
- Severity: Low
- Category: Legacy
- Status: CONFIRMED
- Location: scripts/axe-a11y.ts:L12
- Evidence:
  `const axeSource: string = (axePkg as unknown as { source?: string }).source || fs.readFileSync(require.resolve('axe-core/axe.min.js'), 'utf8');`
  Independent verifier (W34): scripts/axe-a11y.ts:12 `const axeSource: string = (axePkg as unknown as { source?: string }).source || fs.readFileSync(require.resolve('axe-core/axe.min.js'), 'utf8');`. package.json has `"type": "module"`; axe-core installed 4.12.1 (package.json:122 declares ^4.10.0). Executed under tsx 4.23.1 / Node 22.19.0 in a scratch ESM package: `typeof require = undefined`; `axe .source type = string len>0: true` (import of node_modules/axe-core/axe.js); the fallback expression -> `fallback threw: require is not defined`. So the right-hand side is never evaluated today and would throw ReferenceError if it were. `grep -n 'require.resolve\|axeSource\|axe.min' REVIEW.md` -> no hit.
- Problem: package.json has "type": "module", so tsx runs the file as ESM. Executed in a scratch dir with the same package type: `typeof require = undefined`, `axe source type = string`, `require.resolve threw: require is not defined`. axe-core 4.12.1 always exposes `.source` on the default export, so the right-hand side is never evaluated, and if it ever were, it would throw instead of falling back.
- Impact: A fallback that looks like protection but cannot work; if a later axe-core release drops `.source`, the script dies with an unrelated ReferenceError.
- Fix: Drop the fallback and fail clearly: `const axeSource = (axePkg as unknown as { source?: string }).source; if (!axeSource) throw new Error('axe-core exposes no source');`. Verifier on the fix: Correct and minimal: `const axeSource = (axePkg as unknown as { source?: string }).source; if (!axeSource) throw new Error('axe-core exposes no source');`. No lint disable or any needed; the existing cast stays. Fix risk none; run `npm run typecheck` after.
- Fix risk: None for axe-core 4.12.1 (the dependency is ^4.10.0).
- Found by: R5-U27 (W34); candidate H-009
- Resolution: DEFERRED-OWNER (economy): not done under the owner's instruction of 2026-10-13 to watch the consumption; specified in decision-D13.json (.runtime/review5/fix/) as task T-F42, resumable on request.

The marker route is the cheaper one; widening the test-only scanPathForTest adds to the wrapper that R-577 already calls a nit. Fix risk is fair.

- Problem: docs/release-verification.md:L316 promises rejection of 'push, publication' (and L313-L318 'deployment scripts'). The patterns match only the adjacent words 'git push', 'docker push', 'docker image push', 'npm publish'. Scratch runs on a copy of the real tree: package.json script 'docker buildx build --push -t registry.example/app:1 .' -> POLICY PASSES; 'docker compose -f docker/docker-compose.prod.yml push' -> PASSES; 'git -C . push origin main' -> PASSES; scripts/docker-build.sh with 'docker build --push \' -> PASSES; a new scripts/ship-it.mjs containing spawnSync('docker', ['push', tag]) or spawnSync('git', ['push', 'origin', 'main']) -> PASSES (argv arrays are the repo's own style: verify-release.mjs, check-secrets.mjs). Controls: 'docker push ...' in package.json and 'git push origin main' in scripts/ship-it.sh are rejected. Mutation (scratch): replacing any one of eight patterns (version-qualified Vercel, Wrangler and Wrangler Pages, 'cloudflare pages deploy', git push, docker push, docker image push, npm publish) with a never-matching regex leaves all 64 tests green; only Vercel, Wrangler, Wrangler Pages and gh-pages have tests.

State in the doc that argv-style calls cannot be seen by text patterns. Verifier on the fix: The proposed patterns work as written (verified). Argv-style calls cannot be caught by text patterns, so the doc sentence the finder asks for is right. `docker-compose push` (hyphenated v1 form) is not covered by `docker\s+compose`; add it only if wanted. A comment containing '--push' in a scanned file would fail the gate, as the fix risk says. Control (unmodified): POLICY PASSES (no errors). 'server_tokens off;' -> '# server_tokens off;': POLICY PASSES. 'ssl_verify_client on;' -> '# ssl_verify_client on;': POLICY PASSES. 'ssl_verify_client on;' -> 'ssl_verify_client off; # was: ssl_verify_client on;': POLICY PASSES. Nothing else covers these two directives: scripts/test-nginx-ingress.sh:L68 deletes every ssl_(certificate|certificate_key|client_certificate|verify_client|protocols) line from the config it exercises and runs only 'nginx -t' on the production render; a repository search for the template and the directive names finds only release-policy.mjs, its test, test-nginx-ingress.sh and tests/security/claim-token-transport.test.ts (which checks only $request_uri / $uri). - Resolution: FIXED by T-F05 (batch B1, 2026-10-13): the trusted-ingress checks read a comment-stripped copy of the nginx template (stripNginxComments), so a commented-out or disabled ssl_verify_client, server_tokens or similar line no longer satisfies a marker; the three finder mutants are rejected. ### R-659: 'Nginx logging must exclude query strings' only forbids the literal $request_uri; $uri is satisfied by the rate-limit maps, so $request, $args or client IPs in the log format pass
- Severity: Low
- Category: Security
- Status: CONFIRMED
- Location: scripts/lib/release-policy.mjs:L853-L855
- Evidence:
  ```
  if (nginx === undefined || !nginx.includes('$uri') || nginx.includes('$request_uri')) {
      errors.push('Nginx logging must exclude query strings from the claim transport');
    }
  ```
  Independent verifier (W3): scripts/lib/release-policy.mjs:L852-L855 tests `nginx.includes('$uri') && !nginx.includes('$request_uri')` on the whole template. '$uri' also occurs in deploy/nginx/nginx.conf.template L44, L48, L52 (rate-limit maps) besides the log format L16, so the positive half is vacuous. Scratch run: appending `$request $args $remote_addr $http_x_forwarded_for $http_referer` to the origin_safe log_format -> 'Local release policy passed'. Deleting the whole log_format and access_log lines -> fails, but only with 'layered Nginx rate limiting lacks: limit_req=$limit_req_status' (incidental). Control `$request_uri` -> 'Nginx logging must exclude query strings from the claim transport'. tests/security/claim-token-transport.test.ts:L309-L320 repeats `not.toMatch(/\$request_uri/u)` and `toContain('$uri')` on the concatenated sources, so it has the same hole. The template comment (L14-L15) promises no peer IPs, query strings or forwarding headers; docs/security/claim-token-transport.md:L40-L42 promises only '$uri rather than $request_uri', which the policy does enforce (the finder's impact slightly overstates the doc). Fix pieces checked in scratch: on the comment-stripped real template, `log_format origin_safe ...;` is found, `access_log ... origin_safe;` is found, and the forbidden regex does not match the real format; it matches $request, $args, $remote_addr, $http_x_forwarded_for, $http_referer, $request_uri, $query_string and allows $request_id, $request_method, $request_time, $realip_remote_addr.
- Problem: The check runs on the whole template. '$uri' occurs in three rate-limit maps (deploy/nginx/nginx.conf.template L44, L48, L52) as well as in the log format (L16), so the positive half is vacuous; the negative half does not cover $request (it contains the query string), $args, $query_string, $remote_addr, $http_x_forwarded_for or $http_referer. Scratch run on a copy of the real tree: appending '$request $args $remote_addr $http_x_forwarded_for $http_referer' to the origin_safe log_format -> POLICY PASSES. Deleting the whole log_format and access_log lines is caught, but only incidentally by the unrelated rate-limit marker 'limit_req=$limit_req_status'. tests/security/claim-token-transport.test.ts:L309-L320 repeats the same two assertions, so both places have the same hole and no test names the log format.
- Impact: The template comment (L14-L15) and docs/security/claim-token-transport.md:L42 promise access logs without query strings and peer IPs. A debugging edit that adds $request would write the one-time claim tokens that arrive in legacy '?claim=' URLs, and client addresses, into access.log while gate 3, gate 4 and the vitest guard stay green.
- Fix: Check the log format itself: extract 'log_format origin_safe ...;' and the 'access_log ... origin_safe;' line from comment-stripped text, require both, and forbid /\$(?:request(?![_\w])|request_uri|args|query_string|is_args|remote_addr|binary_remote_addr|http_x_forwarded_for|http_referer)\b/u inside the format. Mirror the change in tests/security/claim-token-transport.test.ts (or keep one of the two checks). Verifier on the fix: Correct and verified on the real template. Fix risk is fair: the policy-test fixture uses other format names (`log_format safe`, `log_format claim_safe`, test L244-L245) and must be updated; $request_id/$request_method/$request_time stay allowed through the lookahead.
- Fix risk: $request_id, $request_method and $request_time must stay allowed (hence the lookahead). The fixture template in scripts/tests/release-policy.test.mjs (L244-L245) uses other format names and must be updated.
- Found by: R5-U25 (W3); candidate M-006
- Resolution: FIXED by T-F05 (batch B1, 2026-10-13): the policy requires `log_format origin_safe` and `access_log` using it, and rejects the request line, query and client-address variables in that format ($request, $args, $remote_addr, $http_x_forwarded_for, $http_referer ...); tests/security/claim-token-transport.test.ts mirrors it (19 tests). Evidence: RED on 4 mutated copies of the real template (1 failed each), GREEN 19/19, policy tests 88/88; B1 verifier PASS-WITH-NOTES. Open nit: R-788 (braced and upper-case spellings, other variables).

### R-660: dockerLogicalLines ends an instruction at a full-line comment inside a backslash continuation, so a commented runner RUN is reported as 'must remove npm and npx'
- Severity: Low
- Category: Bug
- Status: CONFIRMED
- Location: scripts/lib/release-policy.mjs:L875-L877
- Evidence:
  ```
  for (const rawLine of source.split(/\r?\n/u)) {
      const trimmed = rawLine.trim();
      if (pending === '' && (trimmed === '' || trimmed.startsWith('#'))) continue;
  ```
  Independent verifier (W3): scripts/lib/release-policy.mjs:L875-L886: L877 skips '#' lines only while `pending === ''`; inside a continuation the comment is appended, has no trailing backslash and closes the logical line, so the next `&& rm -f ...` fragment becomes a separate pseudo-instruction. Scratch real-tree run: a full-line ` # drop the package managers from the runtime image` between `RUN apk add ... \` and `&& rm -rf ...` in the runner stage -> 'docker/Dockerfile.security: runner stage must remove npm and npx' (the RUN still removes npm and npx); the same with the comment before `&& rm -f /usr/local/bin/npm ...` -> same error; control with the comment before the RUN passes. Replacing the join by `pending = fragment` -> 64/64 tests pass, so the backslash path is only covered by the real Dockerfile at gate 3. Docker side: the Dockerfile reference (https://docs.docker.com/reference/dockerfile/, fetched read-only) shows `RUN echo hello \ / # comment / world` and says 'Comment lines are removed before the Dockerfile instructions are executed.' So such a comment is valid Docker syntax and the policy's parser deviates. I did not run docker build and did not check the installed Docker/BuildKit version.
- Problem: L877 skips comment lines only when no instruction is pending. Inside a continuation a '# comment' line is appended as a fragment and, having no trailing backslash, terminates the logical line, so the following '&& rm -f ...' fragment becomes a separate pseudo-instruction. Scratch run on a copy of the real tree: adding the full-line comment ' # drop the package managers from the runtime image' between 'RUN apk add ... \' and '&& rm -rf ...' in the runner stage (the RUN still removes npm and npx) -> 'docker/Dockerfile.security: runner stage must remove npm and npx'. The backslash-joining path has no test at all: replacing the join by 'pending = fragment' leaves 64/64 tests green (only the real Dockerfile at gate 3 catches it). The Dockerfile reference (Format) says comment lines are removed before a continued instruction is executed; I did not run docker.
- Impact: A harmless explanatory comment inside the multi-line runner RUN blocks the release with a misleading message; the fix is to move the comment. Fail-closed, hence Low.
- Fix: Skip '#' lines before the continuation logic (if (trimmed.startsWith('#')) continue;, keeping the blank-line rule) and add a test whose RUN uses backslash continuations with a comment line inside. Verifier on the fix: The fix (skip '#' lines before the continuation logic, keep the blank-line rule) matches the documented Docker behaviour and is minimal; add a test whose RUN uses backslash continuations with a comment line inside. Fix risk is fair (heredoc bodies are not used in the Dockerfile). Fails closed with a misleading message, so Low.
- Fix risk: A heredoc body in RUN (<<EOF) could contain lines starting with '#'; the Dockerfile has none.
- Found by: R5-U25 (W3); candidate M-011
- Resolution: FIXED by T-F13 (batch B3, 2026-10-13): dockerLogicalLines skips full-line '#' comments before the continuation logic (the blank-line rule stays), so a commented RUN inside a backslash continuation no longer ends the instruction. Evidence: policy tests 99 -> 103, RED 3 new tests fail on the old library (fix/logs/T-F13-red.log), GREEN 103/103, validate:release-policy passes on the real Dockerfile, lint and lint:security 0; B3 verifier PASS-WITH-NOTES (mutants killed). The boundary text of docs/release-verification.md:318-320 ('only the runner stage') is stale and belongs to T-F55. Patch R5-T-F13.patch.

### R-661: The Node base-image digest pin that docs/release-verification.md describes is enforced by no gate: the policy pins PostgreSQL and Nginx but not the base of all three production images
- Severity: Low
- Category: Dependencies
- Status: CONFIRMED
- Location: scripts/lib/release-policy.mjs:L1086-L1088
- Evidence:
  ```
  const dockerSource = await readOptional(path.join(root, 'docker/Dockerfile.security'));
    if (dockerSource === undefined) errors.push('docker/Dockerfile.security is required');
    else validateSecurityImageRunnerStage(dockerSource, errors);
  ```
  Independent verifier (W3): scripts/lib/release-policy.mjs:L1086-L1088 reads docker/Dockerfile.security only for validateSecurityImageRunnerStage (USER, ADD, npm removal; L901-L922). git grep for 'node:22-alpine' and the digest prefix 0a7108bf outside REVIEW.md/PROGRESS.md: the four FROM lines (Dockerfile L1, L29, L61, L100), docs/release-verification.md L215/L221/L231 and tag-only strings in scripts/tests/release-policy.test.mjs L175/177/467-477/519. Scratch real-tree runs: runner `FROM node:22-alpine AS runner` (no digest) -> 'Local release policy passed'; workers digest replaced by 64 zeros -> 'Local release policy passed'. No other gate checks it (scripts/docker-build.sh, docker-scan.sh, smoke do not inspect FROM). docs/release-verification.md:L208-L233 describes a manual update procedure (replace every occurrence, repository search). The doc's own boundary text (L318-L322) says the policy checks only the runner stage, so the gap is documented as a boundary, not a broken promise.
- Problem: docs/release-verification.md:L208-L233 states that all four stages of docker/Dockerfile.security use one digest-pinned Node image and gives a manual procedure ('Replace every occurrence of the old digest ... confirm that a repository search finds no old digest left'). The policy reads the Dockerfile only for validateSecurityImageRunnerStage (USER, ADD, npm removal). A search for 'node:22-alpine' outside REVIEW.md/PROGRESS.md finds only the Dockerfile, the doc and a tag-only string in the policy's own test fixture; tests/unit/install-script-allowlist.test.ts and tests/routes/client-error-report.test.ts read the Dockerfile for other reasons. Scratch runs on a copy of the real tree: runner stage 'FROM node:22-alpine@sha256:0a71... AS runner' -> 'FROM node:22-alpine AS runner': POLICY PASSES; workers stage digest replaced by 64 zeros: POLICY PASSES.
- Impact: A tag-only or half-updated base image (workers and migrate images on another Node patch than the web image) passes verify:release; the only protection is the doc's manual search step. It is the one image pin the policy leaves out, while PostgreSQL and Nginx are pinned twice.
- Fix: After the runner check, collect the external FROM instructions via dockerLogicalLines: each must match /^FROM\s+node:22-alpine@sha256:[0-9a-f]{64}(?:\s+AS\s+\S+)?$/iu and all digests must be equal (no constant to maintain, so the doc's 'replace every occurrence' procedure keeps working). Add two tests (tag-only, mixed digests) and one sentence in the doc. Verifier on the fix: The check is correct (real Dockerfile passes, tag-only runner is rejected in scratch), but the stated fix risk omits one item: with the check added, 3 of the 64 existing tests failed in my scratch run, because the baseline fixture Dockerfile and the Dockerfile mutation tests use tag-only `FROM node:22-alpine AS ...` (test L175, L177, L467-L477, L519). Those fixtures must get a 64-hex digest in the same change. 'FROM <stage>' lines must be skipped (none today).
- Fix risk: 'FROM <stage>' lines that reference an earlier stage must be skipped (none today). A Node major bump needs the regex edited with the Dockerfile; use node:[0-9]+-alpine if that friction is unwanted.
- Found by: R5-U25 (W3); candidate M-004
- Resolution: FIXED by T-F13 (batch B3, 2026-10-13): a new check (validateSecurityImageBaseImages) collects the external FROM instructions of docker/Dockerfile.security: each must be node:<major>-alpine@sha256:<64 lowercase hex> with an optional AS name, FROM lines that name an earlier stage are skipped, and all digests must be equal; a FROM with a flag or `scratch` fails closed. Evidence as R-660 (tag-only runner and mixed digests are rejected, the real Dockerfile with 4 FROM lines and one digest passes); B3 verifier PASS-WITH-NOTES.

### R-662: prune-reports: an invalid KEEP_REPORTS (NaN) deletes every report, a negative one deletes the wrong files
- Severity: Low
- Category: Bug
- Status: CONFIRMED
- Location: scripts/prune-reports.ts:L9
- Evidence:
  `const KEEP = Number(process.env.KEEP_REPORTS || 5);`
  Independent verifier (W34): scripts/prune-reports.ts:9 `const KEEP = Number(process.env.KEEP_REPORTS || 5);`, then `if (files.length <= KEEP)` and `files.slice(KEEP)`. Executed `/Users/pvasilakis/site/node_modules/.bin/tsx /Users/pvasilakis/site/scripts/prune-reports.ts` from a scratch cwd with 7 files axe-a11y-report-2026-1..7.json (distinct mtimes): KEEP_REPORTS=abc -> `[prune] kept NaN newest a11y reports (removed 7)`, 0 left; 5x -> same, 0 left; -1 -> `removed 1`, 6 left (files 2-7, the oldest 1 deleted); 0 -> removed 7; 2.5 -> removed 5, 2 left; empty -> 5 kept. The files are git-ignored (.gitignore:48 `/axe-a11y-report*.json`) and produced by scripts/axe-a11y.ts:177-180; package.json:62 `reports:prune`. No REVIEW.md finding mentions prune-reports or KEEP_REPORTS.
- Problem: The value is never validated. `files.length <= KEEP` is false for NaN and `files.slice(NaN)` equals slice(0), so everything is deleted. Run from a scratch cwd with 7 files axe-a11y-report-2026-1..7.json and `/Users/pvasilakis/site/node_modules/.bin/tsx /Users/pvasilakis/site/scripts/prune-reports.ts`: KEEP_REPORTS=abc -> `[prune] kept NaN newest a11y reports (removed 7)`, 0 files left; KEEP_REPORTS=-1 -> `kept -1 newest ... (removed 1)`, 6 left (slice(-1) selects only the oldest); KEEP_REPORTS=0 -> all 7 removed; unset/empty -> 5 kept.
- Impact: A typo such as `KEEP_REPORTS=5x npm run reports:prune` removes all advisory axe reports in the current directory instead of keeping 5. Only files matching /^axe-a11y-report-.*\.json$/ in cwd are affected, and they are gitignored regenerable output, hence Low.
- Fix: -const KEEP = Number(process.env.KEEP_REPORTS || 5); +const KEEP = Number(process.env.KEEP_REPORTS || 5); +if (!Number.isInteger(KEEP) || KEEP < 1) { + console.error('[prune] KEEP_REPORTS must be a positive integer'); + process.exit(1); +} Verifier on the fix: Correct: validate after parsing and exit 1 on a non-integer or negative value. Keep `KEEP < 0` (not `< 1`) if KEEP_REPORTS=0 ('delete all') should stay valid; the finder's own fix risk note says this. Low is fair (regenerable advisory output in the current directory).
- Fix risk: KEEP_REPORTS=0 (delete all) stops working; allow KEEP < 0 only if 0 must stay valid (use `KEEP < 0`).
- Found by: R5-U26 (W34); candidate H-020
- Resolution: DEFERRED-OWNER (economy): not done under the owner's instruction of 2026-10-13 to watch the consumption; specified in decision-D13.json (.runtime/review5/fix/) as task T-F39, resumable on request.

### R-663: scripts/README.md tells developers to source .env.local with the shell, which breaks for valid dotenv values containing spaces
- Severity: Low
- Category: Maintainability
- Status: CONFIRMED
- Location: scripts/README.md:L290-L296
- Evidence:
  `set -a; . ./.env.local; set +a`
  Independent verifier (W34): scripts/README.md:294 `set -a; . ./.env.local; set +a` (followed by npm run outbox:drain / operations:check, package.json:60-61 `tsx scripts/...`; scripts/drain-outbox.ts has no dotenv loading, `grep dotenv\|loadEnv` finds none). GUEST_WIFI_NETWORK is a real required variable (src/lib/runtime-env-schema.js:87). Executed with x.env containing `GUEST_WIFI_NETWORK=Villa Guest` and `OTHER=ok`: bash `./x.env: line 1: Guest: command not found` -> {"GUEST_WIFI_NETWORK":"[unset]","OTHER":"ok"}; zsh `command not found: Guest` -> same; `tsx --env-file=x.env p.ts` -> {"GUEST_WIFI_NETWORK":"Villa Guest","OTHER":"ok"}; dotenv.parse -> {"GUEST_WIFI_NETWORK":"Villa Guest","OTHER":"ok"}. Not covered by any REVIEW.md finding.
- Problem: The orchestrator and next dev read .env.local with dotenv, which accepts unquoted values with spaces. Sourcing it with sh executes the text after the first space as a command. Execution: x.env containing `GUEST_WIFI_NETWORK=Villa Guest` -> `./x.env: line 1: Guest: command not found` and `GUEST_WIFI_NETWORK=[unset]`, while dotenv.parse returns {"GUEST_WIFI_NETWORK":"Villa Guest"}. Values with `$`, `#` or quotes behave differently as well. Verified alternative on this machine: `tsx --env-file=x.env p.ts` printed "Villa Guest" (Node 22.19.0).
- Impact: With a real guest network name (most SSIDs contain spaces) in .env.local, `npm run outbox:drain` / `operations:check` run from the documented shell snippet get a missing or mangled environment and a stray 'command not found' error. Development runbook only.
- Fix: Replace the snippet with `npx tsx --env-file=.env.local scripts/drain-outbox.ts` (or document that values in .env.local must be quoted for this snippet). Verifier on the fix: Docs-only and correct. `npx tsx --env-file=.env.local scripts/drain-outbox.ts` works (verified with Node 22.19.0 and the repo's tsx). ### R-667: load_environment documents 'same parser and precedence as next dev' but differs: no ${VAR} expansion, empty inherited variables are overridden
- Severity: Low
- Category: Logic
- Status: CONFIRMED
- Location: scripts/system-orchestrator.sh:L259-L281
- Evidence:
  ```
  # Load the development env files with the same parser and precedence as
  # `next dev` (dotenv; the first file that defines a key wins; values already
  ```
  Independent verifier (W34): Comment at L259-261: 'same parser and precedence as `next dev`'; load_environment (L262-285) uses plain dotenv.parse (repo dotenv 17.4.2) and L280 `if (process.env[key] !== undefined && process.env[key] !== '') continue;`. Installed @next/env 16.3.8 (node_modules/@next/env/package.json) bundles dotenv-expand (`expand`, `_interpolate`, `_resolveEscapeSequences`) and keeps an inherited empty variable (`typeof p[t]==="undefined"`). Executed both against the same scratch .env.local (FAKE_BASE=abc, FAKE_URL=postgresql://u:${FAKE_BASE}@localhost/db, FAKE_EMPTY_INHERITED=from-file with FAKE_EMPTY_INHERITED='' inherited): @next/env `FAKE_URL = "postgresql://u:abc@localhost/db"`, `FAKE_EMPTY_INHERITED = ""`; orchestrator `FAKE_URL = "postgresql://u:${FAKE_BASE}@localhost/db"`, `FAKE_EMPTY_INHERITED = "from-file"`. Extra finding from the run: even with the literal FAKE_URL pre-set in the environment, @next/env returned the expanded value (dotenv-expand writes into process.env), so an orchestrator-started `next dev` re-expands and may not use the DATABASE_URL the orchestrator probed or exported; the finder's impact text is directionally right, the exact outcome for the fallback case was not run. No file in the repo uses `${` (.env.example grep), so this affects only hand-written env files. Not covered by any REVIEW.md finding.
- Problem: The installed @next/env 16.3.8 (node_modules/@next/env/dist/index.js) runs dotenv-expand logic (`${VAR}` interpolation and `\$` unescaping) on each file and keeps an inherited variable whose value is the empty string (`typeof p[t]==="undefined"`). The orchestrator uses plain dotenv.parse and L280 `if (process.env[key] !== undefined && process.env[key] !== '') continue;`. Execution (same fake .env.local: FAKE_BASE=abc, FAKE_URL=postgresql://u:${FAKE_BASE}@localhost/db, FAKE_EMPTY_INHERITED=from-file; FAKE_EMPTY_INHERITED='' inherited): @next/env printed `FAKE_URL = "postgresql://u:abc@localhost/db"` and `FAKE_EMPTY_INHERITED = ""`; the orchestrator replica printed `FAKE_URL = "postgresql://u:${FAKE_BASE}@localhost/db"` and `FAKE_EMPTY_INHERITED = "from-file"`. scripts/dev-proxy.mjs L22-L25 uses dotenv.config without expansion as well.
- Impact: A DATABASE_URL (or any value) written with `${...}` interpolation, or a password containing an escaped `\$`, is validated, probed and migrated by the orchestrator in its literal form while next dev would see the expanded value. For DATABASE_URL the probe then fails and the script silently falls back to the Docker database and exports that URL to `npm run dev`, so the dev server uses a different database than the one configured. Only affects .env files that use expansion; the generated .env.local does not.
- Fix: Either correct the comment to 'dotenv.parse, no variable expansion' and document that values must be literal, or make the loader call @next/env's loadEnvConfig (already a dependency of next) so both agree. Verifier on the fix: The cheaper option (correct the comment to 'dotenv.parse, no variable expansion; literal values only', and the matching phrase in scripts/README.md:'same precedence as next dev' stays true) is correct and sufficient. Switching to loadEnvConfig is larger and changes empty-variable precedence; only do it if expansion is wanted. Severity Low is borderline Nit because nothing in the repo uses expansion, but the false equivalence claim is in the authoritative loader, so Low is accepted.
- Fix risk: Switching to loadEnvConfig changes which empty-string variables win; check ensure-pepper flow (maybe_ensure_pepper reloads after `unset SECURITY_PEPPER`).
- Found by: R5-U26 (W34); candidate H-019
- Resolution: FIXED by T-F08 (batch B2, 2026-10-13): the loader comment now states what the code does (no ${VAR} expansion, first file wins, an inherited non-empty value is kept, an inherited empty value is replaced, quotes/$/backticks stay literal), checked by executed cases L1-L5 (pass before and after) and compared with @next/env 16.3.8 (which does expand ${VAR}). scripts/README.md:29 ('same precedence as next dev') is the remaining stale phrase and belongs to T-F56 (docs).

### R-668: Fallback DB container is left running with no state file on three failure paths, so `system:down` cannot stop it
- Severity: Low
- Category: Error handling
- Status: CONFIRMED
- Location: scripts/system-orchestrator.sh:L381-L394
- Evidence:
  `wait_for_container_ready "$DB_CONTAINER" 90 || die "Fallback database failed to become ready" 16`
  Independent verifier (W34): `grep -n write_state scripts/system-orchestrator.sh` shows calls only at L409, L424 (prepare_database) and L604 (start_app). start_fallback_database (L381-394) runs `compose up -d`, then `wait_for_container_ready ... || die ... 16`, with DB_MODE="local" set only afterwards; L421-423 dies 17 without a state write; stop_fallback_database_if_needed (L694-717) starts with `if ! load_state; then return; fi`, and L715-716 are `compose ... down || warn "Failed to stop fallback DB cleanly"` then an unconditional `rm -f "$STATE_FILE"`. Executed the verbatim functions (script minus the final `main` line, copied into a scratch repo root; docker replaced by a stub on PATH, sleep stubbed; no real Docker): (1) container never healthy: `prepare_database exit=16`, state file exists? no, container up (stub)? yes, then cmd_down printed `Shutdown complete` and `container up after down? yes`; (2) healthy but DATABASE_URL unreachable: exit=17, same result; (3) state present, stubbed `compose down` failing: `WARNING: Failed to stop fallback DB cleanly`, state file removed, container still up, a second cmd_down does nothing. No trap exists in the script (grep trap: none), so Ctrl-C during the 90 s wait behaves like case 1. Not covered by any REVIEW.md finding (R-561 is the compose-binary finding).
- Problem: write_state is called only at L409, L424 (end of prepare_database) and L604 (start_app): `grep -n write_state scripts/system-orchestrator.sh` lists exactly those call sites. stop_fallback_database_if_needed (L694-717) starts with `if ! load_state; then return; fi` and acts only when DB_MODE=local. Paths that leave the container up without a state file: (1) `compose up -d db` succeeds, then wait_for_container_ready times out (die 16, L389); (2) the container becomes healthy but the single database_reachable check at L421-423 fails (die 17); (3) `compose ... down || warn "Failed to stop fallback DB cleanly"` (L715) fails and L716 `rm -f "$STATE_FILE"` runs anyway, deleting the only handle although the container is still up. A Ctrl-C during the 90 s wait has the same effect.
- Impact: `npm run system:down` prints 'Shutdown complete' while site-dev-db keeps running and holding 127.0.0.1:5433 (and the next run treats it as already running). The developer has to `docker stop site-dev-db` by hand. Dev only, no data loss (the volume is kept).
- Fix: Write the state as soon as the container is started: in start_fallback_database after the `compose ... up -d` line add `DB_MODE="local"; write_state "none"`. In stop_fallback_database_if_needed remove the state only when `down` succeeded: - compose -f "$REPO_ROOT/$DB_COMPOSE_FILE" down || warn "Failed to stop fallback DB cleanly" - rm -f "$STATE_FILE" + if compose -f "$REPO_ROOT/$DB_COMPOSE_FILE" down; then rm -f "$STATE_FILE"; else warn "Failed to stop fallback DB cleanly; state file kept"; fi Verifier on the fix: Correct and minimal: `DB_MODE="local"; write_state "none"` right after the `compose up -d` line, and remove the state file only when `compose down` succeeds. Both are consistent with write_state/load_state semantics (the state is rewritten at L409/L424/L604 later). Fix risk is fair. Dev-only with kept volume, so Low is right.
- Fix risk: State file semantics change slightly (it now exists while the DB is starting). Test with docker stubbed on PATH: failing wait, failing down, then `down` again.
- Found by: R5-U26 (W34); candidate H-014
- Resolution: FIXED by T-F14 (batch B3, 2026-10-13): start_fallback_database records DB_MODE=local and writes the state file right after `compose up -d` succeeds; the fallback stop removes the state file only when `compose down` succeeded and warns that the state file is kept otherwise, so `system:down` can stop the container after a failed start. Evidence: probe RED 84 pass / 9 fail on the T-F08-state copy (fix/logs/T-F14-red.log), GREEN 93/93 (T-F14-green.log), re-run by the lead on the repo script (sha256 3430ba3f) and by the B3 verifier: 93/93; mutants fail as expected. The probe's F6 case can fail once under heavy parallel load (it reads the stub log right after exit while the app starts in the background): probe flake, not repo code. Patch R5-T-F14.patch.

### R-669: Orchestrator never checks that the migration/dev database is local; README says it 'cannot target production'
- Severity: Low
- Category: Security
- Status: CONFIRMED
- Location: scripts/system-orchestrator.sh:L396-L411
- Evidence:
  ```
  if [[ "$DATABASE_URL" == "$DB_LOCAL_URL" ]] && fallback_container_running; then
        DB_MODE="local"
      else
        DB_MODE="managed"
      fi
  ```
  Independent verifier (W34): validate_database_url (scripts/system-orchestrator.sh L303-311) only checks `protocol === 'postgres:' || 'postgresql:'`; prepare_database (L396-411) sets DB_MODE="managed" for any reachable URL that is not the fallback container; run_migrations_with_retry then migrates it and start_app runs `npm run dev` against it. No host or loopback check exists anywhere (read all of L262-L430 and the command flows L735-L770). scripts/README.md:141-142: 'The host orchestrator above is a development helper and cannot target production.' The only enforcement is scripts/lib/release-policy.mjs:640-645 (regex for PROFILE="production" / --profile production / `production)`), exercised by scripts/tests/release-policy.test.mjs:449 ('rejects a system orchestrator that can target production'); it constrains a named production profile, not DATABASE_URL. `grep -rn managed docs scripts/README.md README.md` finds no documentation of the 'managed' mode, so owner intent for a remote development database is unknown. Not covered by any REVIEW.md finding.
- Problem: validate_database_url (L303-311) only requires a postgres:// or postgresql:// protocol. Any reachable URL, from the inherited environment or from .env.local/.env, becomes DB_MODE=managed and flows into run_migrations_with_retry (L501-529) and then `npm run dev`. No host check (loopback) and no confirmation exist. scripts/README.md:141-142 states 'The host orchestrator above is a development helper and cannot target production.' The only enforcement is scripts/lib/release-policy.mjs:640-645, a regex that rejects the strings PROFILE="production" / --profile production in the script; it does not constrain DATABASE_URL. (The 'managed' mode may be intentional for a hosted dev database; I could not establish the owner's intent.)
- Impact: A shell that still exports a production or staging DATABASE_URL (copied from a runbook, or a stale .env.local value) followed by `npm run system:up` applies pending migrations to that database and starts the dev server against it. The README sentence gives false assurance. Realistic only with a mis-set variable; dev machine only.
- Fix: Decision needed. Minimal: in validate_database_url also require the URL host to be localhost, 127.0.0.1 or ::1 unless an explicit opt-in flag (for example --allow-remote-db) is given; otherwise reword scripts/README.md:141-142 to 'does not start production services; it migrates whatever DATABASE_URL points to'. Pair with the DIRECT_URL finding (same check on DIRECT_URL). Verifier on the fix: The facts are verified, but the README sentence can also be read as 'no production profile exists' (which is exactly what release-policy enforces), so the remedy depends on a fact only the owner knows: whether a remote or managed development database is a supported path. That makes the host-check-plus-opt-in-flag fix an owner decision (DEFERRED-OWNER candidate); the cheap alternative is to reword README.md:141-142. Fix risk is fair (breaks the implicit remote-dev-DB path). Raw `npx prisma migrate deploy` has the same exposure, so the benefit is small; Low is the ceiling.
- Fix risk: Developers who use a remote managed development database lose the implicit path unless they pass the flag. Test: loopback URL passes, remote host dies with exit 14, flag lets it through.

- Resolution: FIXED by T-F01 (batch B1, 2026-10-13): validate_database_url refuses a DATABASE_URL host that is not localhost, 127.0.0.1 or [::1] (exit 14, naming --allow-remote-db) unless the new CLI flag is given; the Docker fallback URL passes; unknown flags still exit 1 (O42). Evidence as R-632 (probe cases B1-B12, 37/37). Known gap: R-790 (the opt-in variable can still be set from an env-file line), to be closed in T-F08.

### R-670: app.pid is trusted without checking the process identity: a stale PID file makes `down`/`restart` signal an unrelated process
- Severity: Low
- Category: Bug
- Status: CONFIRMED
- Location: scripts/system-orchestrator.sh:L545-L551
- Evidence:
  ```
  [[ -n "$pid" ]] || return 1
    kill -0 "$pid" >/dev/null 2>&1
  ```
  Independent verifier (W34): app_is_running (L545-551): `[[ -f "$APP_PID_FILE" ]] ... pid=$(cat ...) ... kill -0 "$pid"`; stop_app (L657-692) then `kill "$pid"` and `kill -9` after 15 s. The PID file lives in .runtime/system (git-ignored, survives reboot); the real file at HEAD holds 15837, whose process is `npm run dev`, so the recorded PID is the npm process and the proposed `ps -p $pid -o command=` match is workable on macOS. Executed the verbatim functions in a scratch repo root against a PID file naming an unrelated `/bin/sleep 300`: `app_is_running=true`, `[system] Stopping app process 26760`, `unrelated process alive after stop_app? no`. No existing REVIEW.md finding covers it.
- Problem: app_is_running treats any live process with the recorded PID as the dev server. The PID file is removed only by `down`/stop_app (L657-692), so after a crash, reboot or killed terminal it survives, and the PID can be reused by an unrelated process of the same user. stop_app then runs `kill "$pid"` and, after 15 s, `kill -9`. Replica of L545-551 and L657-692 verbatim with APP_PID_FILE pointing at a scratch file holding the PID of an unrelated `sleep 300`: `app_is_running=true`, `[system] Stopping app process 26492`, `unrelated process alive after stop_app? no`.
- Impact: After a reboot or crash, `npm run system:down`, `system:restart` or `system:up` either kills an arbitrary process of the same user (SIGTERM, then SIGKILL) or refuses to start with 'Application already running with PID n' (die 19). Probability is low (needs PID reuse), the consequence of a kill is unsaved work in some other process.
- Fix: Verify the command line as well as liveness, in app_is_running: kill -0 "$pid" >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 1 + [[ "$(ps -p "$pid" -o command= 2>/dev/null)" == *"npm run dev"* ]] (`bash -lc "npm run dev"` execs npm, so the recorded process is `npm run dev`; scratch test on npm 11.18.0 showed `18945 ... npm run dev`). Remove a stale file when the check fails. Verifier on the fix: Adding `[[ "$(ps -p "$pid" -o command= 2>/dev/null)" == *"npm run dev"* ]]` to app_is_running is correct and minimal (works on macOS and Linux; the Linux process title of npm is also 'npm run dev'). Stale-file removal should also be done in stop_app when the identity check fails. Keep app_cmd in start_app and the match string in sync. Low is right (needs PID reuse).
- Fix risk: ps output format differs between macOS and Linux (`-o command=` works on both); a changed app_cmd must stay in sync. Test with a PID file naming an unrelated sleep process (must not be killed) and with the real start/stop cycle.
- Found by: R5-U26 (W34); candidate H-017
- Resolution: FIXED by T-F14 (batch B3, 2026-10-13): app.pid is trusted only when the process identity matches: app_is_running does `kill -0` and then checks `ps -p <pid> -o command=` for the start command (APP_START_COMMAND, now a reserved name), start_app uses the same constant, and stop_app removes a stale pid file without signalling a process that does not match. Evidence as R-668 (probe cases F4-F8: an unrelated `sleep` is not killed by `down`); a failing ps check fails closed (the app counts as not running). Linux `ps` titles of npm are untested (macOS only).

### R-671: Startup verification: --timeout counts only sleeps (curl is unbounded) and a dead app is waited on for the full timeout
- Severity: Low
- Category: Bug
- Status: CONFIRMED
- Location: scripts/system-orchestrator.sh:L634-L650
- Evidence:
  ```
  sleep 2
      elapsed=$((elapsed + 2))
  ```
  Independent verifier (W34): wait_for_runtime (L624-651): the loop `while (( elapsed < START_TIMEOUT ))` runs three `curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}'` calls without --max-time and then `sleep 2; elapsed=$((elapsed + 2))`; it never calls app_is_running. Executed the verbatim function (scratch repo root, stub curl that sleeps 1 s and returns 000, no app, no PID file) with START_TIMEOUT=4: `ERROR: Runtime did not become ready in 4s (live=000, ready=000, page=000)` and `return=1 nominal START_TIMEOUT=4s, wall time=10s, app_is_running=no`. cmd_verify (L774-777) also calls verify_runtime. Not covered by any REVIEW.md finding.
- Problem: wait_for_runtime increments `elapsed` by 2 per iteration regardless of how long the three `curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}'` calls (L635-637) took; none has --max-time/--connect-timeout, and curl has no default total timeout once connected. The loop also never checks app_is_running, so an app that exited at start-up is polled until START_TIMEOUT. Replica of L609-650 verbatim with a stub curl that sleeps 1 s and returns 000, START_TIMEOUT=4: output `ERROR: Runtime did not become ready in 4s (live=000, ready=000, page=000)` / `nominal START_TIMEOUT=4s, wall time=10s`. With a cold `next dev` compile of /en (first request blocks until compiled) or a server that accepts but never answers, wall time is unbounded while the message still says 'in 120s'.
- Impact: `system:up --timeout N` can hang far beyond N seconds and report a wrong duration; when `next dev` crashes at start-up (bad config, missing build dependency) the developer waits the full 120 s before the tail of app.log is printed.
- Fix: Use real elapsed time and bound each probe, and stop early when the app process is gone: - live_code="$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' "$live" || true)" + live_code="$(curl -s --max-time 5 -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' "$live" || true)" # same for ready and page + app_is_running || { error "Application process exited"; tail -n 120 "$APP_LOG_FILE" || true; return 1; } and compute `elapsed=$((SECONDS - start))` instead of += 2. Verifier on the fix: Wall-clock accounting (`elapsed=$((SECONDS - start))`) and `--max-time` are correct. The early exit `app_is_running || { error ...; return 1; }` as written inside wait_for_runtime is WRONG for `system:verify`: cmd_verify calls the same function, is documented (scripts/README.md:91-92) for a running app, and an app started by hand with `npm run dev` has no PID file, so verify would fail at once. Put the process check only on the `up` path (for example a parameter or a check in cmd_up's caller), not in the shared loop. Cold-compile caveat for --max-time (use ~30 s) is correct. Low is fair (dev [...]
- Fix risk: A cold first compile of /en can exceed 5 s per request on slow machines; choose --max-time generously (30 s) or keep the page probe unbounded but the loop wall-clock bounded. Test with a stub curl on PATH.
- Found by: R5-U26 (W34); candidate H-015
- Resolution: FIXED by T-F20 (batch B4, 2026-10-13): the startup verification counts wall-clock time against --timeout (every curl gets --max-time 30 and the loop ends when the time is used, instead of counting only sleeps), and a dead application ends the wait at once with 'Application process exited' instead of waiting for the full timeout. Evidence: probe RED pass=103 / fail=13 on the pre-task script (cases K1-K3: unbounded curl, 6 calls instead of 3, 15 curl calls for a dead app; fix/logs/T-F20-red.log), GREEN 116/116 (T-F20-green.log: the 79 T-F08 cases, the T-F14 cases and 20 new ones), re-run by the lead on the repo script (sha256 96c91e4a): 116 pass / 0 fail; mutation (early exit also in verify) gives 6 failures. Patch R5-T-F20.patch.

### R-672: `--verbose` (set -x) prints every value loaded from the dotenv files, including secrets, to the terminal
- Severity: Low
- Category: Security
- Status: CONFIRMED
- Location: scripts/system-orchestrator.sh:L854-L856
- Evidence:
  ```
  if (( VERBOSE )); then
      set -x
    fi
  ```
  Independent verifier (W34): main() (L854-856) runs `set -x` when --verbose is given, before load_environment. Executed the verbatim load_environment and validate_database_url under `set -x` in a scratch repo root with a fake .env.local (FAKE-not-a-real-secret-0123456789, URL with password FAKEPASS999): 10 stderr lines contained the fake values, e.g. `+ exports='export FAKE_ADMIN_SECRET='\''FAKE-not-a-real-secret-0123456789'\''`, `+ eval 'export FAKE_ADMIN_SECRET=...`, `++ export DATABASE_URL=postgresql://fakeuser:[fake password]@localhost:5433/site_dev`, `+ [[ -z postgresql://fakeuser:[fake password]@localhost:5433/site_dev ]]` and the node argv line ending with the URL. Opt-in flag (`--verbose` = 'Verbose command tracing' in usage), output goes to the developer's own terminal. Not covered by any REVIEW.md finding.
- Problem: main() enables xtrace before any command runs, so load_environment's `exports="$(...)"` assignment (L264-284) and `eval "$exports"` (L285), whose text is `export KEY='value'` for every key of .env.development.local/.env.local/.env.development/.env, are traced to stderr. Replica of L262-286 verbatim (REPO_ROOT = scratch dir with a fake .env.local containing FAKE-not-a-real-secret-0123456789 and a URL with a fake password) run under `set -x`: 8 stderr lines contain the fake values, e.g. `+ exports='export FAKE_ADMIN_SECRET='\''FAKE-not-a-real-secret-0123456789'\''` and `+ eval 'export FAKE_ADMIN_SECRET=...`. validate_database_url (L309) additionally passes the full DATABASE_URL as a process argument that xtrace prints.
- Impact: A developer who runs `system:up --verbose` to debug and pastes or logs the output exposes ADMIN_JWT_SECRET, GUEST_JWT_SECRET, ADMIN_DASH_SECRET, both peppers, ORIGIN_PROXY_SHARED_SECRET and any AIRBNB_ICAL_URL token that sits in .env.local. The values are development secrets by design, so the damage is limited unless a real value was put there.
- Fix: Keep tracing but silence it around the secret-bearing steps: in load_environment wrap with `{ set +x; } 2>/dev/null` before the `exports=` assignment and restore with `[[ $VERBOSE == 1 ]] && set -x` after the eval; likewise around validate_database_url's node call. Verifier on the fix: The leak is real, but the proposed fix is wrong as written: restoring tracing with `[[ $VERBOSE == 1 ]] && set -x` as the LAST statement of load_environment makes the function return 1 when VERBOSE=0, and under the script's `set -euo pipefail` this aborts every normal run (reproduced on bash 3.2.57: prints 'body', exits 1, never reaches the next line). Use `if (( VERBOSE )); then set -x; fi`. It is also incomplete: DATABASE_URL (with its password) is traced by other lines too (`[[ -z "${DATABASE_URL:-}" ]]` at the start of validate_database_url, node argv), so the quiet region must cover the [...]
- Fix risk: Trace output of those two steps disappears; verify with the same replica that no FAKE value appears on stderr.
- Found by: R5-U26 (W34); candidate H-018
- Resolution: FIXED by T-F08 (batch B2, 2026-10-13): no value of any dotenv key, DATABASE_URL, DIRECT_URL or POSTGRES_* variable reaches stdout, stderr or the `bash -x` trace: the quiet regions cover load_environment, maybe_ensure_pepper, validate_database_url, database_reachable (it no longer takes the URL as an argument), fallback_database_url, start_fallback_database, the URL comparison in prepare_database and T-F01's DIRECT_URL guard; tracing is restored from the saved shell state after each region; a plain run equals the pre-task script (15 commands). Evidence: probe RED 44 pass / 35 fail on the pre-task copy (fix/logs/T-F08-red.log), GREEN 79/79 three times (T-F08-green.log), re-run by the lead on the repo script (sha256 f600d1e8) and by the B2 verifier: 79/79; four verifier mutants all fail the probe. PORT (not a secret) stays visible in the readiness-probe URLs. Patch R5-T-F08.patch.
