### R-674: SECURITY.md incident guidance names only SECURITY_PEPPER and advises 'rehash' of tokens that cannot be rehashed
- Severity: Low
- Category: Security
- Status: CONFIRMED
- Location: SECURITY.md:L36
- Evidence:
  `- If 'SECURITY_PEPPER' is ever leaked, rotate it in your secret store and reissue/rehash any dependent tokens as necessary.`
  Independent verifier (W34): SECURITY.md:L36: '- If `SECURITY_PEPPER` is ever leaked, rotate it in your secret store and reissue/rehash any dependent tokens as necessary.' and L10 names only SECURITY_PEPPER. `grep -n CLAIM_TOKEN_PEPPER SECURITY.md` finds nothing. Code: src/lib/runtime-env-schema.js:L85-L86 requires both `SECURITY_PEPPER` (min 16) and `CLAIM_TOKEN_PEPPER` (min 32); src/lib/portalAuthService.ts:L36 `crypto.createHmac('sha256', requirePepper('CLAIM_TOKEN_PEPPER')).update(rawToken...)` digests every claim grant; src/lib/crypto.ts:L63-L79 `hashSensitive`/`verifySensitive` store/compare sha256(PEPPER:salt:value) of a raw secret the server does not keep, used for refresh tokens (refreshTokenRepository.ts:L300, L329, L394, L526, L629), so existing hashes cannot be re-derived under a new pepper; they simply stop verifying. docs/security/runtime-credential-contract.md:L27-L37 states exactly the effects (refresh tokens no longer verify, in-flight exchange cookies fail once with 401, rate-limit buckets start empty, privacy hashes no longer match, no unconsumed grant can be claimed after a CLAIM_TOKEN_PEPPER rotation). CORRECTION to the finder's problem text: SECURITY.md does point to that contract. L7-L8: 'The maintained production credential map and rotation boundaries are documented in [`docs/security/runtime-credential-contract.md`]'. So the pointer exists at the top; what remains wrong is L36 (omits CLAIM_TOKEN_PEPPER, and 'rehash' is not possible) and L10 (names one pepper). Not a duplicate of R-608 (Fixed in T67): that finding concerned trusted-ingress.md and the missing rotation text in docs/security; its fix added the contract paragraph but left SECURITY.md L36 unchanged (SECURITY.md has no pending diff in git status).
- Problem: SECURITY.md is the entry point for a leak response, and it predates the two-pepper design. Line 10 says 'a server-side secret named SECURITY_PEPPER'. The runtime schema requires a second pepper, CLAIM_TOKEN_PEPPER, with a minimum of 32 characters (src/lib/runtime-env-schema.js:85-86); scripts/ensure-pepper.js:36-38 generates it; and src/lib/portalAuthService.ts:36 uses it for every claim-grant digest. SECURITY.md never mentions it. The advice 'reissue/rehash any dependent tokens' is not possible for the refresh tokens. src/lib/crypto.ts:65-69 and 71-79 store `sha256(PEPPER:salt:value)` of a secret the server never keeps, so these tokens cannot be rehashed; they simply stop verifying. docs/security/runtime-credential-contract.md:27-37 (added by R-608 / T67) says exactly that, but SECURITY.md does not point to it.
- Impact: During an incident the operator reads SECURITY.md, rotates SECURITY_PEPPER, and expects to rehash tokens. The effects the contract lists are missed: every guest's refresh token is invalid, in-flight claim exchange cookies fail once with 401, rate-limit buckets start empty and privacy hashes written before no longer match. A leaked CLAIM_TOKEN_PEPPER has no instruction at all (rotation makes every unconsumed grant unclaimable, so the host must issue new grants).
- Fix: Replace line 36 with: 'If `SECURITY_PEPPER` or `CLAIM_TOKEN_PEPPER` is ever leaked, rotate it in the runtime secret source and restart; the effects of each rotation (refresh tokens, claim exchange cookies, claim grants, rate-limit buckets) are listed in docs/security/runtime-credential-contract.md.' Add CLAIM_TOKEN_PEPPER to line 10. Verifier on the fix: The proposed L36 text and the L10 addition are correct and minimal; since L7-L8 already links the contract, the L36 change can be even smaller. fixRisk correction: scripts/lib/release-policy.mjs:L998 does scan SECURITY.md (activeConfigurationFiles) for the obsolete names JWT_SECRET, SESSION_SECRET, SECURITY_ENC_KEY_HEX(_PREVIOUS) (token split on non-[A-Z0-9_]); the proposed wording contains none of them, so it stays green. scripts/tests/release-policy.test.mjs:L89 only fixture-writes a SECURITY.md stub. Run npm run validate:release-policy once after the edit.
- Fix risk: Documentation only. scripts/lib/release-policy.mjs does not check SECURITY.md markers (`grep -n 'SECURITY.md' scripts/lib/release-policy.mjs` was not needed to be non-empty; run `npm run validate:release-policy` once after the edit).
- Found by: R5-U29a (W34); candidate N-005
- Resolution: DEFERRED-OWNER (economy): not done under the owner's instruction of 2026-10-13 to watch the consumption; specified in decision-D13.json (.runtime/review5/fix/) as task T-F55, resumable on request.

### R-675: Rate-period form: a last night of 9999-12-31 makes validate() throw and the submit does nothing visible
- Severity: Low
- Category: Error handling
- Status: CONFIRMED
- Location: src/app/admin/availability/AdminAvailabilityClient.tsx:L108
- Evidence:
  `body: { startDate: first, endDate: addDays(last, 1), nightlyPriceCents: cents, minimumNights: minimum },`
  Independent verifier (W1a): Read: AdminAvailabilityClient.tsx L106-L109 `body: { startDate: first, endDate: addDays(last, 1), ... }` inside validate(); save() L192-L198 runs `const validated = validate(form);` before the `try {` at L201. calendarDate.ts L18-L23 isoFromUtc throws `RangeError('Date is outside the years 0100-9999')` (L21) when the ISO slice of the instant fails parseIsoDate (year 10000 serialises as '+010000-01-01'); tests/unit/availability-calendar-date.test.ts L74 pins that addDays('9999-12-31', 1) throws. The date inputs have no max (L388, L392). Executed (scratch jsdom vitest on a copy of src, fetch mocked, 3 runs, stable): first night 9999-12-30, last night 9999-12-31, price 85, minimum 1, click 'Add rate period' -> alerts [], statuses [], unhandled rejections ['RangeError: Date is outside the years 0100-9999'], POST calls 0. Sibling guard is real: git diff f7958fa..HEAD adds `earliestCheckOut` with `checkIn === '9999-12-31'` to admin/guests/page.tsx; L108 itself is unchanged since f7958fa. No existing finding: grep of REVIEW.md for '9999-12-31' and 'addDays(last' hits only R-449 (manual bookings, other route); REVIEW.md L430 only notes the last-night conversion is consistent with the server. Not verified: that the unhandledrejection listener (errorReporting.ts L59, created when that module loads; imported only by src/app/error.tsx and src/app/[locale]/error.tsx) is active on /admin/availability.
- Problem: validate() converts the inclusive last night to the exclusive end date with addDays(last, 1). addDays throws a RangeError past 9999-12-31 (calendarDate.ts isoFromUtc). validate() is called in save() at L194 (`const validated = validate(form);`) outside the try block, and save is an async onSubmit handler, so the error becomes an unhandled promise rejection and no feedback is set. The sibling form in src/app/admin/guests/page.tsx got an explicit guard for the same boundary in this delta (earliestCheckOut: `checkIn === '9999-12-31'`). Executed with Node 22.19.0 from a scratch script: addDays(parseIsoDate('9999-12-31'), 1) printed `THROWS RangeError Date is outside the years 0100-9999`. parseIsoDate accepts '9999-12-31' (4-digit year, real day), so the earlier checks in validate() pass for first and last night 9999-12-31 with a valid price and minimum.
- Impact: An admin who types a year of 9999 as the last night (the browser date input allows it) clicks 'Add rate period' and nothing happens: no message, only an unhandledrejection that errorReporter forwards to /api/errors. Rare and harmless (no data is written), but it is a silent dead end in a form whose other errors are all explained.
- Fix: In validate(), before building the body: `if (last === '9999-12-31') return { ok: false, message: 'The last night must be before 9999-12-31.' };` (same guard as earliestCheckOut), and add one case to tests/components/admin-availability.test.tsx that submits last night 9999-12-31 and expects the message. Verifier on the fix: Minimal fix is correct: in validate() return `{ ok: false, message: 'The last night must be before 9999-12-31.' }` when `last === '9999-12-31'` (the guard the sibling form uses), or wrap addDays in try/catch, and add one row to the 'explains %s without calling the API' table in tests/components/admin-availability.test.tsx. Fix risk negligible (client-only message, no API or data change). Low agrees with how R-449 (year typo) was rated, although the trigger (typing year 9999) is very rare; nothing is written.
- Fix risk: None for existing behaviour: only the single boundary date changes. Run tests/components/admin-availability.test.tsx.
- Found by: R5-U2 (W1a); candidate C-001; also found independently by R5-U13 (wave 2a, D-002)
- Resolution: FIXED by T-F27 (batch B5, 2026-10-13): the rate-period form's validate() returns { ok: false, message: 'The last night must be before 9999-12-31.' } for that date, before the request body is built, so the submit shows a message instead of throwing (wording of decision D13 Q6, English-only admin). Evidence: RED 1 failed / 26 passed with an unhandled RangeError 'Date is outside the years 0100-9999' (fix/logs/T-F27-red.log), GREEN 27/27; lead gates B5 all green. Patch R5-T-F27.patch.

- Severity: Low
- Category: Tests
- Status: CONFIRMED
- Location: src/app/admin/guests/page.tsx:L266-L286

### R-679: Passwords longer than 72 bytes are silently truncated by bcrypt, although the claim and sign-in schemas accept 128 characters
- Severity: Low
- Category: Security
- Status: CONFIRMED
- Location: src/app/api/portal/claims/route.ts:L22-L24
- Evidence:
  ```
  phone: z.string().trim().min(8).max(32),
    password: z.string().min(8).max(128),
    remember: z.boolean().optional().default(false),
  ```
  Independent verifier (W1a): Read: claims/route.ts L23 and sessions/route.ts L18 `password: z.string().min(8).max(128)` (UTF-16 code units); UnifiedGuestClient.tsx L276-L277 minLength 8 / maxLength 128; portalAuthService.ts L17 BCRYPT_ROUNDS = 12, L196 `bcrypt.hash(input.password, BCRYPT_ROUNDS)`, L222 and L354 `bcrypt.compare`; no pre-hash. The installed bcrypt 6.0.0 README (node_modules/bcrypt/README.md L41): 'only the first 72 bytes of a string are used. Any extra bytes are ignored when matching passwords. Note that this is not the first 72 characters.' Executed against bcrypt 6.0.0 (cost 4 for speed; truncation does not depend on cost): 100 ASCII chars -> compare(password + 'ZZZ') true, first 72 chars true, first 71 false; 60 Greek letters (120 bytes) -> first 36 letters true, first 35 false; 128 Greek letters (256 bytes) -> first 36 true; a 30-char password is unaffected (exact true, +'X' false). No earlier review mentions it (grep of REVIEW.md, docs, src, tests and the older reviews for '72 byte' and bcrypt truncation: nothing). No authentication bypass: the effective strength stays 72 bytes.
- Problem: Both password schemas allow up to 128 UTF-16 code units (claims/route.ts L23, sessions/route.ts L18; the form input has minLength 8 / maxLength 128 and the placeholder says 'At least 8 characters'). The password is hashed with `bcrypt.hash(input.password, BCRYPT_ROUNDS)` (portalAuthService.ts L196) and checked with `bcrypt.compare` (L222, L354). bcrypt uses only the first 72 bytes of the UTF-8 encoding. Executed against the installed bcrypt 6.0.0 (scratch probe bcrypt-probe.cjs): for a 100-character ASCII password `compare(password + 'ZZZ', hash)` returned true; for 60 Greek letters (120 bytes) `compare(first 72 bytes, hash)` returned true, so only the first 36 characters count; the same for 128 Greek letters (256 bytes). Zod's `.max(128)` counts UTF-16 code units, not bytes, and nothing in the repo mentions the 72-byte limit (grep of REVIEW.md and of the Review 3 REVIEW.md for '72 byte', 'truncat' with bcrypt found nothing).
- Impact: A guest, or a password manager, that creates a passphrase over 72 bytes gets no error but a shorter effective password: 36 characters of Greek text, 72 characters of ASCII. Everything after that point is never checked, so a sign-in with a wrong tail succeeds, and the 5-per-15-minutes limiter is the only bound on guessing the prefix. This is no authentication bypass and does not touch typical 8-30 character passwords; the defect is a misleading limit and a silent lossy conversion of the credential.
- Fix: Put the byte limit where passwords are created, the claims schema: `password: z.string().min(8).refine((value) => Buffer.byteLength(value, 'utf8') <= 72, { error: 'Use at most 72 bytes (Greek letters count as 2).' })`, and mirror it in `isGuestFormValid` (`new TextEncoder().encode(password).length <= 72`) with a hint under the field. Keep `.max(128)` on the sign-in schema (sessions/route.ts L18) so existing longer passwords still work. Alternative with no visible limit: pre-hash new passwords and version the stored hash, which needs a migration path. Verifier on the fix: Neither fix is free. (a) Enforce a 72-byte limit where a password is created (claims route: `.refine((value) => Buffer.byteLength(value, 'utf8') <= 72, ...)` with a clear message) and leave sign-in unchanged so existing hashes keep verifying; the form's maxLength={128} counts characters and a Greek passphrase hits 72 bytes at 36 letters, so the hint text must change. (b) Pre-hashing (SHA-256, then bcrypt) would invalidate every stored hash. The zero-risk alternative is a comment or doc note that only the first 72 bytes count. Low is fair for a misleading limit (silent lossy conversion of a [...]
- Fix risk: Existing accounts whose password is longer than 72 bytes could no longer pass the claims schema when they attach a second booking (their first 72 bytes would still match). Sign-in is unchanged. Run tests/unit/guest-access-reset.test.ts, tests/routes/portal-sign-in-rate-limit.test.ts, tests/components/guest-claim-errors.test.tsx and add a 73-byte case.
- Found by: R5-U1 (W1a); candidate C-025
- Resolution: DECLINED by decision D13 (2026-10-13, the owner's delegate): No exploitable weakness: the first 72 bytes carry far more entropy than any guessing budget, and sign-in with the full password keeps working. A 72-byte cap would reject Greek passphrases above 36 letters, and pre-hashing needs a versioned migration of every stored hash; neither is worth the risk to the claim flow (owner may ask for the pre-hash).

### R-680: A failed Logout request shows the 'Token refresh failed' banner, and its 'Retry now' button retries the refresh, not the logout
- Severity: Low
- Category: Bug
- Status: CONFIRMED
- Location: src/components/AdminSessionManager.tsx:L102-L110
- Evidence:
  ```
  async function logout() {
      try {
        const response = await internalFetch('/api/admin/logout', { method: 'POST' });
        if (!response.ok) throw new Error('logout failed');
        window.location.reload();
      } catch {
        setStatus('error');
      }
    }
  ```
  Independent verifier (W34): src/components/AdminSessionManager.tsx:L102-L110 logout() catch calls setStatus('error'); L119-L123 render `{status === 'error' && ... Token refresh failed. You may need to re-login. ... <button onClick={() => retryRef.current()}>Retry now`; retryRef.current is set to `() => void refresh()` at L86. Executed (scratch copy of the component test, W34-VE/t_asm.test.tsx, config under scratchpad): fetch('/api/admin/logout') -> 500: after clicking 'Logout' `screen.getByText(/Token refresh failed/u)` is found with 0 refresh calls; same for a rejected fetch (TypeError); clicking 'Retry now' makes exactly 1 POST /api/admin/refresh and 0 further logout calls, the banner disappears and 'Session: ok' shows. Server side: src/app/api/admin/logout/route.ts revokes the session and clears the cookie only inside the handler, so a 5xx leaves the cookie valid. No test clicks Logout: `grep -rn "'Logout'\|Retry now\|admin/logout" tests` only hits tests/routes/admin-logout.test.ts (route, not component). Not in REVIEW.md (R-476 touches the same JSX lines but only the animate-pulse class and is DECLINED).
- Problem: logout() reuses the refresh status: on a non-OK or failed POST /api/admin/logout it calls setStatus('error'), and L119-L123 then render 'Token refresh failed. You may need to re-login.' with a 'Retry now' button wired to retryRef.current (= refresh(), L86). Executed in a scratch copy of admin-session-manager.test.tsx (cwd /Users/pvasilakis/site, config under scratchpad/review5/R5-U30/run2): expiresAt 120 min away, fetch('/api/admin/logout') answers 500, click 'Logout' -> screen.getByText(/Token refresh failed/u) found, test passed. No test covers the Logout button (grep -rn "'Logout'\|Retry now" tests: no hit besides the route test tests/routes/admin-logout.test.ts, which does not render the component).
- Impact: When the logout request fails (network error or 5xx) the admin reads a message about a token refresh that never ran. 'Retry now' re-runs the refresh, which usually succeeds and clears the banner, so the admin can believe the logout went through while the admin cookie is still valid on a shared machine. Realistic but rare (only when the logout call itself fails).
- Fix: Track the logout failure separately instead of reusing status: add `const [logoutFailed, setLogoutFailed] = useState(false);`, in logout() clear it at the start and call `setLogoutFailed(true)` in the catch (instead of setStatus('error')), and render `{logoutFailed && <div className="admin-session-error ..." role="alert">Logout failed. Try again.</div>}` without the Retry-now button. Add a component test: logout answers 500 -> 'Logout failed' shown, 'Token refresh failed' absent. Verifier on the fix: Correct and minimal: a separate `logoutFailed` state with its own role=alert text, no Retry-now button. Keep the new markup on existing admin token classes (tests/unit/admin-css-tokens.test.ts scans AdminSessionManager.tsx for palette utilities) and do not re-add animate-pulse (R-476 declined/motion gate). Fix risk is fair: only the 'Session: error' label after a failed logout changes. Q-013's 'Logout failure shows an error' test depends on this fix.
- Fix risk: Small. The 'Session: error' label no longer appears after a failed logout (arguably correct). Re-run tests/components/admin-session-manager.test.tsx; the existing refresh-failure test still expects the 'Token refresh failed' text for refresh errors.
- Found by: R5-U30 (W34); candidate Q-007
- Resolution: DEFERRED-OWNER (economy): not done under the owner's instruction of 2026-10-13 to watch the consumption; specified in decision-D13.json (.runtime/review5/fix/) as task T-F29, resumable on request.

### R-681: R-434 fix attributes the restart to a booked night that lies beyond the 30-night cap, so the cap explanation is withheld
- Severity: Low
- Category: Logic
- Status: CONFIRMED
- Location: src/components/availability/AvailabilityPlanner.tsx:L304-L305
- Evidence:
  ```
  // Without a booked night in between, only the limit of MAX_STAY_NIGHTS can have ended the check-out days.
          const pastMax = crossed === undefined && day > checkIn && nightsBetween(checkIn, day) > MAX_STAY_NIGHTS;
  ```
  Independent verifier (W2): Read: AvailabilityPlanner.tsx handleSelect L303-L306 `const crossed = day > checkIn ? eachNight(checkIn, day).find((night) => nightCodeOn(night, today, nights) === 'b') : undefined; ... const pastMax = crossed === undefined && day > checkIn && nightsBetween(checkIn, day) > MAX_STAY_NIGHTS;` and stayQuote.ts maxCheckOut L100-L114 (`nights < MAX_STAY_NIGHTS && checkOut < horizonEnd && !blockedNights.has(checkOut)`), so the window ends at the first blocked night OR after 30 nights; blockedNights = bookedNights() = exactly the 'b' nights, same set as nightCodeOn === 'b'. Executed my own jsdom reproduction (scratchpad review5/W2-VB/keep/cap.test.tsx, real AvailabilityPlanner, today 2026-10-01, rate 80 EUR, check-in 2026-11-02, click 2026-12-25): (A) only 2026-12-20 booked -> afterCheckIn 'at the latest Wed 2 Dec 2026'; afterClick 'Sun 20 Dec 2026 is booked, so Fri 25 Dec 2026 is your new check-in.Now choose your check-out day, at the latest Sun 24 Jan 2027.' (no 30-night text); (B) nothing booked -> 'A stay can be at most 30 nights. For a longer stay, call us or send a WhatsApp message.'; (C) booked exactly at check-in+30 (2 Dec) -> booked note; (D) booked inside window (10 Nov) -> booked note. So the defect is real but narrow: the booked-night note is still TRUE (a stay across 20 Dec is impossible regardless of the cap), it is only incomplete; the finder's sentence that the wording 'suggests the stay would work without that booking' is an overreach, and the user who hits it cannot get that stay anyway. Existing tests (availability-planner.test.tsx L168-L210) cover only crossing-without-cap and cap-without-booked. Not in REVIEW.md (grep pastMax/withheld: no hit); R-434 is its FIXED predecessor (Resolution T23) and does not cover this combination.
- Problem: The T23 fix assumes that a booked night between the check-in and the clicked day is what ended the check-out window, and shows the max_nights note only when no booked night is found. maxCheckOut (stayQuote.ts L100-L114) stops at the first blocked night OR after MAX_STAY_NIGHTS, whichever comes first. When the cap is the binding limit and a booked night lies further away (more than 30 nights after the check-in), eachNight(checkIn, day).find(...) still returns that far booked night, `crossed` is defined and `pastMax` is false. The note then names a booked night that is not what ended the window and never mentions the 30-night limit or the phone/WhatsApp hint. validateStay checks the cap before blocked nights (stayQuote.ts L117-L119 and L129-L130), so the click note and the validation order disagree. Executed scratch test (scratchpad review5/R5-U13/cap-and-booked.test.tsx, availability with only 2026-12-20 booked, rate 80 EUR all year): click 2 Nov, then 25 Dec. Output: afterCheckIn = "Now choose your check-out day, at the latest Wed 2 Dec 2026."; afterClick25Dec = "Sun 20 Dec 2026 is booked, so Fri 25 Dec 2026 is your new check-in.Now choose your check-out day, at the latest Sun 24 Jan 2027.", hash #checkin=2026-12-25, note class ui-callout--warning. 20 Dec is 48 nights after 2 Nov, so the window had ended on 2 Dec because of the cap.
- Impact: A guest who wants a long winter stay (2 Nov to 25 Dec, 53 nights) while any later night is booked is told only that a night is booked and that the click became a new check-in. The guest does not learn that stays are capped at 30 nights or that a longer stay can be arranged by phone or WhatsApp, which is the purpose of R-434. The booked-night wording also suggests that the stay would work without that booking.
- Fix: Treat the booked night as the reason only when it is what ends the window (checkOutDays.last), otherwise fall back to the cap check. In handleSelect: `const firstBooked = day > checkIn ? eachNight(checkIn, day).find((night) => nightCodeOn(night, today, nights) === 'b') : undefined; const crossed = firstBooked !== undefined && firstBooked === checkOutDays?.last ? firstBooked : undefined; const pastMax = crossed === undefined && day > checkIn && nightsBetween(checkIn, day) > MAX_STAY_NIGHTS; select({ checkIn: day, checkOut: null }, crossed ?? null, pastMax);` and fix the comment above pastMax. Verifier on the fix: The proposed fix is correct. Treat the booked night as the reason only when `firstBooked === checkOutDays?.last`, else fall back to the cap check. I derived that firstBooked !== last implies firstBooked > checkIn+30 (otherwise last = firstBooked), hence day > checkIn+30 and pastMax is true, so exactly one of the two notes is chosen; the existing crossing test (7 Oct, click 12 Oct, booked 10 Oct) keeps its message because last = 10 Oct. fixRisk Low is fair (only the note text changes; add one regression test with a booked night more than 30 nights after the check-in). Also fix the comment [...]
- Fix risk: Low; only the note changes. The existing crossing test (check-in 7 Oct, click 12 Oct, booked 10 Oct) keeps its message because the first booked night equals checkOutDays.last. Add a regression test with a booked night more than 30 nights after the check-in (for example 2026-12-20: click 2026-11-02, then 2026-12-25 expects the max_nights text and no 'is booked' text). The case of a booked night exactly at check-in + 30 coincides with the cap and keeps the crossing message.
- Found by: R5-U13 (W2); candidate D-001
- Resolution: DEFERRED-OWNER (economy): not done under the owner's instruction of 2026-10-13 to watch the consumption; specified in decision-D13.json (.runtime/review5/fix/) as task T-F26, resumable on request.

We'll confirm availability as soon as possible.' and 'reload calls after a second advance(0): 1' (0 before it, because the timer is armed after the act flush, then fires at 0 ms). The existing T69 tests (checkin-wifi.test.tsx:207-238) close the form only with 'Cancel'. After the reload GET /api/check-in/arrival-request restores the pending request panel ('Latest request Pending ... Your request has been received'), so only the in-page confirmation/error callout is lost; no data loss, no loop (wifiReloadMissed resets with the reload).
- Problem: R-619 (T69) arms a 'missed' reload whenever the arrival form was open while the disclosure time was still ahead (wifiReloadMissed.current = true, L512) and the form is closed after that time. The task only tested closing the form with Cancel. The form also closes through handleSubmitArrivalRequest, which calls setIsRequestingArrival(false) and then setArrivalRequestSuccess(ui.requestSent) (or setArrivalRequestError(ui.requestAlreadyPending)) in the same batch. The effect then runs with delay <= 0 and the ref true, so reloadIn = Math.max(0, negative) = 0 and window.location.reload() is scheduled for the next tick, right after the confirmation is rendered. Reproduced with a scratch vitest file under the scratchpad (not in the repo): CheckInInfo with wifiAvailableAt = now+5s, open 'Request different arrival time', advance 10 s, mock the POST /api/check-in/arrival-request as 200, click 'Send request'. The existing T69 tests only close the form with 'Cancel', so they do not cover this path.
- Impact: A guest who keeps the arrival-request form open across the Wi-Fi disclosure time (the exact case R-619 targets) and then sends the request sees the page reload immediately. The 'Request sent' or 'request already pending' message is lost in the same tick. The request itself is stored, because the POST has completed before the reload. The Wi-Fi details do appear after the reload. The defect is a lost confirmation, with no data loss and no reload loop.
- Fix: Give the owed reload a floor, so a message set by the submit stays readable, for example `const reloadIn = Math.max(wifiReloadMissed.current ? 4_000 : 0, delay + 1_000);`. Alternatively, in the missed case, re-fetch the preferences instead of reloading. Add a case to tests/components/checkin-wifi.test.tsx: open the form before the time, submit after it, and assert that the success text is present at the moment of the reload. Verifier on the fix: Correct diagnosis. Smallest fix: when the form was closed by a completed submit (success or request_already_pending) do not reload at 0 ms, e.g. keep a short minimum delay in the missed branch (`Math.max(delay + 1_000, wifiReloadMissed.current ? 4_000 : 0)`) or arm the reload only while neither arrivalRequestSuccess nor arrivalRequestError is set and re-arm when they clear; R-619's own alternative (re-fetch preferences instead of reload) loses the server-side session renewal that R-391's comment relies on. fixRisk: the T69 tests expect an immediate reload after Cancel, so a delay needs the [...]
- Fix risk: The existing T69 case 'reloads once when the arrival request form is closed after the disclosure time' advances only 1_000 ms after Cancel and would have to advance by the floor, so one existing assertion changes. The cases 'reloads once, one second after the Wi-Fi details become available' and 'reloads after the form is closed again before the disclosure time' are not affected (ref false, or reloadIn already above the floor). The loop guard (a page loaded after the time never reloads) must stay.
- Found by: R5-X3, R5-U4 (W1a); candidate C-006
- Resolution: FIXED by T-F06 (batch B1, 2026-10-13): no reload any more, so a successful arrival-request submit keeps its confirmation message and the form text survives the reveal (the wifiReloadMissed and isRequestingArrival gating are removed). Evidence as R-684 (tests 'a form open across the reveal keeps its text' and 'a submit after the reveal keeps its success message', two timings).

### R-684: The automatic Wi-Fi reload is unconditional: offline at the reveal moment it replaces the open check-in page with the offline page
- Severity: Low
- Category: Error handling
- Status: CONFIRMED
- Location: src/components/CheckInInfo.tsx:L518
- Evidence:
  `const timer = window.setTimeout(() => window.location.reload(), reloadIn);`
  Independent verifier (W1b): Code read: CheckInInfo.tsx:518 `const timer = window.setTimeout(() => window.location.reload(), reloadIn);` has no connectivity check. public/sw.js: PRIVATE_PAGE_PREFIXES contains '/en/check-in','/el/check-in'; isNetworkOnlyPage() is true for them, so networkFirstPage never stores them and its `catch` returns `cache.match('/${locale}/offline')`. Executed: (1) the unchanged public/sw.js in a node vm with a rejecting fetch: online '/en/check-in' -> '200 <html>live check-in page</html>'; offline '/en/check-in', '/el/check-in', '/en/guest' -> '200 <html>OFFLINE PAGE</html>'. (2) Real headless Chrome against the dev server (loopback only; the dev PwaManager cleanup neutralised in the page; the same sw.js registered manually, page controlled; page and service-worker target both offline via CDP; document URL /en/check-in; `location.reload()` = the call the timer makes): log 'nav request /en/check-in', 'nav response /en/check-in status=200 fromSW=true', final text "Skip to content Dolce Far Niente YOUR STAY You're offline Pages you opened before are still here. When the connection is back, tap Retry." Without a service worker the same reload shows Chrome's error page (ERR_INTERNET_DISCONNECTED). Not run: the timer itself firing on an authenticated production page at a real reveal moment (same reload call, same outcome by construction).
- Problem: The timer callback calls window.location.reload() with no connectivity check. A reload is a navigation request, which public/sw.js L197-L199 sends to networkFirstPage (L146-L167). For /en/check-in and /el/check-in (PRIVATE_PAGE_PREFIXES, L30-L32) isNetworkOnlyPage is true, so no cached copy exists, and a rejected fetch is answered with the cached /{locale}/offline page (L159-L165). Executed: scratch/sw-offline-check.mjs loads the unchanged public/sw.js in a vm with a fetch that rejects: `offline /en/check-in -> 200 <html>OFFLINE PAGE</html>`; with the network back: `200 <html>live check-in page</html>`. Not run in a real browser, so the full chain (page open, device offline at reveal + 1 s, service worker controlling the page) is reasoned, not observed. Before T13 the page was never reloaded automatically; PwaManager's own reload (PwaManager.tsx L88-L110) is user-initiated.
- Impact: The reveal is 24 h before check-in, when the guest is likely travelling with spotty signal. A tab that is offline at that moment loses the address, house rules and emergency numbers it had on screen (the page is not cached offline by design) until the guest taps Retry while online. Low: recoverable, rare combination.
- Fix: Guard the reload: if navigator.onLine === false do not reload and re-arm on the window 'online' event; or refresh by fetch (re-run the preferences GET and redirect to /portal/refresh on 401) instead of navigating, which keeps the page and also makes the wifiReloadMissed workaround unnecessary. Verifier on the fix: Either option works: navigator.onLine === false guard plus re-arm on 'online' narrows it (onLine can be true without connectivity); the refetch variant (see B-003) removes the case entirely. fixRisk is fair; keep the loop guard. Combine with B-003 in one task.
- Fix risk: navigator.onLine can be true without connectivity, so the guard narrows the case but does not remove it. The fetch variant needs its own 401 handling and tests. Keep the loop guard (a page loaded after the time must not retry).
- Found by: R5-U15 (W1b); candidate B-004
- Resolution: FIXED by T-F06 (batch B1, 2026-10-13): the Wi-Fi details are refetched (GET /api/check-in/preferences, one second after wifiAvailableAt) instead of reloading the page; the refetch updates only the three Wi-Fi fields, a 401 replaces once to /portal/refresh with the same guard as the submit path, and a failed fetch retries once on 'online'. Evidence: RED 12 failed / 15 passed (fix/logs/T-F06-red.log), GREEN 27/27; B1 verifier PASS-WITH-NOTES (R-792: four mutants survive). The real-phone part stays with the owner (deferOwner list). Patch R5-T-F06.patch.

### R-685: Reveal fix R-379 leaves a dead zone: a [data-reveal] block in the bottom 35 % of the viewport stays at opacity 0 after any non-scroll change (resize, zoom-out, DevTools, orientation, late scroll restoration)
- Severity: Low
- Category: Bug
- Status: SUSPECTED
- Location: src/components/home/HomeRevealObserver.tsx:L41-L56
- Evidence:
  ```
  let frame = requestAnimationFrame(() => {
        frame = requestAnimationFrame(() => {
          for (const [target, observer] of owners) {
  ```
  Independent verifier (W1a): HomeRevealObserver.tsx:41 `{ rootMargin: `0px 0px -${Math.round(threshold * 100)}% 0px` }` and L48-56 the `top >= window.innerHeight` pass runs once, two rAFs after mount; FactCounters.tsx:54-59 is the same. No resize/visualViewport listener exists in either file (read both completely). The mechanism is therefore real by the IntersectionObserver spec: a block first brought on-screen by a viewport that grew (window maximised, DevTools closed) with top > 0.65*innerHeight is not isIntersecting and stays `:not(.is-in)` (motion.css:185-186, 343 `.host .letter:not(.is-in) { opacity: 0; }`) until the next scroll. BUT the finder's headline example is wrong: the fact strip is revealed by the load pass and `is-in` is never removed (observer.unobserve after add), so zooming out does not give an empty fact card. Also, a block whose top sits in the bottom 35 % is hidden by design while scrolling (HomeRevealObserver.tsx:5 'reveal once the element's top is past this share'). Only the state 'hidden while visible with no scroll yet' after a viewport growth is new, and it self-heals on the first scroll. tests/components/home-reveal-observer.test.tsx uses a stub IntersectionObserver (lines 93-170), so real geometry is untested. Not reproduced: a real browser is not allowed in this round.
- Problem: R-379 moved the trigger to `rootMargin: '0px 0px -35% 0px'` (L41), so an element only intersects once its top is above the 65 % line; the bottom 35 % of the viewport is a band in which a block is on screen but not intersecting. The class of problem was patched only for the moment of load: the compensating pass `top < window.innerHeight` runs exactly once, two frames after mount (L48-56), and the same holds for FactCounters.tsx L54-59. Any later event that leaves a not-yet-revealed block in that band without moving it above the 65 % line does not fire the IntersectionObserver (isIntersecting stays false, so no callback): a viewport that grows (browser zoom-out, DevTools closed, window maximised, rotation to a taller viewport), or a scroll restoration or hash jump that lands after the second frame. Under data-motion=full motion.css then keeps `.facts:not(.is-in) .fact`, `.host .letter:not(.is-in)`, `.teaser .nights:not(.is-in) .night`, `.relief-wrap:not(.is-in) ...` at opacity 0 and `.window:not(.is-in)` behind closed shutters while they are visible. tests/components/home-reveal-observer.test.tsx uses a stub IntersectionObserver and fake rects, so it cannot show the real-browser rootMargin geometry.
- Impact: A desktop visitor who zooms out (100 % to 50 %: the viewport grows from 800 to 1600 CSS px) sees an empty fact card, an invisible host letter or hidden night cells in the lower third of the screen until the first scroll moves them above the 65 % line; the same after toggling DevTools or maximising the window. It also yields blank bands in any browser audit or screenshot that resizes the viewport after load (audit:responsive:ux). Self-healing on the next scroll, hence Low. Not reproduced: no browser and no dev server were allowed.
- Fix: Factor the load-time pass into a function and call it also from a passive `resize` listener (rAF-throttled, removed in the cleanup): reveal every non-`is-in` target whose `getBoundingClientRect().top < window.innerHeight`, and `unobserve` it from its owner. Do the same for FactCounters' `start()` (it is already idempotent via `started`). Verifier on the fix: Direction is fair but the problem is smaller than stated: repeat the existing `top < innerHeight` pass on a debounced `resize` (and `visualViewport` resize) using the `owners` map already in the effect, and the same for FactCounters; remove the listeners in cleanup. fixRisk: low, blocks reveal slightly earlier than the scroll trigger after a resize; the two-frame tests need a resize case. Severity could drop to Nit (cosmetic, self-healing, narrow trigger).
- Fix risk: A resize reveals blocks earlier than the 65 % rule (like the load-time pass already does). Extend tests/components/home-reveal-observer.test.tsx with a resize case (dispatch `resize` after placing a target between 0.65 and 1.0 of innerHeight) and check the listener is removed on unmount and under StrictMode.
- To confirm: In a real browser at 1280x800 with motion=full: load /en at scroll 0, then enlarge the window or zoom out and check whether a [data-reveal] block that was below the fold, now within the lower 35 % of the viewport, has `is-in` without any scroll (audit:responsive:ux or puppeteer against a local production build; loopback only). Run request: Lead (loopback production build + headless Chrome): load /en with data-motion=full at 1280x800, then page.setViewport({width:1280,height:1600}) without scrolling and read getComputedStyle(.host .letter).opacity and whether .letter has class is-in
- Found by: R5-U4 (W1a); candidate C-004
- Resolution: DEFERRED-OWNER (economy): SUSPECTED; the reproduction command is recorded in decision-D13.json (leadReproduce) and was not run under the owner's instruction of 2026-10-13 to watch the consumption; a confirmed reproduction would become the conditional task T-F64.

### R-688: The update banner compares the running worker's version with a stored baseline that only the Refresh button advances: after a waiting worker activates by itself, the next visit offers it again as an update
- Severity: Low
- Category: Logic
- Status: CONFIRMED
- Location: src/components/PwaManager.tsx:L143-L146
- Evidence:
  ```
  const banner = document.getElementById('update-banner');
          const versionChanged = storedVersion !== newVersion;
          const buildChanged = !!newBuild && newBuild !== storedBuild;
          if (banner && (versionChanged || buildChanged)) {
  ```
  Independent verifier (W1b): Read PwaManager.tsx L129-170: the listener never looks at e.source; with stored app-version present (L135, written only at L139-140 first message and L110-111 Refresh) and a message whose version/build differ, L144-146 sets versionChanged/buildChanged and L160-168 sets display:flex unless the key was dismissed. L45 posts REQUEST_VERSION to navigator.serviceWorker.controller on every load; sw.js L138-143 answers with its own VERSION/BUILD. Chromium lifecycle run (real sw.js, A=v0.1.1 build probe-a active, page registers B=v0.1.2 build probe-b -> waiting): same document: reply from probe-a has sourceIsController true, reply from probe-b has sourceIsWaiting true. After the page was closed and a new page opened: controller scriptURL ...v=0.1.2&build=probe-b, registration.waiting null, caches ['guest-guide-probe-b'], and the controller answered {"type":"RUNTIME_VERSION","meta":{"version":"0.1.2","build":"probe-b"}} with sourceIsController true. With localStorage app-version 0.1.1 that message goes through the same branch tests/components/pwa-manager.test.tsx L252-259 already exercises (banner flex, 'Update available: 1.0.0 -> 2.0.0'). Dismiss stores update-dismissed-version only (L116-124), so a dismissed banner stays hidden for that key but app-version stays old. I did not run the jsdom component scenario myself; it follows from the code paths above. No earlier finding.
- Problem: The handler cannot tell a message of a waiting worker from one of the worker that already controls the page. app-version and app-build are written only in the first-message branch (L139-L140) and in the Refresh handler (L110-L111); nothing records the version of a worker that took over by itself. Real Chromium lifecycle run (scratch browser-update.cjs): A active, the page registers B (installed, waiting), every tab is closed, a new page opens: controller = sw.js?v=0.1.2&build=probe-b, registration.waiting = null, caches ["guest-guide-probe-b"], and the controller answers REQUEST_VERSION with {"type":"RUNTIME_VERSION","meta":{"version":"0.1.2","build":"probe-b"}}; PwaManager asks the controller on every load (L45). The real PwaManager in jsdom with a worker double that answers like that (scratch vt/tests/pwa-scenarios.test.tsx): stored app-version 0.1.1 / app-build probe-a, controller reply 0.1.2 / probe-b, registration.waiting null -> #update-banner display flex, text "A new version is ready: 0.1.1 -> 0.1.2". In Chromium MessageEvent.source is identical to navigator.serviceWorker.controller for the active worker's reply and to registration.waiting for the waiting worker's reply (scratch browser-source.cjs).
- Impact: A guest sees the (valid) banner after a deploy, ignores it and closes the tab; the browser activates the new worker. On every later visit the banner says an update is ready although nothing is pending; Refresh only reloads. Dismiss records the key, but app-version stays old, so later banners name the wrong old version. Cosmetic, but it makes the banner untrustworthy.
- Fix: After `if (!newVersion) return;` treat a message from the controlling worker as the baseline: `if (e.source && e.source === swContainer?.controller) { writeStored(() => localStorage.setItem('app-version', newVersion)); if (newBuild) writeStored(() => localStorage.setItem('app-build', newBuild)); return; }`. The waiting worker's message still reaches the banner logic. Give the test helper runtimeVersionMessage a source. Verifier on the fix: The proposed `e.source === swContainer?.controller` baseline rule is correct for the observed lifecycle (controller reply and waiting reply have different source objects, measured in Chromium) and leaves the waiting-worker path untouched; unconditionally writing app-build for a controller message is also consistent with the first-message branch. Only Chromium was checked (Safari/Firefox identity untested); if identity fails there the old behaviour remains, so the risk is low as stated. The test helper needs a source, as proposed. Severity Low agreed (cosmetic, but it makes the banner [...]
- Fix risk: Verified only in Chromium (source identity); Safari and Firefox not tested. The first-message path (no controller yet) is unchanged. Existing tests send messages without a source and fall through to the old logic.
- Found by: R5-U16 (W1b); candidate B-014
- Resolution: FIXED by T-F21 (batch B4, 2026-10-13): PwaManager takes the version baseline from the message of the RUNNING worker (the message whose source is the page's controller), so an activated waiting worker no longer offers itself again as an update on the next visit; the Refresh message of a waiting worker still raises the banner. Evidence: RED pwa-manager.test.tsx 1 failed ('expected flex to be empty': the controller message was offered as an update; fix/logs/T-F21-red-pwa.log), GREEN 72/72 over pwa-manager, service-worker and privacy-storage-inventory (T-F21-green.log); source identity was verified only in Chromium (Safari and Firefox untested). Patch R5-T-F21.patch.

### R-689: Clicking 'Contact' a second time does nothing once the URL already ends in #contact (header, menu and footer nav)

Next 16.3.8, node_modules/next/dist/client/components/segment-cache/navigation.js:385-387 `const onlyHashChange = ... url.pathname === oldUrl.pathname && url.search === oldUrl.search && url.hash !== oldUrl.hash;` and :439 `forceScroll = true` only inside the `else if (onlyHashChange)` branch, so a click on a link equal to the current URL creates no new segment and scrolls nothing. Executed (puppeteer 25.12.0, Chrome 154, dev server, loopback only; W2-VA/d013.cjs, /en 1440x900): header Contact click: scrollY 0 -> 6530, URL /en#contact, `#contact` present once (DIV, the footer block); scrollTo(0,0); header Contact again: scrollY stays 0 after 1.8 s (contact block top 6964 px). Control, same state: a native `<a href='#contact'>` click: scrollY 6530. W2-VA/d013b.cjs at 390x844: menu Contact -> 7052; scroll to top; menu Contact again -> 0 (menu closes, URL unchanged); hard load /en#contact (scrollY 7052), scrollTo(0,0), menu Contact -> 0. The footer nav link is the same `<Link>`, not clicked separately. Not covered by REVIEW.md (grep -F '#contact': 0 hits); not a declined item.
- Problem: The 'Contact' item is a next/link to `/{l}#contact` in SiteHeader (L92-L99), MobileMenu (L77-L90) and, through footerNavLinks, SiteFooter. Next only scrolls to the hash when `url.hash !== oldUrl.hash` (node_modules/next/dist/client/components/segment-cache/navigation.js L385-L388: `url.pathname === oldUrl.pathname && url.search === oldUrl.search && url.hash !== oldUrl.hash`), so a click on a link whose full URL equals the current URL does not scroll, whereas a native anchor would. Executed in puppeteer (1440x900, dev server): on /en click header 'Contact' -> /en#contact, scrollY 0 -> 6508 (the footer contact block, id present once); scrollTo(0,0); click 'Contact' again -> scrollY 0 after 1.5 s; again at the bottom -> still 0. The mobile-menu path at 390 px behaves the same (after a first jump, scrolled to top, 'Contact' from the menu: scrollY 0, contact block at y 7358). The same happens after a hard load of /en#contact. The hash target is now the footer (9d4784f), so 'jump to the bottom, scroll back up, press Contact again' is the normal use; the behaviour predates that commit (the ContactBand had the same id).
- Impact: After the first use, the nav's 'Contact' link silently does nothing while the URL carries #contact; the guest has to scroll by hand. Other links to `/{l}#contact` (ApartmentCta, ErrorSummary, guest page) are affected the same way only from the home page.

Verifier on the fix: Correct and minimal: next/link calls the user's onClick first and skips the navigation when `e.defaultPrevented` (node_modules/next/dist/client/app-dir/link.js:327-336), so `preventDefault()` plus `document.getElementById('contact')?.scrollIntoView()` when location.pathname + location.hash equals the href works at the three call sites (the menu already runs close()). FixRisk is fair: jsdom has no scroll, so assert the scrollIntoView call with a mock and re-check in a browser. Declining it as framework behaviour is also defensible.
- Fix risk: Three call sites; the menu also needs close() to run (it already does in onClick). Add component tests with the mocked pathname/hash; verify in a browser because jsdom has no scroll.
- Found by: R5-U11 (W2); candidate D-013
- Resolution: FIXED by T-F22 (batch B4, 2026-10-13): a same-hash helper scrollToCurrentHash in shellLinks.ts (used by the header, the menu and the footer): when the click lands on the link that points to the hash already in the URL, the default navigation is prevented and the target is scrolled into view; it also leaves modified clicks (ctrl, meta, shift, alt), non-primary buttons, prevented events and a missing #id target alone; the menu closes first because an open menu locks the scroll. Evidence: RED 20 failed / 67 passed (fix/logs/T-F22-red.log), GREEN 87/87; lead check in real Chromium on the production build (fix/logs/B4-lead-shell.log): at 1440 px (header, footer) and 390 px (menu, footer), full and reduced motion, the second click after scrolling away brings #contact into view again (top 456, 434, 328 and 306 px both times); the first click is unchanged. D13's remark that CSS scroll-behavior keeps reduced motion instant does not apply: the repo sets no scroll-behavior, scrollIntoView() is always instant. Patch R5-T-F22.patch.

### R-690: A failed sign-out is silent: the menu closes, nothing is shown, and the guest stays signed in
- Severity: Low
- Category: Error handling
- Status: CONFIRMED
- Location: src/components/shell/SiteHeader.tsx:L65-L70

Executed in headless Chromium (repo puppeteer, loopback-only args, dev server on http://localhost:3000, /api/portal/sessions fulfilled as {authenticated:true,checkinEnabled:true}, /api/portal/logout intercepted): 390x844 /en/apartment with logout 500 -> menu Sign out present, after click dialog closed (open=false), URL still /en/apartment, live regions only 'An update is available/Refresh', 'status/polite:Online', empty 'status/polite:' (no new text), reopening the menu still offers 'Sign out'; only console traces `[WARN] internalFetch non-OK response ... 500` and `[ERROR] Guest logout failed`. Same with the request aborted (network failure): URL unchanged, Sign out still offered. Control with logout 204: URL becomes /en and Sign out disappears. Also 1440x900 /en/stay (header Sign out button, logout 500): URL unchanged, button still present, no feedback. ToastProvider wraps SiteHeader in src/app/[locale]/layout.tsx L41-L43 and useToast throws outside the provider (Toast.tsx L57-L61), as the finder says. REVIEW.md: R-537 (FIXED, tests only) mentions this branch but only as a regression hazard; the missing user feedback is not raised anywhere (grep handleSignOut|Guest logout failed|still signed in).
- Problem: useGuestSession.signOut() returns false when POST /api/portal/logout is not ok or throws (src/hooks/useGuestSession.ts L54-L62); handleSignOut has no else branch, and the mobile-menu button closes the dialog before calling it (MobileMenu.tsx L122-L125). The only trace is logger.error. This is the only client call site of signOut (grep 'signOut(' src: SiteHeader.tsx L66 and the hook). Executed in puppeteer at 390 px with /api/portal/sessions answered 200 {authenticated:true,checkinEnabled:true} and /api/portal/logout answered 500 by request interception (loopback only): after clicking 'Sign out' the dialog was closed, URL still /en/apartment, the live regions still held only the 'Online' status text, and 'Sign out' was still offered on reopening; with logout answering 200 the URL became /en and 'Sign out' disappeared.

It needs one new user-facing string in both locales (src/i18n/domains/common.ts ui block next to signOut), which is owner-approved-copy territory, so the wording needs a decision. Verifier on the fix: Direction is right (use the existing useToast, keep or reopen the menu on failure) but it needs one new user-facing string in both locales in src/i18n/domains/common.ts, i.e. owner-approved copy (DEFERRED-OWNER style decision on wording), and SiteHeader tests must wrap the header in ToastProvider (site-shell.test.tsx renders SiteHeader bare, 11 render calls). fixRisk fair. Severity Low is right: needs a failed logout request, the session cookie also expires on its own, and exposure is limited to the portal data of that guest.

- Found by: R5-U11 (W2); candidate D-011
- Resolution: FIXED by T-F07 (batch B2, 2026-10-13): when signOut() resolves false the header pushes the toast common.ts ui.signOutFailed (EN "We couldn't sign you out. Try again.", EL "Δεν ήταν δυνατή η αποσύνδεση. Δοκιμάστε ξανά.", wording of decision D13 Q6); on true it keeps router.replace('/{locale}') and router.refresh(). Evidence: RED 3 failed / 34 passed (fix/logs/T-F07-red.log), GREEN 37/37, i18n parity 4/4; B2 verifier PASS (7 mutants of SiteHeader killed). Patch R5-T-F07.patch.
