- Category: Tests
- Status: CONFIRMED
- Location: src/lib/bookingOutbox.ts:L107-L109
- Evidence:
  ```
  await prisma.$transaction(async (tx) => {
        await tx.outboxEvent.updateMany({
          where: { id: eventId, status: 'LEASED', leaseOwner },
  ```
  Independent verifier (W34): src/lib/bookingOutbox.ts L107-L109: `await tx.outboxEvent.updateMany({ where: { id: eventId, status: 'LEASED', leaseOwner },`. tests/unit/booking-outbox.test.ts has 19 cases; the only lease-ownership case is 'does not record a delivery for a lease it no longer owns' (L224-L235), which covers the success write (L92) only. Other files that touch the module mock it (grep -rln bookingOutbox tests: worker-disconnect, arrival-request, admin-dead-outbox-actions mock it; integration check-in-request-repository.test.ts only mentions MAX_ATTEMPTS in a comment; grep deliverOutboxEvent|drainOutbox tests/integration: nothing). Executed mutation in a scratch copy of bookingOutbox.ts with `leaseOwner` removed from the failure-write where clause, aliased via a scratch vitest config: unmodified 19 cases still pass on the mutant; one added case (fetch mock sets event().leaseOwner='another-worker' and returns Response 500, expect resolves false and event toMatchObject {status:'LEASED', leaseOwner:'another-worker'}) gives MUTANT=0 'Tests 20 passed (20)' and MUTANT=1 'Tests 1 failed | 19 passed (20)' with diff `- leaseOwner: 'another-worker' / + leaseOwner: null`, `- status: LEASED / + status: PENDING`. Impact path re-derived: without the guard the first worker's late failure write flips the second worker's LEASED row to PENDING/DEAD and clears its lease, so the second worker's DELIVERED write (L92) matches nothing and the webhook is resent (same Idempotency-Key) or a delivered event ends DEAD.
- Problem: Executed mutation experiment. I copied HEAD's src/lib/bookingOutbox.ts into the scratchpad, removed `leaseOwner` from the where clause at L109 (mutant M4) and ran tests/unit/booking-outbox.test.ts against it through a scratch vitest config outside the repo that aliases '@/lib/bookingOutbox' to the copy (/private/tmp/claude-503/-Users-pvasilakis-site/606a1291-f73f-481a-9763-fc1af9c28431/scratchpad/review5/R5-U24a/vitest.M4.config.mjs): 'Test Files 1 passed (1), Tests 19 passed (19)'. Controls: an identical copy (C0) gives 19/19, and a sanity mutant (MAX_ATTEMPTS 10 -> 2, X0) goes red, so the alias really loads the copy. tests/unit/booking-outbox.test.ts is the only test that executes the real module: tests/routes/arrival-request.test.ts L24, tests/routes/admin-dead-outbox-actions.test.ts L14 and tests/unit/worker-disconnect.test.ts L12 mock it, and `grep -rn "deliverOutboxEvent\|drainOutbox" tests/integration` finds nothing (the integration suite never runs the worker; outbox-dead-lifecycle.test.ts only seeds DEAD/DELIVERED rows by raw SQL). The same unit file does pin the neighbouring rules: dropping the success-write guard (L92, mutant M3) turns 'does not record a delivery for a lease it no longer owns' red, and dropping `status: 'PENDING'` (L29, M1) or `nextAttemptAt` (L30, M2) from the claim turns four and one cases red. The failure-path guard is the one that nothing pins. A candidate case (copy of the success-path case, but the webhook mock answers new Response('', { status: 500 }) after setting event().leaseOwner = 'another-worker', then expects the event to stay { status: 'LEASED', leaseOwner: 'another-worker' }) passes on the HEAD copy (21/21 with the two extra cases I tried) and fails on M4 ('1 failed | 20 passed'); file: [...]
- Impact: If a worker stalls for more than LEASE_MS (5 minutes), drainOutbox (L146-L159) recovers its lease and a second worker leases the event. When the first worker's request then fails, the unguarded write sets the event back to PENDING (DEAD at the tenth attempt) and clears the second worker's lease, so the second worker's DELIVERED write (L92) matches no row: the webhook is sent twice (same Idempotency-Key) or a delivered event is left DEAD and opens the critical 'Dead outbox events' alert. It needs a stall of more than five minutes (the fetch itself has a 5 s timeout), so the probability is low; but the guard is the only protection and nobody would notice its removal. The guard is the 'leased-work ownership check in the same write as the status update' that CLAUDE.md requires.
- Fix: Add one case to tests/unit/booking-outbox.test.ts next to 'does not record a delivery for a lease it no longer owns' (L224): same setup, but the fetch mock sets event().leaseOwner = 'another-worker' and returns new Response('', { status: 500 }); expect deliverOutboxEvent to resolve false and event() toMatchObject({ status: 'LEASED', leaseOwner: 'another-worker' }). No production change. Verifier on the fix: Correct: add the one unit case next to L224 using the file's in-memory fake; it passes at HEAD and fails on the mutant (shown). Test-only, milliseconds; the rationale (CLAUDE.md: leased-work ownership checks in the same write as the status update) holds. Probability remains low (needs a worker stall over LEASE_MS = 5 min), so Low is right. Not covered by an existing R-id.
- Fix risk: Test only. The case uses the file's in-memory fake and runs in milliseconds; no existing case changes.
- Found by: R5-U24a (W34); candidate G-015
- Resolution: DEFERRED-OWNER (economy): not done under the owner's instruction of 2026-10-13 to watch the consumption; specified in decision-D13.json (.runtime/review5/fix/) as task T-F48, resumable on request.

### R-694: Logger sanitizeMetadata renders Date, URL and Map values as {}, marks a repeated (non-circular) object as '[CIRCULAR]', and makes the logging call throw on a BigInt
- Severity: Low
- Category: Bug
- Status: CONFIRMED
- Location: src/lib/logger-enterprise.ts:L133-L136
- Evidence:
  ```
  if (!value || typeof value !== 'object') return value;
        if (seen.has(value)) return '[CIRCULAR]';
        seen.add(value);
        if (Array.isArray(value)) return value.map((item) => redactRecursively(item));
  ```
  Independent verifier (W1a): Read logger-enterprise.ts L120-L159: `if (!value || typeof value !== 'object') return value; if (seen.has(value)) return '[CIRCULAR]'; seen.add(value);` (never removed after a node is finished) and `const serialized = JSON.stringify(redacted);` (L148, unguarded). Executed with the real logger (scratch vitest, LOG_LEVEL=debug): `{ at: new Date() }` -> {"at":{}}; URL -> {"u":{}}; Map -> {"m":{}}; Set -> {"s":{}}; `{ a: shared, b: shared }` -> b is '[CIRCULAR]'; `{ list: [shared, shared] }` -> second element '[CIRCULAR]'; a true cycle -> '[CIRCULAR]'; `{ n: BigInt(10) }` -> logger.info THROWS 'TypeError: Do not know how to serialize a BigInt'. No test pins any of it (grep CIRCULAR in tests: none). The sanitiser is unchanged since f7958fa except the sensitive-key union; Review 4 touched only redaction keys (T34) and LOG_LEVEL (T35). Latent claim: a grep scan of the 69 logger-enterprise call sites (7 lines after every logger.info/warn/error/debug call) for Date/getTime/new URL/Map/Set/BigInt found only ratePeriodRepository.logWrite, which logs IsoDate strings; this is a heuristic scan, not a type-level proof. Not covered by an existing finding.
- Problem: Any object that is not a plain record or array goes through `Object.entries`, which has no own enumerable properties for Date, URL, Map or Set, so the value becomes {}. `seen` is never cleared after a node is finished, so an object that appears twice in the metadata (a DAG, not a cycle) is replaced by '[CIRCULAR]' the second time. A bigint passes the `typeof value !== 'object'` branch unchanged, and the later `JSON.stringify(redacted)` (L148) throws. Executed (scratch logger-probe.ts, real logger, LOG_LEVEL=debug): `{ at: new Date(...) }` -> 'at: {}'; `{ a: shared, b: shared }` -> '{ a: { ok: true }, b: "[CIRCULAR]" }'; `{ u: new URL(...) }` -> 'u: {}'; `{ m: new Map(...) }` -> 'm: {}'; `{ n: 10n }` -> 'THROWS: TypeError: Do not know how to serialize a BigInt'. No test pins any of this (grep CIRCULAR in tests: none).
- Impact: Latent today: I read the metadata of all 87 logger call sites (grep list of `logger.*(` and `elogger.*(`) and none passes a Date, Map, URL or bigint. The next `logger.info('...', { lastSuccessAt: state.lastSuccessAt })` silently logs {}; a bigint value (for example from a $queryRaw count) turns a log line into an exception inside the request or worker flow.
- Fix: Before the generic object branch add `if (typeof value === 'bigint') return value.toString();` and `if (value instanceof Date) return Number.isNaN(value.getTime()) ? 'Invalid Date' : value.toISOString();`, and make `seen` track the current path only (`seen.add(value)` before recursing, `seen.delete(value)` after). Add three rows to tests/unit/logger-enterprise.test.ts. Verifier on the fix: Real but latent. Minimal fix in redactRecursively: bigint -> String(value), Date -> toISOString(), URL -> href, Map/Set -> Array.from before recursing; track ancestors only (delete the node from `seen` once its children are processed) so a repeated object is not marked circular; guard JSON.stringify(redacted) with try/catch and a '_unserializable' marker. Same file as C-022: one task. Fix risk low: changes log output only (Dates stop printing as {}); tests/unit/logger-enterprise.test.ts and the redaction tests must stay green; add one row per value type. Low is fair only as a trap for the [...]
- Fix risk: Output of Date values changes from {} to an ISO string; check tests that spy on logger output (tests/unit/logger-enterprise.test.ts, tests/security/api-boundaries.test.ts, client-identity.test.ts import the real logger).
- Found by: R5-U3 (W1a); candidate C-021
- Resolution: DEFERRED-OWNER (economy): not done under the owner's instruction of 2026-10-13 to watch the consumption; specified in decision-D13.json (.runtime/review5/fix/) as task T-F31, resumable on request.

### R-695: The 'Recent high-severity security events' alert uses a 5-minute window equal to its 5-minute schedule, so an event stored between two evaluations is never counted
- Severity: Low
- Category: Logic
- Status: CONFIRMED
- Location: src/lib/operationalMonitor.ts:L65-L70
- Evidence:
  ```
  windowMinutes: 5,
      severity: 'high',
      read: (windowMinutes) => prisma.securityAuditEvent.count({
        where: {
          severity: { in: ['high', 'critical'] },
          occurredAt: { gte: new Date(Date.now() - windowMinutes * 60_000) },
  ```
  Independent verifier (W1a): Read operationalMonitor.ts L61-L74 (rule 'Recent high-severity security events': `windowMinutes: 5`, `occurredAt: { gte: new Date(Date.now() - windowMinutes * 60_000) }`, no cursor, no overlap) and evaluateOperationalAlerts L144-L205 (rules run in sequence; windowMinutes comes from the stored rule row; an open alert is updated, never duplicated; a quiet window resolves it). scripts/run-operational-maintenance.ts awaits syncAirbnbCalendar (fetch up to 10 s) before evaluateOperationalAlerts; scripts/README.md L258-L260 schedules `*/5 * * * * ... flock -n ... timeout 280 ... operations`. Executed (scratch vitest on a copy of src; real evaluateOperationalAlerts, in-memory fake prisma, fake timers): evaluation 1 at +1 s, a 'high' event stored at +2 s, evaluation 2 at +300 s -> opened=1; at +301 s -> opened=1; at +303 s -> opened=0, openAlerts=0; at +304 s -> opened=0, openAlerts=0. Any two evaluations further apart than the 5-minute window leave the interval in between uncovered; with cron spacing of exactly 300 s the gap appears whenever the start-up delay (container start + sync + earlier rules) grows from one run to the next, and a skipped run (flock -n, timeout) loses at least 5 minutes. Not measured: the real delay variance, so the per-event miss probability (about E[max(0, delta)] / 300 s) is unknown. Not covered: R-416 and R-457 concern the stale-calendar rule; R-462 (declined) concerns stored rule rows.
- Problem: The rule counts rows with `occurredAt >= Date.now() - windowMinutes` and keeps no cursor and no overlap. The runbook runs the operations worker as `*/5 * * * * ... flock -n ... timeout 280 docker compose ... run --rm --no-deps operations` (scripts/README.md L259). `read()` executes after the container start, after the calendar sync (a fetch of up to FETCH_TIMEOUT_MS = 10 s, icalFetch.ts) and after the two outbox rules, so consecutive evaluation instants are 5 minutes plus a variable delay, not exactly 5 minutes. Whenever evaluation k+1 runs later (relative to its cron tick) than evaluation k, the interval between the end of window k and the start of window k+1 belongs to no window; a skipped run (flock -n, timeout, host down) leaves a gap of at least 5 minutes. Executed: scratch alert-window-probe.ts imports the real evaluateOperationalAlerts, installs an in-memory fake Prisma client as globalThis.__prisma__ and a controlled Date.now: evaluation at +1 s, a 'high' security event stored at +2 s, evaluation at +304 s (window start +4 s). Output: 'evaluation at +1 s -> opened=0 resolved=0 openAlerts=0', 'evaluation at +304 s -> opened=0 resolved=0 openAlerts=0'.
- Impact: A high or critical security audit event (refresh replay, theft signals) can produce no alert and no webhook; the row stays in security_audit_events for 90 days and the host has to find it. The chance per event is about (difference of the two start-up delays) / 300 s: small, but not zero; the real delay variance was not measured. Events that occur around a failed or skipped run are lost with certainty.
- Fix: Make consecutive windows overlap: windowMinutes 10 with the description changed to 'last ten minutes' (an alert then resolves one evaluation later), or count events since a persisted 'evaluated up to' timestamp. The upsert's update branch never rewrites windowMinutes (R-462, declined), so the existing alert_rules row must be updated once (SQL) or windowMinutes added to the update. Verifier on the fix: Right direction: overlap the windows. Setting this rule's windowMinutes to 10 (twice the schedule) is safe because an open alert is looked up and updated, not duplicated, and a quiet window resolves it; also reword the description ('last five minutes'). But the stored AlertRule row keeps its old windowMinutes (the upsert's update branch refreshes only description and metricName; R-462 declined changing that), so the fix needs either a one-line SQL update as an owner step or an explicit decision to add windowMinutes to the upsert update. Fix risk: low code risk; an alert stays open up to 10 [...]
- Fix risk: Alerts stay open one evaluation longer; the webhook payload and the stored description change; tests/unit/operational-alerts-calendar.test.ts, operational-alert-webhook.test.ts and the integration operations tests assert the rule definition; the stored rule row of a deployed database must be changed explicitly.
- Found by: R5-U3 (W1a); candidate C-020
- Resolution: FIXED by T-F32 (batch B6, 2026-10-13): the 'Recent high-severity security events' alert rule uses a 10-minute window (windowMinutes 10, description 'High or critical security audit events were recorded in the last ten minutes.') for a 5-minute schedule, so an event stored between two evaluations is counted by the next one; the upsert's update branch now writes windowMinutes, so a stored 5-minute row is corrected on the next run (the other three rules keep windowMinutes 5, their rows do not change). Evidence: RED 5 failed / 0 passed on the old code (create and update arguments, the 10-minute count; fix/logs/T-F32-red.log), GREEN 5/5; the integration suite after B6 passed (23 files / 125 tests, fix/logs/B6-integration.log); B6 verifier PASS. Patch R5-T-F32.patch.

### R-696: normalizePhone rejects numbers written with the 00 international call prefix (and with dots or slashes), so a guest typing them cannot claim or sign in and burns the claim budget
- Severity: Low
- Category: Bug
- Status: CONFIRMED
- Location: src/lib/phone.ts:L31-L35
- Evidence:
  ```
  // If all digits and plausible length, assume international number missing '+'
    if (/^\d{8,15}$/.test(raw)) {
      const prefixed = `+${raw}`;
      return isE164(prefixed) ? { e164: prefixed } : null;
    }
  ```
  Independent verifier (W1a): Read phone.ts L13-L38: raw digits are prefixed with '+', so '0049 170 1234567' becomes '+00491701234567', which isE164 (`/^\+[1-9]\d{7,14}$/`, L54) rejects. Executed (scratch vitest, real src/lib/phone.ts): normalizePhone('0049 170 1234567','ABROAD'), ('0044 7911 123456','ABROAD'), ('0030 691 234 5678','GR'), ('00306912345678','GR'/none) all -> null and phoneLookupCandidates -> []; '+49 170 1234567' works; '+33 6.12.34.56.78', '+44 7911/123456' and '+30 691.234.5678' -> null. claims/route.ts L22 accepts the string (min 8, max 32) and the form (UnifiedGuestClient.tsx L247-L258) only checks length with placeholder '+30 690 000 0000'; a null normalisation makes consumeBookingClaimGrant throw INVALID_CLAIM (L170) -> 401 'The claim token or account credentials are invalid'; every claims response clears the exchange cookie (POST wrapper, L121-L127) and the 'portal-claim' limiter allows 5 per hour (L38-L42). Sign-in answers 401 with the signInFailed text that names the phone number. Experiment in the scratch copy: mapping a leading `00` to `+` in normalizePhone made all four 00 spellings resolve (+491701234567, +447911123456, +306912345678 x2) and kept tests/unit/date-phone-validation.test.ts, phone-lookup-candidates, phone-lookup-parity and tests/security/rate-limit-persistence.test.ts green (62 tests with the probe); copy restored. Adjacent decisions, different inputs: R-397 (leading 0, fixed by T02), R-607 and O90 (invisible format characters, accepted: 'strip if a guest reports it').
- Problem: A digits-only input is turned into '+' + digits. '0049 170 1234567' becomes '+00491701234567', which `isE164` rejects (first digit must be 1-9), so the function returns null. Executed (scratch phone-probe.mts, real src/lib/phone.ts): normalizePhone('0049 170 1234567','ABROAD'), ('0044 7911 123456','ABROAD'), ('0030 691 234 5678','GR') and ('00306912345678','GR') all return null and phoneLookupCandidates returns [] for each; '+49 170 1234567' works. Dots and slashes are not separators either: '+33 6.12.34.56.78' and '+44 7911/123456' return null. The 00 prefix is the usual way to write a foreign number in Greece and most of Europe. The form (UnifiedGuestClient.tsx) only requires phone.trim().length >= 8 (guestValidation.ts) and the placeholder is '+30 690 000 0000'. R-397 and R-607 covered a leading 0 and invisible characters, not this. No earlier review mentions the 00 prefix.
- Impact: Claim: consumeBookingClaimGrant throws INVALID_CLAIM, the route answers 401, the guest sees the generic 'We couldn't verify your identity' text with no hint about the phone. Every claims response clears the exchange cookie (claims/route.ts POST wrapper) and every attempt counts against the 5-per-hour grant and address buckets, so a guest who retries the same spelling is blocked for up to an hour after five tries, and the 30-minute default grant may expire meanwhile and the host must issue a new one. Access reset has the same effect for a guest whose original number was stored from '+' input. Sign-in answers 401 with the signInFailed text, which at least names the phone number. The workaround is to type '+' and the country code.
- Fix: At the top of normalizePhone, after stripping separators, turn a leading '00' into '+' (`const raw = stripped.startsWith('00') ? '+' + stripped.slice(2) : stripped`), and add '.' and '/' to the stripped separator class. normalizeIdentifier in sensitiveRateLimit.ts L25 repeats the separator class by design ('Same separators as normalizePhone'), so change it in the same patch; the 00 case then merges into the '+' bucket automatically because it delegates to normalizePhone. Verifier on the fix: Minimal fix (tested): in normalizePhone treat a leading `00` followed by digits as `+`: `const raw = /^00\d+$/.test(stripped) ? '+' + stripped.slice(2) : stripped;`. The limiter calls normalizePhone, so its bucket key follows automatically. Keep dots and slashes out of the same task: widening the separator set must also change the limiter's `compact` regex (sensitiveRateLimit.ts L25) so that the limiter strips exactly what normalizePhone strips (R-607 invariant). Fix risk: more spellings resolve to an account and share a limiter bucket; stored numbers are unaffected (they are always +E.164); [...]
- Fix risk: Sign-in, claim, the admin phone search and the limiter all go through normalizePhone, so inputs that were unresolvable become resolvable; the GR rule is untouched because it needs a first digit 1-9. Update tests/unit/date-phone-validation.test.ts (accept table), phone-lookup-candidates, phone-lookup-parity and tests/security/rate-limit-persistence.test.ts, and check that the limiter and sign-in keep one bucket per account (the 10-digit international case stays the accepted O54 exception).
- Found by: R5-U1 (W1a); candidate C-026
- Resolution: FIXED (variant of decision D13) by T-F33 (batch B6, 2026-10-13): normalizePhone accepts the 00 international call prefix (`0030 694 123 4567` -> `+306941234567`; `00` alone is rejected; a bare 0 followed by 9 digits stays rejected, O54 unchanged), and the sign-in, claim and rate-limit paths go through it, so the limiter bucket of the 00 spellings equals the bucket of the `+30` spelling; dots and slashes stay rejected as decided (D13 added no new separators; tests pin the rejection). Evidence: RED 8 failed / 68 passed (4 normalize rows, 1 parity row, 3 limiter rows; fix/logs/T-F33-red.log), GREEN 76/76; integration suite passed; B6 verifier PASS (side effect that follows the spec: a 10-digit `00`-prefixed input such as 0012345678 now reads as +12345678 and passes E.164, consistently in the limiter and sign-in). Patch R5-T-F33.patch.

### R-697: retryFailedNotifications can revive an event that a concurrent erasure cancels between its two statements
- Severity: Low
- Category: Concurrency
- Status: SUSPECTED
- Location: src/lib/prisma-repositories/checkInRequestRepository.ts:L314-L318
- Evidence:
  ```
  const cancelled = await prisma.outboxEvent.findMany({
      where: { checkInRequestId: id, status: 'DEAD', payload: { path: ['redacted'], equals: true } },
      select: { id: true },
    });
    const retried = await prisma.outboxEvent.updateMany({
  ```
  Independent verifier (W1a): Read all paths. checkInRequestRepository.ts L313-L333: `prisma.outboxEvent.findMany({ where: { checkInRequestId: id, status: 'DEAD', payload: { path: ['redacted'], equals: true } } ... })` and then `prisma.outboxEvent.updateMany({ where: { checkInRequestId: id, status: 'DEAD', ...(cancelled.length > 0 ? { id: { notIn: ... } } : {}) } ...})` are two separate autocommit statements (no $transaction). privacyService.ts L163-L174 (inside the erasure transaction) turns PENDING/LEASED events into `status: 'DEAD'` with `payload: { redacted: true, reason: 'privacy_erasure' }`. If that transaction commits between the two statements, the event is DEAD when the updateMany runs but is not in `cancelled`, so it matches and is set to PENDING with the redacted payload kept. bookingOutbox.ts drainOutbox (L145-L170) selects `status: 'PENDING'` with no `redacted` filter, and deliverOutboxEvent (L16-L118) builds the body from the live check-in row (requestId, bookingId, requestedTime, status; name, e-mail, phone and message are already null after erasure), so the event would be sent to the webhook. tests/unit/checkin-request-repository.test.ts L132-L215 pin the two-statement shape with a fake that throws on unknown filters; the integration test (tests/integration/operations/check-in-request-repository.test.ts L238-L262) is sequential, not interleaved. R-436 is the origin (fixed by T09); this is an incomplete-fix angle no finding states. Not executed: needs two real PostgreSQL transactions (Docker).
- Problem: The R-436 fix finds the erasure-cancelled ids with one query and then excludes them by id in a second, separate statement (no transaction, default Read Committed). privacyService.ts L163-L175 turns PENDING/LEASED events into DEAD with payload { redacted: true } inside the erasure transaction. If that transaction commits after the findMany and before the updateMany, the event is DEAD at updateMany time but not in `cancelled`, so it is set back to PENDING (payload stays { redacted: true }). The outbox worker then claims it (status PENDING) and sends a webhook for an erased guest (the check-in request row is already blanked of name, e-mail, phone and message, but requestId, bookingId, requestedTime and status are sent). The code comment says these events 'must never be sent'. I read both code paths; I did not run the interleaving (needs two real PostgreSQL transactions, i.e. the Docker integration suite).
- Impact: Needs an admin to press Retry on a request in the same few milliseconds in which another admin action erases that guest, while the request has both a genuinely DEAD event and a PENDING/LEASED one. The leaked data is the pseudonymous booking id and arrival time only. Practically negligible; it is a gap in the invariant the fix states, not a likely production event.
- Fix: Run both statements in one interactive transaction with a snapshot isolation level so the updateMany sees the same rows as the findMany: `prisma.$transaction(async (tx) => { const cancelled = await tx.outboxEvent.findMany(...); return tx.outboxEvent.updateMany(...); }, { isolationLevel: Prisma.TransactionIsolationLevel.RepeatableRead })`, with the same P2034 retry loop updateStatus uses. Verifier on the fix: Two sound options. (a) One atomic statement: $executeRaw UPDATE ... WHERE check_in_request_id = $1 AND status = 'DEAD' AND NOT COALESCE(payload @> '{"redacted": true}'::jsonb, false); the code comment shows a Prisma NOT filter was avoided because a missing JSON path yields NULL; this rewrites the two unit tests that pin the query shape. (b) Defence at the point of sending: in deliverOutboxEvent refuse (mark DEAD, return false) an event whose payload.redacted === true; closes every route to a revived cancelled event, needs one test, but adds a branch to the delivery path (explicit coverage [...]
- Fix risk: tests/unit/checkin-request-repository.test.ts mocks prisma.outboxEvent directly and would need a $transaction mock; add an integration case in tests/integration/operations/check-in-request-repository.test.ts. A serialization failure would surface as P2034 if the retry loop is not added.
- To confirm: On a real PostgreSQL 16: seed a check-in request with one exhausted genuine DEAD event and one PENDING event; make findMany run the erasure to commit right after it returns (spy that awaits the real findMany, then eraseGuestByAdmin), then let updateMany run; the bug exists if the erased event ends PENDING with payload { redacted: true }. Run request: npm run test:integration with a new deterministic-interleaving test in tests/integration/operations/check-in-request-repository.test.ts (needs Docker; lead only)
- Found by: R5-U2, R5-X1 (W1a); candidate C-003
- Resolution: DECLINED by decision D13 (2026-10-13, the owner's delegate): SUSPECTED. Reproducing it needs a new deterministic two-transaction harness for a millisecond window that requires an admin retry at the same moment an erasure commits. Nothing personal can leave (the erasure nulls name, e-mail and phone), and only to the host's own webhook (verifier: decline defensible).

- Severity: Low
- Category: Security

### R-699: Content build gate rejects duplicate slugs but not duplicate item ids, which are React keys, favourite ids and lookup keys
- Severity: Low
- Category: Logic
- Status: CONFIRMED
- Location: src/lib/validation.ts:L42-L44
- Evidence:
  ```
  const owner = slugOwners.get(it.slug);
        if (owner !== undefined) throw new Error(`Duplicate slug in category ${c.id}: items ${owner} and ${it.id}`);
        slugOwners.set(it.slug, it.id);
  ```
  Independent verifier (W1b): src/lib/validation.ts:29-45 checks name/title, slug empty/malformed/duplicate, but never `it.id`; src/lib/data.ts:49-80 (strict loader) does not dedupe ids; src/data/schemas.ts `id: z.string()`. Id uses verified: GuideList.tsx:158,171,187 `key={entry.id}`, PhonesDirectory.tsx:75 `key={entry.id}`, guideEntries.ts:77-79 `${category.slug}:${item.id}` (favourites), homeRelief.ts:38 `.find((item) => item.id === source.moment)`. No test asserts id uniqueness (grep over tests). Committed data is clean (node script: moments 18 ids/18 unique, phones 11/11). Executed (scratch vitest, node:fs mocked to serve two items with id 'dup' and different names, real getItemsByCategory + validateLocalization): strict loader returns ['dup/alpha-place','dup/beta-place'], validateLocalization does not throw, favoriteIdOf gives ['phones:dup','phones:dup'], React logs 'Encountered two children with the same key, `%s`. Keys should be unique ... Non-unique keys may cause children to be duplicated and/or omitted'. With the proposed check applied in a scratch copy of validation.ts: the new test (same id, different slugs -> 'Duplicate id in category food: taverna') passes and tests/unit/content-localization-validation.test.ts + content-gate-strict.test.ts stay green (42 passed); against HEAD validation.ts the new test fails.
- Problem: validateLocalization (L29-L45) enforces unique slugs per category (R-446/T24) but nothing checks it.id. The id is used as React key (src/components/guide/GuideList.tsx L158 key={entry.id}, L171, L187; src/components/guide/PhonesDirectory.tsx L75), as the favourites id (guideEntries.ts L77-L79 `${category.slug}:${item.id}`) and as a lookup key (src/components/home/homeRelief.ts L38 .find((item) => item.id === source.moment)). Executed in the scratch copy: fs mocked to serve two items with id 'dup' and different names; getItemsByCategory('moments', { strict: true }) returned ['dup/alpha-place','dup/beta-place'] and validateLocalization([...locales]) did not throw. Rendering PhonesDirectory with the two resulting GuideEntry values: favoriteIds ['phones:dup','phones:dup'] and React logged 'Encountered two children with the same key'. No test asserts id uniqueness (grep over tests), and the committed data has none today (moments 18 ids, phones 11 ids, checked with a script). This test pair lives in tests/unit/content-localization-validation.test.ts and content-gate-strict.test.ts, which cover slugs only.
- Impact: Copying a JSON entry and changing the name but not the id passes `npm run build` (validate-content.ts). In the guide, saving one place as a favourite marks both, React can drop or duplicate rows when the filter changes (its own warning text), and id lookups return only the first item.
- Fix: In validateLocalization, before `for (const it of items)` add `const idOwners = new Set<string>();` and, ahead of the `if (it.slug === undefined) continue;` line, `if (idOwners.has(it.id)) throw new Error(`Duplicate id in category ${c.id}: ${it.id}`); idOwners.add(it.id);`. Add a row to tests/unit/content-localization-validation.test.ts: two items with the same id and different slugs expect toThrow('Duplicate id in category food: taverna'). Verifier on the fix: Correct and minimal as proposed (Set per category, throw before the slug checks, one new row in content-localization-validation.test.ts); verified in a scratch copy. fixRisk is fair; also run `npx tsx scripts/validate-content.ts` (ids are unique today).
- Fix risk: Low: committed ids are unique (script check) and the existing mock tests use distinct ids. Run content-localization-validation, content-gate-strict and `npx tsx scripts/validate-content.ts`. The location is in validation.ts, which is outside this unit's file list; the regression test belongs to this unit.
- Found by: R5-U15 (W1b); candidate B-002
- Resolution: FIXED by T-F30 (batch B5, 2026-10-13): the content gate (validateLocalization in src/lib/validation.ts) rejects duplicate item ids inside one category (after the name-localization checks, before the slug checks); the same id in different categories stays valid (a test pins that scope). Evidence: RED 1 failed / 24 passed (fix/logs/T-F30-red.log), GREEN 43/43 over the content tests; `npm run build` (which runs scripts/validate-content.ts) passes on the real content. Patch R5-T-F30.patch.

### R-700: Up close section: CSS columns leave one quarter or one third of the grid empty at every width from 768 px
- Severity: Low (the finder said Medium: Visual-only: all ten photos are present and reachable and nothing is hidden or broken. The earlier Mediums of this repo are functional failures (R-377 pinch-zoom blocked, R-379 content stuck at [...])
- Category: Bug
- Status: CONFIRMED
- Location: src/styles/components/apartment.css:L223-L225
- Evidence:
  ```
  @media (min-width: 1280px) {
    .apt-masonry { columns: 4; }
  }
  ```
  Independent verifier (W2): src/styles/components/apartment.css:213-225 `.apt-masonry { columns: 2; ... }`, `@media (min-width: 768px) { .apt-masonry { columns: 3; ... } }`, `@media (min-width: 1280px) { .apt-masonry { columns: 4; } }`, :231 `break-inside: avoid`; src/data/apartmentPhotos.ts:69-78 ten details entries, all `width: 1280, height: 1920`. Measured (W2-VA/cols.cjs, /en/apartment, column bottoms of `#details .apt-masonry__item` relative to the list top): 390: 1318/1318; 768: 1370/1370/679; 1024: 1831/1831/910; 1280: 1280/1280/1280/419; 1440: 1379/1379/1379/452; 1510: same as 1440 (tile widths 172/222/299/279/301). Screenshot W2-VA/details-1440.png (looked at): the fourth column holds one tile, rows 2 and 3 of it are blank. identity.md:1024 documents 'CSS columns: 5 + 5 on mobile, 4 + 4 + 2 at md, 3 + 3 + 3 + 1 at xl' as the intended split and PROGRESS.md:387 says it came 'from the CSS, not from a render (check a browser at 390, 768 and 1280)', so no render check was done before. Not in REVIEW.md (grep masonry/apt-masonry: 0 hits); D3 (the single-tile branch kept) is unrelated. The finder's fix emulation reproduces (W2-VA/even.cjs, ul.style.columns = 2 below 1024 and 5 from 1024): spread 0 at 390/768/1024/1280/1440, section heights 1318/2595/536/674/727, tile widths 172/340/175/221/238 px.
- Problem: 9d4784f added the `details` section: ten tiles that are all 2:3. `.apt-masonry` uses CSS `columns` (2 / 3 at md / 4 at xl) with `break-inside: avoid`. Ten equal tiles then split 5+5, 4+4+2 and 3+3+3+1 (the split that identity.md:1024 and PROGRESS.md say was derived from the CSS and not rendered). I rendered it (puppeteer, loopback, http://localhost:3000/en/apartment, column bottoms of #details .apt-masonry__item): 390 px: 1318/1318 (even). 768 px: 1370/1370/679 (third column 691 px short). 1024 px: 1831/1831/910 (921 px short). 1280 px: 1280/1280/1280/419 (fourth column holds one tile, 861 px empty). 1440 px: 1379/1379/1379/452 (927 px empty). Screenshot of the 1440 px render: rows 2 and 3 of the right-hand column are blank (scratchpad review5/R5-X1b/shots/details-1440.png). Emulating the proposed fix in the page (ul.style.columns = '2' below 1024 px and '5' from 1024 px) gave column bottoms 2595/2595 (768), 536 x5 (1024), 674 x5 (1280), 727 x5 (1440): spread 0 at all four widths, tile widths 340/175/221/238 px.
- Impact: On a tablet or any desktop the closing 'Up close' gallery of the public apartment page looks unfinished: a blank block about 900 px tall next to the photos. The documentation presents the 3+3+3+1 and 4+4+2 splits as the intended result.
- Fix: Give a section whose tiles all share one aspect ratio (the details list) an even grid: a modifier class such as `apt-masonry--even` with `columns: 2` below 1024 px and `columns: 5` from 1024 px (ten tiles fill 5x2 or 2x5 exactly). Set the details tiles' `sizes` to the real tile widths (the shared TILE_SIZES says 30 vw at 768 px, but the tile is 340 px wide there, so the image is requested too small). Update identity.md:1024 and :1130 (column counts). Verifier on the fix: Problem real and fix works (spread 0, verified), but the 2/5-column fix makes the section 1.9x taller at 768 px (2595 px against 1370 px now) and gives 175 px tiles at 1024, so it is a design choice, not a free fix. A row-major grid (`display: grid`, 2/3/4 columns, item margin 0, gap 8/12 px; measured in gridalt.cjs) keeps today's heights and tile widths exactly and leaves only a short last row (3+3+3+1 at 768-1279, 4+4+2 from 1280). Either way identity.md:1024 and :1130, the tone-alternation sentence and the per-section `sizes` need a re-read; the finder's fixRisk is fair.
- Fix risk: `sizes` per section in ApartmentGallery.tsx; component tests select `.apt-masonry img`, so keep that class; the tone-alternation sentence in identity.md:1024 depends on the column count and must be re-read; check in a browser at 390, 768, 1024, 1280 and 1440 px.
- Found by: R5-X1b (W2); candidate E-001
- Resolution: FIXED by T-F16 (batch B3, 2026-10-13): ApartmentGallery adds apt-masonry--grid to a section with more than one tile when all its tiles share one box aspect ratio (the Up close details and bedroom-2); apartment.css lays it out row-major with 2 columns, 3 from 768 px and 4 from 1280 px, the same gaps and no item margins; mixed sections keep the CSS columns and the single-tile branch stays (D3). Evidence: RED 3 failed (fix/logs/T-F16-red.log), GREEN 25/25; lead measurements in real Chromium on the production build for en and el at 390, 768, 1024, 1280 and 1440 px (fix/logs/B3-lead-gallery.log): details 2/3/3/4/4 columns with equal tile widths (172/222/299/279/301 px) and only the last row short (4+4+2 at 1280 and 1440), bedroom-2 as 2x2, 3+1, 3+1, 4, 4; no horizontal overflow; B3 verifier PASS-WITH-NOTES (identity.md follows in T-F54). Patch R5-T-F16.patch.

### R-701: .pwa-banner is limited to about half the viewport width by left: 50%, so on phones the iOS tip and the update banner render as a narrow tall pill whose text spills outside the rounded background; the two pills also sit on the same anchor and the tip hides the update banner's Refresh button
- Severity: Low
- Category: Bug
- Status: CONFIRMED
- Location: src/styles/components/shell.css:L48-L64
- Evidence:
  ```
  .pwa-banner {
    position: fixed;
    bottom: calc(8px + env(safe-area-inset-bottom));
    left: 50%;
    z-index: 50;
    align-items: center;
    gap: 8px;
    max-width: calc(100vw - 32px);
  ```
  Independent verifier (W1b): src/styles/components/shell.css L48-64 has position:fixed; left:50%; max-width:calc(100vw - 32px); translate:-50% 0 and no width; the production CSS chunk (.next/static/chunks/*.css, grep) has the same declarations, no width. Chromium on /en/stay and /el/stay with inline display:flex set by hand: 390x844 iOS tip 195x104 with 4 lines (Greek 195x127, 5 lines); 320x640 tip 160x172, 7 lines; 540x900 still 2 lines in a 270 px box; 1280x720 one line. Update banner at 390: 227x104, 4 lines (default text; Greek 265x104). Root cause: with width:max-content the same boxes become 313x58 (1 line, English) / 358x59 (2 lines, Greek) at 390, 288x59 at 320, unchanged at 1280. Screenshot banner-en-390.png shows the text lines spilling outside the 999px-radius pill. Overlap: both pills have bottom 8px and left 50%; with both shown elementFromPoint at the Refresh button centre returns an element inside #ios-a2hs-tip at 390, 320, 540 and 1280. Layout: src/app/[locale]/layout.tsx L43-58 renders both with class pwa-banner. PwaManager shows the tip for isIOS && !isStandalone && !dismissed (L76-83). Different from R-401 (BookBar z-index, DECLINED, SUSPECTED): that one is about stacking, this one about width; no earlier finding on width.
- Problem: With left: 50% and width auto, the shrink-to-fit width of an absolutely positioned box is bounded by the space to its right (50vw), not by max-width: calc(100vw - 32px). Real Chromium on /en/stay and /el/stay with PwaManager's inline display: flex applied by hand (scripts browser-banner*.cjs; the production CSS in .next/static/chunks has the same declarations): at 390x844 the update banner is 217x149 px with 6 text lines (text column 49 px; Greek 238x172, 7 lines) and the iOS tip is 195x104 px with 4 lines (Greek 195x127, 5 lines); at 320 px the tip is 160x172 px with 7 lines; at 540 px it still wraps to 3 lines; from 600 px up it is 2 lines. The border-radius is 999px, so on a tall box the text lines reach beyond the curved background at the corners (screenshots banner-en-390.png, tip-el-390.png). Same geometry in light and dark. Root cause confirmed: with width: max-content the same banner is 358x59 px with 2 lines (also with left/right: 16px and no translate). Second observation: #ios-a2hs-tip and #update-banner share bottom and left, so when both are shown they overlap (390x844: 86% of the banner; element at the Refresh button's centre is a span inside #ios-a2hs-tip). R-401 (BookBar z-index) is a different issue; this one is the width.
- Impact: PwaManager shows the iOS tip to every iPhone visitor who has not dismissed it (isIOS && !isStandalone), on every localized page, including the first page after the QR scan; the guest sees a malformed 104-172 px tall pill over the content at the bottom. The update banner looks the same for returning visitors. Text stays legible and both buttons are reachable, so this is cosmetic, but it is the most visible element for the main device class.
- Fix: In .pwa-banner add `width: max-content;` after max-width (keeps left: 50% and translate). For the overlap, either stack both pills in one flex column container or offset the later one by the height of the first. Verifier on the fix: `width: max-content;` after max-width is correct and I measured it (313x58 / 358x59 at 390, same at 1280). The overlap half needs a design choice (stack in one container or offset), so it is slightly bigger than a one-liner. Component CSS stays unlayered (O38); no unit test can pin the geometry, a browser check or audit:responsive:ux is needed, as the fixRisk says. Severity Low agreed (cosmetic, controls reachable apart from the overlap); it is the first-visit view for every iPhone guest, but the pill is dismissible.
- Fix risk: Check both pills at 320-1280 px in both themes and with the BookBar shown (R-401, declined, still applies); component CSS stays unlayered (O38); no unit test pins the geometry (jsdom has no layout), so verify in a browser or with npm run audit:responsive:ux.
- Found by: R5-U16 (W1b); candidate B-012
- Resolution: FIXED by T-F12 (batch B2, 2026-10-13): #update-banner and #ios-a2hs-tip sit in one fixed flex column .pwa-banners (left/right 16 px, bottom 8 px + safe area, gap 8 px, pointer-events none); the pills are static with pointer-events auto and max-width 100%. Evidence: lead measurements in real Chromium on the production build (fix/logs/B2-lead-pills.log): 96 checks passed for en and el at 320, 390, 768 and 1280 px, light and dark: each pill alone and both inside the 16 px margins, no overlap, the Refresh button is clickable, the empty container does not block the bottom edge; screenshots in fix/lead-checks/shots/. B2 verifier PASS. Residue: R-797 (the fixed net-status dot overlaps the left end of a full-width pill at 320 px). Patch R5-T-F12.patch.

### R-703: Opening the mobile menu on a classic-scrollbar desktop shifts the page by the scrollbar width (overflow: hidden on the root, no gutter reserved), and the menu now serves 768-1319 px
- Severity: Low
- Category: Bug
- Status: CONFIRMED
- Location: src/styles/components/shell.css:L226
- Evidence:
  `:root:has(.mobile-menu[open]) { overflow: hidden; }`
  Independent verifier (W2): src/styles/components/shell.css:226 `:root:has(.mobile-menu[open]) { overflow: hidden; }`; grep -rn scrollbar-gutter src: no hit. Executed (Chrome 154 headless with --hide-scrollbars removed via ignoreDefaultArgs, classic 10 px scrollbar; /en/apartment 1280x720; W2-VA/d014.cjs): menu closed clientWidth 1270, header left 64 / width 1142 / right 1206, root overflow visible; menu open: root overflow hidden, clientWidth 1280, header width 1152, right 1216 (+10 px); closed again 1270/1142. W2-VA/d014b.cjs: `scrollbar-gutter: stable` on :root (also `stable both-edges`, and html gutter + body overflow hidden) does not keep the gutter, still 1270 -> 1280 / 1142 -> 1152, also with a plain inline `overflow: hidden` and no dialog (the finder's two failed CSS attempts reproduce); `overflow: clip` behaves the same; `overflow: hidden scroll` keeps 1270 but leaves the page scrollable (no lock). W2-VA/d014c.cjs: `:root:has(.mobile-menu[open]) { padding-right: var(--sbw) }` with --sbw = innerWidth - clientWidth measured while closed keeps the header at 1142 both open and closed, so a workable fix exists. History: git show b82684c -- shell.css has `-@media (min-width: 1280px)` -> `+@media (min-width: 1320px)`: the menu already served 768-1279 px before, b82684c added only 1280-1319 px (the title's 'now serves 768-1319' overstates the regression). Firefox and Safari not tested (the mechanism is the generic classic-scrollbar behaviour); macOS overlay scrollbars and phones are unaffected. REVIEW.md has no finding for it (its only scroll-lock hit, line 475, lists the lightbox lock as fine).
- Problem: The scroll lock removes the viewport scrollbar, so on browsers with classic (non-overlay) scrollbars the layout box grows by the scrollbar width while the dialog opens, and shrinks back when it closes. Since b82684c the nav stays behind the menu button up to 1319 px (shell.css L202), so ordinary laptop windows now use this menu. Executed in headless Chromium started with the default --hide-scrollbars removed (classic 10 px scrollbar), 1280x720 on /en/apartment: menu closed documentElement.clientWidth 1270, header width 1142; menu open clientWidth 1280, header width 1152 (the sticky header and the content behind the scrim widen by 10 px). I also tried `scrollbar-gutter: stable` on `:root:has(.mobile-menu[open])` and unconditionally on `:root` via an injected style: clientWidth still jumped 1270 -> 1280, so that simple fix does not work in this Chromium. macOS overlay scrollbars and mobile browsers are unaffected; Firefox and Safari were not tested.
- Impact: A visible 10-17 px horizontal jump of the page behind the scrim each time the menu opens and closes on Windows/Linux desktop browsers between 768 and 1319 px.
- Fix: No verified fix. The two CSS attempts above failed here; a working approach needs a new experiment (for example reserving the width by measuring `innerWidth - documentElement.clientWidth` before open and applying it as padding-right on the root while the dialog is open). Verifier on the fix: The finder proposes no fix. CSS-only `scrollbar-gutter` fails in Chrome 154 (re-verified). A measure-and-pad works (padding-right = innerWidth - clientWidth, measured before showModal(); verified: header width unchanged) but adds JS to MobileMenu's open path and must follow resizes. Purely cosmetic, so declining is reasonable; the finder's fixRisk is fair, only 'no verified fix' is too pessimistic.
- Fix risk: Any JS compensation touches the open/close path of MobileMenu; test in Chromium, Firefox and Safari with classic scrollbars. Cosmetic, so declining it is reasonable.
- Found by: R5-U11 (W2); candidate D-014
- Resolution: DECLINED by decision D13 (2026-10-13, the owner's delegate): Cosmetic, and only on classic-scrollbar desktops below 1320 px. No CSS fix works (scrollbar-gutter fails in Chrome, re-verified), and a JS padding workaround adds risk to the modal's open path.

### R-704: No print rule: printing or saving the home page as PDF omits every block the visitor has not scrolled past, and shows the balcony photo behind closed shutters
- Severity: Low
- Category: Bug
- Status: CONFIRMED
- Location: src/styles/motion.css:L342-L343
- Evidence:
  ```
  :root[data-motion="full"] .host .letter { transition: opacity var(--dur-reveal) var(--ease-glide); }
    :root[data-motion="full"] .host .letter:not(.is-in) { opacity: 0; }
  ```
  Independent verifier (W1b): grep -rn 'media print|media not print|@media (print|print:|only print' src docs public finds nothing; grep -rn 'print' src/styles src/app/globals.css finds nothing; in the page's styleSheets 0 CSSMediaRule mention print. Executed (headless Chrome, 1280x720, no-preference, page hydrated and never scrolled, then emulateMediaType('print')): {motion:'full', factO:'1', hlO:'0', letterO:'0', pinsO:'0', shutter:'block', shutterTransform:'none', isIn: facts true, highlights-stage/window/rooms-deck/relief-wrap/letter false}. Real print-to-PDF (page.pdf A4, no scroll, rasterised with Ghostscript): page 2 shows the balcony heading with two closed shutters instead of the photo and a blank band where the season cards belong; page 4 shows the relief plan without pins and an empty host-letter area. (An earlier PDF of mine looked complete only because my own element screenshots had scrolled the blocks into view; the clean run is the one reported.) Landscape A4 (width >= 1024 px): the rooms deck stays piled (page 5).
- Problem: The hidden states depend on IntersectionObserver adding `is-in` while the visitor scrolls; a printout has no scrolling. `grep -rn "media print\|media not print\|print {" src docs/design/identity.md` returns nothing, so no print rule resets them. Run evidence: puppeteer, 1280x720, no-preference, page loaded and left at the top, then page.emulateMediaType('print'): `{"motion":"full","letter":"0","hl":"0","shutter":"block","isIn":"facts:true highlights-stage:false window:false rooms-deck:false relief-wrap:false letter:false"}`.
- Impact: A guest or the owner who uses Print or Save as PDF on the home page gets a document without the host letter, season cards, night strip and relief pins (only what was scrolled into view is printed), and the balcony section shows two closed shutters instead of the photo.
- Fix: Add a print reset next to the gate, for example `@media print { :root[data-motion="full"] .facts .fact, :root[data-motion="full"] .facts .facts__more, :root[data-motion="full"] .intro .hl, :root[data-motion="full"] .teaser .night, :root[data-motion="full"] .location .relief__contour, :root[data-motion="full"] .location .relief__pins, :root[data-motion="full"] .host .letter { opacity: 1 !important; transform: none !important; } :root[data-motion="full"] .window .shutter { display: none !important; } }`, or scope the motion gate to `screen`. Verifier on the fix: A separate @media print block is right and will not trip tests/unit/motion-css-gate.test.ts (it only inspects rules declaring animation/transition/view-transition-name; read the file). Corrections: the proposed list misses the rooms deck, which stays piled at print widths >= 1024 px (landscape A4): add `.rooms .rooms-deck .room-card { transform: none !important }`; `.window__img` keeps scale(1.14) (cosmetic). Check A4 portrait and landscape for /en and /el. fixRisk otherwise fair.
- Fix risk: Adding rules inside a new @media print block should not trip tests/unit/motion-css-gate.test.ts (it reads motion.css at-rule preludes, per REVIEW.md); run it. Scoping the whole gate to `screen` would change every prelude the gate test matches, so prefer the separate print block. Check the print preview of /en and /el at A4.
- Found by: R5-U10 (W1b); candidate B-006
- Resolution: FIXED by T-F17 (batch B3, 2026-10-13): a separate @media print block forces the final state of every :not(.is-in) reveal state of the motion gate (facts, highlights, window image, room cards, nights, relief contour and pins, letter), hides the window shutters, and a print block from 1024 px keeps the rooms deck fan transform of home.css instead of piling the cards; transitions are off in print. Evidence: RED 3 failed (print reset of 15 class/property pairs missing, shutters, M28 range; fix/logs/T-F17-red.log), GREEN 8/8, the new test also passes lint:security after one corrective retry (fix/logs/T-F17-retry1-*.log; the first version had an unsafe regex and a dynamic RegExp); lead check in real Chromium on the production build (fix/logs/B3-lead-motion.log): print emulation of /en and /el at A4 portrait and landscape: every hidden reveal class is opaque, shutters gone, the six deck cards on six distinct positions; B3 verifier PASS-WITH-NOTES (6 mutants killed). Open nit: R-799 (A4 portrait print keeps the deck as a horizontal row wider than the page). Patch R5-T-F17.patch.

### R-705: Intro heading is shown semi-transparent and tilted at load on viewports taller than about 1190 px (the KineticBand no longer pushes it below the fold)
- Severity: Low
- Category: Bug
- Status: CONFIRMED
- Location: src/styles/motion.css:L527-L529
- Evidence:
  ```
  animation: section-title-rise linear both;
        animation-timeline: view();
        animation-range: entry 0% cover 30%;
  ```
  Independent verifier (W2): src/styles/motion.css:526-529 `transform-origin: 50% 100%; animation: section-title-rise linear both; animation-timeline: view(); animation-range: entry 0% cover 30%;` and :562-565 keyframes from opacity 0 + `perspective(600px) translateY(.5em) rotateX(-58deg)` to opacity 1. Executed (W2-VA/e003.cjs, no-preference, dark, data-motion=full, CSS.supports('animation-timeline: view()') true; computed opacity of `#intro .ui-section__title` 2.8 s after load, title top / viewport height): 1440x900: 0 (1096/900, below the fold); 1440x1000: 0 (below the fold); 1920x1080: 0 (below the fold); 390x844: 0 (below the fold); 1440x1200: 0.20 (1173/1200, only 27 px of the title inside); 1920x1200: 0.20; 2560x1300: 0.42; 2560x1440: 0.68; 1024x1366: 0.56; 1440x1400: 0.61. W2-VA/e003b.cjs at 1440x1400: opacity 0.61 and rotateX -22.6 deg at load, unchanged 3 s later, 0.83 at scrollY 100, 1 at 300. So the dimmed, tilted title is clearly visible only from about 1250 px of viewport height (1440p monitors, portrait iPad Pro); between about 1190 and 1250 px only a sliver at the bottom edge shows. Cause check: git show 9d4784f -- home.css: `.kinetic` padding-top clamp(48px,9vw,120px) + two rows of font-size clamp(3.2rem,11vw,9.5rem), line-height 1.02 = 120 + 2 x 155 = about 430 px at 1440 px width, removed between FactStrip and the intro. PROGRESS.md:417 carries it as SUSPECTED (no R-id); REVIEW.md has no hit for section-title, M28 or view().
- Problem: M28 is a scroll-driven animation (`entry 0% cover 30%`), so a heading that is already inside the viewport at load starts mid-animation. Before 9d4784f the KineticBand (padding clamp(48px,9vw,120px) plus two rows of clamp(3.2rem,11vw,9.5rem) text, about 430 px at widths of 1440 px and more, computed from the removed CSS, not rendered) sat between the fact strip and #intro. Now #intro's title is higher. Measured at load on http://localhost:3000/en (puppeteer, loopback, data-motion=full, computed opacity of `#intro .ui-section__title` after 2.2 s): 1440x1000 and 1920x1080: 0; 1440x1200 and 1920x1200: 0.20; 2560x1300: 0.42; 2560x1440: 0.68; 1024x1366: 0.56; 1440x1400: 0.61 with a rotateX transform (matrix3d, about 22 degrees). It reaches 1 only after the user scrolls. PROGRESS.md:370 lists this as SUSPECTED ('M28 intro heading rise on tall desktop viewports'); this run settles the measurement.
- Impact: On 1440p monitors (viewport about 1300 px high) and on a portrait iPad Pro the first view of the intro section shows its headline dimmed and tilted until the first scroll; same family of symptom as the empty-card report of 2026-10-12.
- Fix: Owner design decision. Smallest change: end the rise inside the entry phase for headings, `animation-range: entry 0% entry 100%`, so a heading that is fully inside at load is already at its final state (all Section titles change; check the other M28 titles). Or accept and record it as intended. Verifier on the fix: The proposed `animation-range: entry 0% entry 100%` removes the symptom (injected: 1440x1400 opacity 1 at load) but changes M28 on every Section title: the title reaches opacity 1 when its top is at 84% of the viewport (755 px of 900) instead of 64% (575 px), so the rise runs over about 145 px of scroll instead of about 325 px. That is an owner design decision, as the finder says; accepting and recording the load state as intended is the alternative. motion-css-gate.test.ts:74 only checks that a rule for `.ui-section__title` exists and stay-routes.test.tsx collects class names, so neither [...]
- Fix risk: Changes the M28 look on every marketing page; stay-routes.test.tsx parses this block; verify in a browser at 1440x900 (no heading visible at load) and 2560x1440.
- Found by: R5-X1b (W2); candidate E-003
- Resolution: FIXED by T-F17 (batch B3, 2026-10-13): the M28 heading rule uses animation-range: entry 0% entry 100% (it was entry 0% cover 30%), so a heading fully in view at load is final. Evidence: test of the range (RED/GREEN as R-704); lead check in real Chromium (fix/logs/B3-lead-motion.log): at 1440x1400 and 2560x1440 the intro title is at opacity 1 on load; at 1440x900 a heading below the fold is still hidden at load and reaches 1 when scrolled well into view. docs/design/identity.md:783 follows in T-F54.

### R-716: Session-only logout, the path of every sign-in without remember-me, is proven for a single session only
- Severity: Low

L1 (L475-L512) seeds one principal and one session; its snapshots are `sessions: { total: 1, active: 1 }` then `{ total: 1, revoked: 1 }`, so a widened `where: { userId: session.userId, revokedAt: null }` would still produce the same counts. Other tests that reach revokeAuthorizationForSession use bound chains (revokeFamilyGraph path: refresh-revocation-race, regression L1275, logout L2-L6); tests/security/auth-session.test.ts mocks the repository (`revokeAuthorizationForSession: vi.fn()`, L21). portalAuthHttp.ts:L46-L49 and L55-L67 confirm that sign-in without remember-me issues no refresh token, so several session-only rows per user are a real state.
- Problem: L1 seeds one principal and one session. The session-only branch of revokeAuthorizationForSession (refreshTokenRepository.ts:586-592, taken when no refresh token has the session id) is executed by no other test: L2-L6 and the revoked-session file use bound chains, which take revokeFamilyGraph (whose family scoping is proven by the test at refresh-revoked-session-regression.test.ts:1110); tests/security/auth-session.test.ts mocks the repository; refresh-revocation-race.test.ts uses a bound chain (`grep -rln 'portal/logout\|revokeGuestSessionById\|revokeAuthorizationForSession' tests` lists five files, only the logout file drives the route). Changing `where: { id: sessionId, revokedAt: null }` (:588) to `where: { userId: session.userId, revokedAt: null }` leaves L1 green, because its snapshots contain exactly one session ({ total: 1, active: 1 } then { total: 1, revoked: 1 }). issueSessionOnly exists but is called once.
- Impact: A guest who signed in twice without remember-me (portalAuthHttp.ts:46-49 clears the refresh cookie and issues no refresh token, :55-67 only for remember) holds two session-only rows. A widened revoke on logout would end the other device as well and nothing in the suite would notice.

Verifier on the fix: Correct in substance. Prefer adding a new test (or a new case) rather than changing L1's literal expectations, since adding sessions to L1 changes its `before`/`afterFirst` totals. safeGraphState filters by userId+bookingId, so the primary principal would report sessions { total: 2, active: 1, revoked: 1 } and the isolated principal's session needs includeIsolatedPrincipal: true. Unexecuted (Docker).

### R-717: L1: the refresh 'denial' assertion cannot fail, because a refresh request without guest_rt is answered 401 before any session state is read
- Severity: Low
- Category: Tests
- Status: CONFIRMED
- Location: tests/integration/auth/logout-characterization.test.ts:L489-L491
- Evidence:
  ```

        sessionToken: session.sessionToken,
      }));
  ```
  Independent verifier (W34): logout-characterization.test.ts:L489-L491 calls performRefresh with `{ sessionToken }` only, so requestWithCookies (L274-L285) sends no guest_rt. refresh/route.ts:L121-L124 `const refresh = req.cookies.get(GUEST_REFRESH_COOKIE)?.value; if (!refresh) { return unauthorizedResponse(); }` returns 401 'Unauthorized' with both cookies cleared (L35-L39) before the limiter (L128) and before rotateRefreshToken (L137), independent of the session state. Executed: `npx vitest run --config vitest.config.ts tests/routes/portal-refresh-route.test.ts` (Node 22.19.0) -> 1 file, 6 passed, including 'never calls the limiter for a request without the refresh cookie'. `expect(refreshDenial).toEqual(EXPECTED_REFRESH_DENIAL)` (L510, 401/'Unauthorized'/cleared) is thus true whether or not logout worked; the revocation is proven only by afterFirst (L502-L508).
- Problem: performRefresh is called with a session cookie only. The route returns unauthorizedResponse() as soon as the guest_rt cookie is missing (src/app/api/portal/refresh/route.ts:121-124), before the limiter and before rotateRefreshToken, so the result is identical whether or not the session was revoked. Executed: `npx vitest run --config vitest.config.ts tests/routes/portal-refresh-route.test.ts` -> 6 passed, including 'never calls the limiter for a request without the refresh cookie' (401, rotateRefreshToken not called). `expect(refreshDenial).toEqual(EXPECTED_REFRESH_DENIAL)` at :510 therefore proves nothing about the revoked session; the revocation itself is proven only by afterFirst (:502-508). A real refresh-based denial needs a guest_rt cookie, which the session-only fixture does not have.
- Impact: No wrong result today. The assertion reads as 'a logged-out session cannot be used to refresh' but would stay green if logout did nothing, so a maintainer gets false assurance; the actual access check (verifyGuestSessionAccess on the revoked row) is never exercised in L1.

Verifier on the fix: Correct. verifyGuestSessionAccess(parseGuestSession(token)) returns null for a revoked row (guestSession.ts:L151-L154) while the JWT still parses (not expired, valid signature); sessionModule is already loaded and used the same way at L384. Prefer replacing the vacuous refresh call over dropping it, so the revoked-session access check is exercised. Unexecuted (Docker).
- Fix risk: Test only; verifyGuestSessionAccess returns null for a revoked row (guestSession.ts:151-154).

### R-719: Lock order of revokeFamilyForToken (logout and sign-in revocation) is not pinned by any concurrent integration test
- Severity: Low
- Category: Tests
- Status: CONFIRMED
- Location: tests/integration/auth/refresh-revocation-race.test.ts:L274-L277
- Evidence:
  ```
  revocationPromise = revokeRepository.revokeAuthorizationForSession(
                ROOT_CREDENTIAL_ID,
                'race_test_revocation',
              );
  ```
  Independent verifier (W34): Read refreshTokenRepository.ts:L616-L647: `if (!(await lockUser(tx, initial.userId)) || !(await lockFamily(tx, initial.familyId)))` at L632, so no defect today (User then Family, same as rotate L382 and revokeAuthorizationForSession L581/L586). Comment L133-L135 states the order. refresh-revocation-race.test.ts only calls revokeRepository.revokeAuthorizationForSession (L274-L277, L303-L306). `grep -rn 'revokeRefreshFamily|revokeFamilyForToken' tests src` shows callers: logout route L21, portalAuthHttp.ts:L43, and in tests only vi.fn() mocks (tests/security/portal-auth-client-identity.test.ts, client-identity-route-regression.test.ts) plus two single awaited calls (logout-characterization.test.ts:L576, refresh-revoked-session-regression.test.ts:L1176). Every performLogout call (L482-L686) is serial. tests/unit/guest-data-store.test.ts and phone-lookup-parity.test.ts mock the repository as `{}`; no unit test runs the real repository. So a flipped lock order in revokeFamilyForToken cannot be detected by any current test (an inversion needs two concurrent transactions). The consequence (PostgreSQL deadlock abort) is standard behaviour and was not executed.
- Problem: The comment at src/lib/prisma-repositories/refreshTokenRepository.ts:L133-L135 says every issuance, rotation and revocation path takes the User row lock and then the Family row lock. This file pins that order with PostgreSQL barriers (waitForDatabaseLock L157-L187: first a FOR UPDATE wait on refresh_token_families, then a FOR UPDATE wait on users) only for rotate() and revokeAuthorizationForSession(); L274 and L303 are the only revocation entry points the file exercises. The other revocation function, revokeFamilyForToken (refreshTokenRepository.ts:L616-L647, lockUser then lockFamily at L632), is the path of POST /api/portal/logout (src/app/api/portal/logout/route.ts:L21) and of every sign-in that presents a refresh cookie (src/lib/portalAuthHttp.ts:L43). grep -rn 'revokeRefreshFamily|revokeFamilyForToken' tests finds it only in vi.fn() mocks (tests/security/portal-auth-client-identity.test.ts, tests/security/client-identity-route-regression.test.ts) and in two single awaited calls with nothing running beside them (tests/integration/auth/logout-characterization.test.ts:L576 and tests/integration/auth/refresh-revoked-session-regression.test.ts:L1176). No test interleaves it with rotate().
- Impact: No defect in the code today: revokeFamilyForToken takes lockUser and then lockFamily, matching rotate. The gap is regression cover. If that function were changed to take the family lock first, or lost the user lock, every integration gate would stay green, although User->Family against Family->User is exactly the deadlock the comment at L133-L135 exists to prevent (PostgreSQL would abort one of the two transactions after deadlock_timeout, so a logout or a refresh would fail with a 500). This is reasoning about lock behaviour; it was not executed.
- Fix: Parametrize executeRace (L222-L352) with the revocation call and add one case per ordering that calls revokeRepository.revokeFamilyForToken(`${ROOT_CREDENTIAL_ID}.${ROOT_SECRET}`, 'race_test_revocation'). The expected result and RaceState are the same as for the two existing orderings (revocationResult true, familyReason 'race_test_revocation'). No existing assertion is removed or weakened (O36/O46). Verifier on the fix: Correct. I traced both orderings for revokeFamilyForToken: revoke-first blocks on the family lock held by the blocker (query contains "refresh_token_families" and FOR UPDATE), then rotate reaches "users" held by the first pid and ends invalid; refresh-first rotates, then the revocation takes both locks, finds the root token (revokedAt is not checked there), and revokeFamilyGraph writes the reason, giving the same RaceState as the existing cases (familyReason 'race_test_revocation', revocationResult true). The reason must be passed explicitly (default is 'logout'). fixRisk is fair: test-only, [...]
- Fix risk: Test-only; needs Docker through npm run test:integration. Pass the reason argument explicitly because the function defaults to 'logout'. One repetition per ordering is enough because the barrier makes the interleaving deterministic; each repetition costs one fresh database plus migrations.

The only audit assertion in the two files is for the genuine replay (refresh-revoked-session-regression.test.ts:770-777). `grep -rn authorization_chain_revoked tests` finds nothing, and docs/testing.md:108 calls a request that re-reads an already-revoked predecessor a completed replay, so the quiet branch is also undocumented, although it was added on purpose (git log -S: 4c28aa4, c604ac2). The reason stays 'logout' (the repository default at L619) and afterEach clears the audit table, so the count starts at 0. ### R-723: Claim race tests never race two distinct grants of one booking: the booking-level single-owner guard and the sibling-revoke deadlock/retry path are exercised by no test
- Severity: Low
- Category: Tests
- Status: SUSPECTED
- Location: tests/integration/auth/support/claim-route-worker.ts:L171
- Evidence:
  `body: JSON.stringify({ claimToken: CLAIM_RACE_TOKEN }),`
  Independent verifier (W34): claim-route-worker.ts:L171 and L10/L231: both actors of A2 and A3 exchange with the same CLAIM_RACE_TOKEN (the claim then uses that exchange cookie); CLAIM_RACE_SIBLING_TOKEN appears only in the redaction list (L231) and the fixture/state reads (claim-concurrency L30, L171, L235). `grep -rn 'consumeBookingClaimGrant\|claims/route' tests` outside mocked security tests lists only serial callers (claim-lifecycle, guest-access-reset, claim-ineligible-window, portal-eligibility-consistency:L234). In portalAuthService.ts the grant guard `if (consumed.count !== 1) throw new PortalAuthError('INVALID_CLAIM')` (L259) already decides a race on one grant row, so the booking guard `OR: [{ userId: null }, { userId }]` + `claimed.count !== 1` (L261-L268) and `{ isolationLevel: 'Serializable' }` (L304) cannot change the outcome of A2/A3. With two grants, sibling revoke (L270-L273) updates the other grant row after the booking row while the other claimant holds that grant row and waits for the booking row, an inversion that PostgreSQL resolves with 40P01. Installed @prisma/adapter-pg 7.10.0 index.js:L539-L542 maps `case "40001": case "40P01":` to kind TransactionWriteConflict, and @prisma/client 7.10.0 runtime/client.js maps TransactionWriteConflict to "P2034" ('write conflict or a deadlock. Please retry'), which isSerializationConflict (L39-L44) retries (L306-L312, 3 attempts). The 'tests stay green under mutation' part rests on PostgreSQL row-lock semantics and was not executed.
- Problem: Both actors of both scenarios (A2, A3) exchange and claim with the same CLAIM_RACE_TOKEN; the worker has no per-actor token. The sibling grant seeded at claim-concurrency-characterization.test.ts:168-174 and CLAIM_RACE_SIBLING_TOKEN are used only for state assertions and the redaction lists (git grep: claim-concurrency:30,171,235; worker:10,231). With one contested grant row, the single-use guard `if (consumed.count !== 1) throw new PortalAuthError('INVALID_CLAIM')` (src/lib/portalAuthService.ts:259) alone, or the Serializable option (:304) alone, already yields one winner and one 401. By reading every path, A2/A3 therefore stay green if the booking-level guard (`OR: [{ userId: null }, { userId }]` plus `claimed.count !== 1`, :261-268) were removed. Two open grants with different channels (REMOTE + ONSITE, as claim-lifecycle-characterization.test.ts:179-195 seeds them) claimed concurrently by different identities contest the booking row instead. There, 'revoke siblings' (:270-273) touches the other grant row after the booking row while the other claimant holds that grant row and waits for the booking row: a lock-order inversion that PostgreSQL resolves with a deadlock abort (40P01). @prisma/adapter-pg maps 40001 and 40P01 to TransactionWriteConflict (node_modules/@prisma/adapter-pg/dist/index.js:539-542), which isSerializationConflict (:39-44) retries (:306-312). A repo-wide search found no integration test that races two claims (git grep -n 'consumeBookingClaimGrant|claims/route' -- tests/integration lists only serial callers).
- Impact: If a refactor weakened the Serializable option or the booking guard, every claim test would stay green while two identities could each obtain a session for one booking, the later claimant overwriting booking.userId. The deadlock-retry recovery would also stay unverified. Production code looks correct by reading, so this is a missing proof, not a known bug.
- Fix: Add a third race scenario ('a4') in the same harness: actor a claims with CLAIM_RACE_TOKEN, actor b with CLAIM_RACE_SIBLING_TOKEN (seed the sibling with channel 'ONSITE'), distinct phones. Block on `SELECT ... FROM "bookings" WHERE "id" = ... FOR UPDATE` and match /UPDATE[\s\S]*"bookings"/i in waitForBlockedWorkers. Expect one 200, one 401, users 1, booking owner = winner, the winner's grant consumed and the other grant revoked. Verifier on the fix: Plausible and well formed. The barrier must hold the bookings row (`SELECT ... FROM "bookings" ... FOR UPDATE`) and waitForBlockedWorkers needs a /UPDATE[\s\S]*"bookings"/i branch; the sibling token must be seeded as a second open grant (it already is, same REMOTE channel, so no channel change is strictly needed). By my trace the deadlock victim retries and finds its grant revoked by the winner, giving 200 plus 401 (not 409), as the finder expects. Expect about 1 s per repetition for deadlock_timeout; the 5 s lock_timeout (prismaPgConfig.ts:L13) is higher, so it does not fire first. [...]
- Fix risk: Test code only; needs Docker (npm run test:integration). Expect about 1 s extra per repetition for PostgreSQL's default deadlock_timeout; keep repetitions modest (5-10) and CLAIM_WORKER_TIMEOUT_MS unchanged. The worker's 5 s lock_timeout (src/lib/prismaPgConfig.ts:13) is above deadlock_timeout, so it does not fire first.
- To confirm: In a scratch copy remove the `OR` guard at portalAuthService.ts:L261-L268 and the Serializable option at L304, run the integration suite, and see whether A2/A3 stay green; then add the 'a4' race (two distinct grants, distinct phones, barrier on UPDATE "bookings") and check that it goes red with the mutation and green without it. Run request: Lead, Docker: after the scratch-copy mutation described in toConfirm, run `npm run test:integration` (the runner takes no file filter; tests/integration/run.ts runs vitest.integration.config.ts) and report whether claim-concurrency-characterization A2/A3 stay green.
- Found by: R5-U21 (W34); candidate G-005
- Resolution: DEFERRED-OWNER (economy): SUSPECTED; the reproduction command is recorded in decision-D13.json (leadReproduce) and was not run under the owner's instruction of 2026-10-13 to watch the consumption; a confirmed reproduction would become the conditional task T-F65.

### R-727: Health probe pg_isready uses the Unix socket, so the container can turn healthy while the entrypoint's temporary server (no TCP) is up; the harness then makes one TCP connect without retry
- Severity: Low
- Category: Concurrency
- Status: CONFIRMED
- Location: tests/integration/support/database-lifecycle.ts:L234
- Evidence:
  `'--health-cmd', 'pg_isready --username="$POSTGRES_USER" --dbname="$POSTGRES_DB"',`
  Independent verifier (W34): LEAD REPRODUCTION (2026-10-13, executed by the lead on a throwaway container from the local postgres:16-alpine image, no network, script .runtime/review5/w0/health-probe2.sh): sampling every 50 ms inside the container during its first start gave 9 samples socket=no tcp=no, then 2 samples socket=yes tcp=no (the entrypoint's temporary server listens on the unix socket only), then 2 samples socket=no tcp=no (the restart gap), then 187 samples socket=yes tcp=yes. So a health command that asks over the unix socket can report ready before the real server accepts TCP connections. The window is about 0.1-0.25 s wide: a first run with the real health command at a 1 s interval (.runtime/review5/w0/health-probe.sh) saw health turn healthy together with TCP, so the effect is a rare flake, not a constant failure. Verifier: Code read: database-lifecycle.ts L234 `'--health-cmd', 'pg_isready --username="$POSTGRES_USER" --dbname="$POSTGRES_DB"'` (no --host, so the default Unix socket; the container mounts --tmpfs /run/postgresql), L235 interval 1s; L264-L265 `await waitForHealthyContainer(runtime); await assertDisposableContainer(runtime);` (the latter re-checks Docker state only, database-safety.ts L302-L306); then withVerifiedDisposableDatabase -> connect() (database-safety.ts L309-L322: one `client.connect()`, no retry), whose catch maps every non-guard error to 'the live database fingerprint could not be verified' (L384-L388). The same pg_isready-on-socket pattern is used in docker-compose.yml L14 and docker/docker-compose.prod.yml L42. The premise that the official image's init phase runs a temporary server with listen_addresses='' (socket only) comes from the docker-library/postgres entrypoint, recalled from memory, not verifiable offline here. Counter-evidence: the baseline run [...]
- Problem: The health command has no --host, so pg_isready probes the default Unix socket. The official image's entrypoint (docker-entrypoint.sh in docker-library/postgres; recalled from memory, not verifiable offline) runs initdb, then a temporary server started with listen_addresses='' (socket only) to create POSTGRES_DB, stops it, and only then execs the real server. A probe that lands while the temporary server is up reports healthy; waitForHealthyContainer accepts the first healthy (database-lifecycle.ts:146), assertDisposableContainer re-checks only Docker's status, and startDisposablePostgres then makes exactly one TCP connect (database-safety.ts:309-322, no retry) through withVerifiedDisposableDatabase, whose catch maps every connect error to 'the live database fingerprint could not be verified' (database-safety.ts:384-388). The probe interval is 1 s (line 235).
- Impact: A spurious, fail-closed start-up failure (container removed, exit code 1) whose message hides that the cause was a refused or reset connection. Whether it happens depends on init speed relative to the 1 s probe interval: on a fast host init may finish before the first probe; on a slower or loaded host a probe can fall into the temporary-server window. No safety impact. The one baseline run (.runtime/review5/w0/integration.log, 23 files / 125 tests) shows no failure, and PROGRESS.md records no intermittent integration failure, so the rate is unknown.
- Fix: Make healthy imply the transport the harness uses: add --host=127.0.0.1 to the probe ('pg_isready --host=127.0.0.1 --username="$POSTGRES_USER" --dbname="$POSTGRES_DB"'), because the temporary server never listens on TCP. Optionally retry the first connect() for ECONNREFUSED/ECONNRESET inside the existing bounded deadline and include error.code (not the URL) in the rejection reason. Verifier on the fix: If the premise holds, adding `--host=127.0.0.1` to the probe is the standard fix (the temporary server does not listen on TCP; the final server listens on '*' in the official image). Optionally retry the first connect() for ECONNREFUSED/ECONNRESET inside a bounded deadline and include error.code (not the URL) in the reason. Fix risk fair (needs Docker; several consecutive starts). Keep Low at most: fail-closed, no safety effect, rerun is the cost. Do not change before the lead has measured it.
- Fix risk: The real server listens on all addresses in the official image after init, so a loopback TCP probe works; confirm with several consecutive npm run test:integration start-ups on Docker (needs Docker, lead only). docs/testing.md step 4 ('Wait on Docker health and a real PostgreSQL fingerprint') stays accurate.
- Found by: R5-U24b (W34); candidate G-022
- Resolution: DEFERRED-OWNER (economy): not done under the owner's instruction of 2026-10-13 to watch the consumption; specified in decision-D13.json (.runtime/review5/fix/) as task T-F37, resumable on request.

### R-729: sanitizeDatabaseDiagnostics prints only AggregateError.message, so run.ts shows one generic sentence and drops both causes when setup or teardown fails twice
- Severity: Low
