  Independent verifier (W34): database-safety.ts L401: `let text = value instanceof Error ? value.message : String(value);`. database-lifecycle.ts L295-L299 (setup + cleanup both failed) and L361-L371 (teardown) throw `new AggregateError([...], 'fixed sentence')`; run.ts L98-L101 and L108-L112 print them only via sanitizeDatabaseDiagnostics. Executed with tsx under Node 22.19.0: AggregateError([Error('connect ECONNREFUSED 127.0.0.1:49321 secret'), Error('the runner-issued Docker container cannot be inspected')], 'Database teardown verification and exact-container removal both failed closed.') -> sanitizeDatabaseDiagnostics(agg, ['secret']) returned exactly "Database teardown verification and exact-container removal both failed closed."; a second AggregateError with causes 'x','y' returned only its message. Broader than reported: the single-failure teardown variant (L366-L368, `errors: [databaseError]`, message 'Database teardown verification failed; the exact disposable container was removed.') also drops the only cause (the guard rejection or connection error), so the operator never sees why teardown verification failed. Precedent for the same pattern in production code: R-603 (bookingOutbox AggregateError message without causes), fixed by putting causes into the message.
- Problem: database-lifecycle.ts:295-299 (setup failed and exact-container cleanup also failed) and :366-371 (teardown verification and container removal both failed) throw an AggregateError whose causes live in .errors; the setup cause is even pre-sanitized (:282, :296), so it was meant to be shown. run.ts prints both throws only through sanitizeDatabaseDiagnostics (run.ts:98-101 and 109-112), which reads only .message. Executed (tsx, Node 22.19.0) with an AggregateError built like database-lifecycle.ts:366: sanitizeDatabaseDiagnostics(agg, ['secret']) returned exactly 'Database teardown verification and exact-container removal both failed closed.' - the two inner messages are gone.
- Impact: When start-up fails and the exact-container cleanup then cannot verify the container (for example the container died while starting: with --rm it is already removed, so docker inspect fails), the operator sees only '[integration] Disposable PostgreSQL setup failed and exact-container cleanup also failed closed.' with no cause, and the wording suggests a leftover container that may not exist. The dedicated message 'Disposable PostgreSQL exited before becoming healthy.' (database-lifecycle.ts:147-149) is probably unreachable for the same reason (SUSPECTED, Docker timing not run). The same loss applies to '[integration] Cleanup failed closed: ...'. Diagnosis needs docker ps and a manual re-run.
- Fix: In database-safety.ts add a recursive helper and use it for the first line of sanitizeDatabaseDiagnostics: +function diagnosticText(value: unknown): string { + if (value instanceof AggregateError) { + return [value.message, ...value.errors.map(diagnosticText)].join(' | '); + } + return value instanceof Error ? value.message : String(value); +} ... - let text = value instanceof Error ? value.message : String(value); + let text = diagnosticText(value); Add a unit test beside 'redacts connection URLs and credentials from diagnostics' in tests/unit/integration-database-safety.test.ts: an AggregateError with two inner errors, one containing the password, must show both reasons and not the password. Verifier on the fix: Correct. A recursive diagnosticText() that joins message and errors keeps the existing URL regex, per-secret redaction loop and 12,000-character tail, so unsanitized inner errors (teardown) stay redacted; the setup cause is pre-sanitized already. Alternative equally minimal: put the causes into the AggregateError message in database-lifecycle.ts (as R-603's fix), but then each inner message must be sanitized there. Add the unit test beside 'redacts connection URLs and credentials' (L244) with an AggregateError containing the password in one cause. Diagnostics-only; no exit code change.
- Fix risk: Diagnostics text only. The combined text still goes through the same URL regex, the per-secret redaction loop and the 12,000-character tail cut, so secrets inside inner errors (the teardown inner errors are not pre-sanitized) are still removed. No behaviour or exit-code change.

- Severity: Nit
- Category: Redundant

- Location: public/sw.js:L81-L83
- Evidence:
  ```
  function scriptSrcs(html) {
    return [...html.matchAll(/<script\b[^>]*\bsrc="([^"]+)"/gu)].map((match) => match[1]);
  }
  ```
  Independent verifier (W1b): sw.js L81-83 scriptSrcs matches every `<script ... src="...">`. Installed Next 16.3.8, node_modules/next/dist/server/app-render/app-render.js L1893-1900 and L4909-4916: `polyfills = buildManifest.polyfillFiles.filter(...).map(polyfill => ({ src: ..., crossOrigin, noModule: true, nonce }))`. Dev HTML cached by the real worker (Chromium) contains `<script src="/_next/static/chunks/node_modules_next_dist_build_polyfills_polyfill-nomodule.js" noModule="">` and the install put it in the cache (cache listing, 39 entries). Local production build (.next/build-manifest.json): polyfillFiles ["static/chunks/0cz1d0mv5g_q7.js"], 112,594 bytes, 39,490 gzipped (production HTML not run). Browsers that support service workers and module scripts do not fetch nomodule scripts. The proposed regex /<script\b(?![^>]*\bnoModule\b)[^>]*\bsrc="([^"]+)"/giu, run on sample HTML, drops noModule tags (attribute before or after src) and keeps normal ones including the &amp; query one.
- Problem: scriptSrcs (T05, R-381) takes every <script src>. Next marks the polyfill chunk noModule (node_modules/next/dist/server/app-render/app-render.js L1899 and L4915, noModule: true; dev HTML: <script src="/_next/static/chunks/node_modules_next_dist_build_polyfills_polyfill-nomodule.js" noModule="">), and the real install put it in the cache (list in browser-lifecycle.cjs output). In the local production build .next/build-manifest.json names polyfillFiles static/chunks/0cz1d0mv5g_q7.js: 112,594 bytes, 39,490 gzipped (production HTML not run).
- Impact: About 39 KB gzipped is fetched on every worker install (first visit and every deploy) and never used; any browser with service workers and Promise.allSettled supports module scripts and skips noModule scripts.
- Fix: Skip tags that carry noModule, e.g. match /<script\b(?![^>]*\bnoModule\b)[^>]*\bsrc="([^"]+)"/giu, and add a case with a noModule script to the R-381 test. Verifier on the fix: The regex fix is correct and tested by me on sample HTML; add a noModule case to the R-381 test (tests/unit/service-worker.test.ts L134-168) and check the production offline page's script list once, as the fixRisk says. Severity Nit agreed (about 39 KB gzipped once per install).
- Fix risk: Very low; if Next ever loads that file for a module-capable browser, hydration offline would depend on it, so check the production offline page's script list once.
- Found by: R5-U16 (W1b); candidate B-015
- Resolution: FIXED by T-F15 (batch B3, 2026-10-13): script tags that carry the noModule attribute (any case or position, bare or self-closing; `nomodule-ui.js` as a path or data-nomodule-* attributes do not count) are neither requested nor stored. Evidence: tests for each spelling (fix/logs/T-F15-green.log); lead check on the production build: the polyfill chunk /_next/static/chunks/0cz1d0mv5g_q7.js carries noModule and is not in the cache while the 13 module scripts are (fix/logs/B3-lead-precache.log).

### R-746: A scanner run that exits 1 with an empty report (gitleaks partial scan) is accepted as a clean scan
- Severity: Nit (the finder said Low: The code-side acceptance is real, but I could not make the pinned gitleaks 8.30.1 produce exit 1 with an empty report under the gate's arguments, and the finder's listed triggers (read error, [...])
- Category: Error handling
- Status: SUSPECTED
- Location: scripts/check-secrets.mjs:L310-L312
- Evidence:
  ```
  if (!Array.isArray(report)) {
      throw new Error('The maintained secret scanner produced an invalid evidence shape.');
    }
  ```
  Independent verifier (W2): LEAD ATTEMPT (2026-10-13): gitleaks 8.30.1 (the checksum-locked local binary) run on a scratch directory with one readable file and one file with mode 000, report seeded with [] : it exited 0, wrote [] and printed nothing at --log-level error, so an unreadable file does not produce the exit 1 plus empty report case; no input that makes gitleaks exit 1 with an empty report was found, and the claim stays SUSPECTED (the code path in check-secrets.mjs does accept status 1 with an empty array). Verifier: scripts/check-secrets.mjs L276-L312: runGitleaks accepts status 0 or 1, parses the report, and checks only Array.isArray(report); the report is seeded '' (L360, R-420 fix), so only a report that was never written is rejected. That the gate accepts exit 1 + '[]' is true by reading. Reachability: gitleaks v8.30.1 cmd/root.go findingSummaryAndExit writes the report first and exits 1 afterwards when err != nil (fetched). But the err comes only from DetectSource's Fragments result (detect/detect.go, fetched: per-fragment errors are 'Log the error and move on to the next fragment ... return nil', final `return d.Findings(), err`), and sources/file.go (fetched) yields read and filetype errors through yield, i.e. the logged-and-continue path, not the return path; walk errors in sources/files.go are logged and skipped with `return nil`. The non-nil returns are context cancellation and archive-extraction errors. My real runs of the pinned binary ($HOME/.local/share/gitleaks/8.30.1/gitleaks, gate arguments, repo gitleaks.toml, scratch trees): a mode-000 unreadable file + dangling symlink -> exit 0, report []; corrupt .zip/.tar/.tar.gz with default args and with --max-archive-depth 3 -> exit 0, report [], empty stderr. So a skipped unreadable file yields exit 0 (a different silent [...]
- Problem: R-420's fix handles only the 'report never written' case (empty seed, L299-L306). The comment at L299 itself says exit 1 means findings or fatal errors. In gitleaks v8.30.1 (cmd/root.go, fetched from raw.githubusercontent.com at the tag with the WebFetch tool) findingSummaryAndExit first writes the report ('if detector.Reporter != nil { ... os.Create(detector.ReportPath) ... Reporter.Write(file, findings)') and only afterwards does 'if err != nil { os.Exit(1) }', before the findings check, so a scan that fails midway leaves exit 1 plus a valid report that may be '[]'. The pinned binary contains the matching strings 'failed to scan directory' and 'no leaks found in partial scan' (`strings` dump, binary not run). runGitleaks accepts status 0 or 1 and then trusts the report. Execution with a fake scanner (a shell script, not gitleaks, scratch dir .../scratchpad/review5/R5-U18/fk, tool.lock rewritten for it): mode clean => ACCEPTED (unexpected=0 stale=0); mode partial (stderr 'ERR failed to scan directory', report '[]', exit 1) => ACCEPTED (unexpected=0 stale=0); mode nowrite => REJECTED ('did not produce valid JSON evidence. Scanner stderr: ...').
- Impact: If a read error ends a scan midway (v8.30.1 sources/file.go returns 'could not read file' when no bytes were read; a filetype detection error or a cancelled context do the same), the gate prints SECRET SCAN PASSED although later files were never scanned. For the sources scope the stale allowlist entries usually expose a scan that stopped early; the artifact scope has no such cross-check. Probability is low: the copies are regular files made by the same user with mode 0600.
- Fix: After the shape check add the invariant that exit status 1 and a non-empty report go together (gitleaks exits 1 for findings, default --exit-code 1): `if ((result.status === 1) !== (report.length > 0)) { throw new Error('The maintained secret scanner exit status contradicts its report.'); }`. Prototype against the fake scanner: clean accepted, partial rejected, no-report rejected, a findings report still returned as unexpected. Verifier on the fix: The invariant is cheap and fail-closed, but it targets a state I could not reach, and it would not catch the silent per-file skips that I could reach (exit 0, stderr only at error level which the gate discards). If the owner wants the hardening, a better target is also to surface scanner stderr or compare scanned-file counts; otherwise leave as is. ### R-752: Nit group (2): unconditional --no-sandbox in the responsive audit; duplicated report-writing block
- Severity: Nit
- Category: Maintainability
- Status: CONFIRMED
- Location: scripts/responsive-ux-audit.ts:L645
- Evidence:
  `args: ['--no-sandbox', '--disable-dev-shm-usage', '--disable-gpu', ...LOCAL_ONLY_ARGS],`
  Independent verifier (W34): (a) scripts/responsive-ux-audit.ts:645 `args: ['--no-sandbox', '--disable-dev-shm-usage', '--disable-gpu', ...LOCAL_ONLY_ARGS]`; axe-a11y.ts:55 and audit-vitals.ts:223 launch with only LOCAL_ONLY_ARGS (grep -n 'puppeteer.launch'). `git log -S'--no-sandbox'` -> d2d8e2b (only that commit); not mentioned in REVIEW.md/PROGRESS.md/docs. The browser reaches only loopback (LOCAL_ONLY_ARGS plus blockNonLocalRequests lines 108-139), so exposure is small. (b) Launch-failure branch lines 654-698 and the normal path lines 790-815 both build an AuditReport, write the same JSON and MD paths and log the two report paths; read side by side, confirmed (the failure branch has one different closing log line and sets exitCode). Caveat on (a), from general knowledge of Puppeteer/Chrome behaviour and not verified here: non-root Linux hosts that restrict unprivileged user namespaces (for example Ubuntu 23.10+ AppArmor) also need --no-sandbox, so the claim that it is only needed as root in Docker is too strong.
- Problem: (a) Only this script (of the three Puppeteer audits) disables the Chrome sandbox, for every user and platform; axe-a11y.ts:55 and audit-vitals.ts:223 launch with the sandbox. The browser loads only loopback pages (non-local requests are aborted), so exposure is small. The Linux container flags are only needed when running as root in Docker. (b) The launch-failure branch (lines 654-698) repeats the report object, the two writeFile calls and the three log lines of the normal path (lines 790-810).
- Impact: (a) A weaker browser sandbox on developer machines for no gain. (b) The two copies can drift when a report field is added.
- Fix: (a) Add '--no-sandbox' only when process.getuid?.() === 0 or when an env var asks for it. (b) Move the report building and writing into one function used by both paths. Verifier on the fix: (b) is a safe pure refactor if the owner wants it (one helper writeReport); not worth a task alone. (a) is riskier than stated: gating --no-sandbox on uid 0 or an env switch could break non-root Linux runs where userns are restricted, and the benefit on the owner's macOS machine is nil. Recommend leaving (a) and only batching (b) with a later edit of this file.
- Fix risk: (a) Linux CI as root needs the env switch. (b) Pure refactor; compare the JSON of a launch-failure run before and after.
- Found by: R5-U27 (W34); candidate H-011
- Resolution: FIXED for part (b) by T-F03 (batch B1, 2026-10-13): the report building and writing is one writeReport function used by the normal and the launch-failure path (the JSON and Markdown outputs are identical apart from the timestamp: hashes d25eee481afc and 3cd500c0769f before and after, fix/logs/T-F03-launchfail-compare.log). Part (a), the unconditional --no-sandbox, is DECLINED as the Phase 1 verifier advised: gating it on uid 0 or an env switch could break non-root Linux runs with restricted user namespaces and brings nothing on the owner's macOS machine; the browser loads loopback pages only.

### R-753: The production-image smoke never requests /_next/image, so the sharp/libvips files that the sharp 0.35.5 and next 16.3.8 bump relies on are not proven to be in the runner image by any gate
- Severity: Nit (the finder said Low: The finder's impact is wrong for the installed Next 16.3.8. When sharp cannot be loaded, optimizeImage throws inside the try at node_modules/next/dist/server/image-optimizer.js L1370; the catch at [...])
- Category: Tests
- Status: SUSPECTED
- Location: scripts/smoke-production-image.ts:L6-L7
- Evidence:
  ```
  * directory, and checks the container the way a release would be used: migrations, health,
   * security headers, CSP report intake, service worker + offline fallback, cross-origin images,
  ```
  Independent verifier (W2): git grep -n -E '_next/image|sharp' -- scripts tests docker docs/deployment: no gate fetches /_next/image (only tests/unit/service-worker.test.ts L320-338 with a stub fetch). Docker/sharp: next.config.ts L8-14 forces sharp into the trace; package.json L140-141 has sharp 0.35.5 under optionalDependencies; docker/Dockerfile.security has no 'sharp' line (builder `npm ci` on node:22-alpine, runner copies .next/standalone). scripts/smoke-production-image.ts checks: images present, security headers (L220-230 img-src/COEP), version.json, SW, offline, and 'no CSP violation or console error' (L341-346). Puppeteer 25.12.0 (cdp/Page.js L456-L464) turns Log.entryAdded into console events, so an HTTP 4xx/5xx image on /en/moments would fail that check, but a sharp-less fallback returns 200, so the check cannot catch it either. The proposed fix check (status 200 + content-type image/*) is also blind to the fallback: with Accept */* getSupportedMimeType returns '' and the upstream jpeg is returned as image/jpeg in both cases. Needs Docker to prove anything about the musl image.
- Problem: Seven site components use next/image (ApartmentGallery, GalleryLightbox, GuideCard, GuideDetail, PhonesDirectory, BalconyWindow, RoomsShowcase) and the service worker caches `/_next/image` URLs, so the photos depend on the Next image optimizer and sharp in the standalone output; next.config.ts forces sharp into the trace with `outputFileTracingIncludes`. `git grep -n -E '_next/image|sharp' -- scripts tests docker docs/deployment` shows no gate that fetches `/_next/image`: the smoke's 'cross-origin images' wording refers to the img-src/COEP header check at lines 227-230, not to the optimizer, and tests/unit only exercise the service worker with a stub fetch. A local darwin build in .next/standalone does contain node_modules/sharp, @img/colour, detect-libc and semver (ls, names only), so tracing works on this machine; the Alpine/musl image (@img/sharp-linuxmusl-x64 and its libvips package) was not inspected because Docker is not allowed here.
- Impact: If the musl sharp binary or libvips were missing or unloadable in the runner image (for example after the planned Next security bump of 2026-10-14, task T60), every optimized photo would fail in production while all 23 smoke checks stay green.
- Fix: Add one check after 'version.json': fetch `${BASE}/_next/image?url=%2Fhouse%2Fbalcony%2Fbalcony_2.jpeg&w=640&q=75` with the identity headers and assert status 200 and a `content-type` starting with `image/`. Verifier on the fix: The idea of one /_next/image check in the smoke is right, but the proposed assertion is insufficient. It must send `Accept: image/webp` and assert `content-type: image/webp` (default images.formats is ['image/webp'], and the fallback returns the upstream image/jpeg), optionally also that the body is smaller than public/house/balcony/balcony_2.jpeg. Needs the image build and Docker, so the lead runs it. Fix risk is fair (width must be in Next's default sizes, q=75 allowed, the file must stay in the catalogue, the check count in docs/deployment/production-image-smoke.md changes).
- Fix risk: Needs the image build and Docker (lead). The URL must use a width in Next's default sizes and q=75 (the Next 16 default qualities), and the file must stay in the catalogue; the check count in the docs/deployment/production-image-smoke.md list changes.
- To confirm: Build the images and run the smoke or `docker run` the runner image, then request /_next/image?url=%2Fhouse%2Fbalcony%2Fbalcony_2.jpeg&w=640&q=75 with Accept: image/webp. image/webp means sharp works; image/jpeg with 200 means the silent fallback (check `docker logs` for the sharp error). Run request: Lead with Docker: npm run docker:build, start the smoke project, curl -H 'Accept: image/webp' -H 'x-origin-proxy-attestation: ...' -H 'x-origin-verified-client-ip: 127.0.0.1' 'http://localhost:3002/_next/image?url=%2Fhouse%2Fbalcony%2Fbalcony_2.jpeg&w=640&q=75' -D - -o /dev/null and read content-type
- Found by: R5-U19 (W2); candidate D-009
- Resolution: DEFERRED-OWNER (decision D13): At the next release build (docker:build needs registry access), with the smoke project up, run: curl -H 'Accept: image/webp' plus the identity headers 'http://localhost:3002/_next/image?url=%2Fhouse%2Fbalcony%2Fbalcony_2.jpeg&w=640&q=75' -D - -o /dev/null. Confirm content-type image/webp. If it is image/jpeg or an error, the lead records a new finding and adds a smoke check. If no answer: No /_next/image smoke check.

A throw there runs the finally (browser close, compose down, rm) and rejects main() before the loop at L425-430 prints `results`; L433 `process.exitCode = await main();` (top-level await) then ends the process with the error and exit code 1 (so no gate is weakened; 'unhandled rejection' is the finder's wording, the effect is an uncaught top-level-await rejection). If Chrome cannot start, the exception leaves the try block, the finally block tears the stack down, and main() rejects before the result loop at L425-L430 runs; 'process.exitCode = await main()' (L433) then ends with an unhandled rejection. ### R-755: `up` starts the dev server before checking that curl exists, so a missing curl leaves the app running after a fatal exit
- Severity: Nit (the finder said Low: The ordering defect is real, but it needs a machine without curl; curl ships with macOS and every mainstream Linux, the README targets 'macOS or Linux shell', and the consequence is a stray dev [...])
- Category: Error handling
- Status: CONFIRMED
- Location: scripts/system-orchestrator.sh:L624-L625
- Evidence:
  ```
  wait_for_runtime() {
    require_cmd curl
  ```
  Independent verifier (W34): cmd_up (L757-767): `run_bootstrap_sequence; start_app; if (( SKIP_VERIFY )) ... return; fi; verify_runtime`. require_cmd curl is the first statement of wait_for_runtime (L624-625). run_preflight (L719-733) checks node and npm only (check_node_and_npm_versions, L222-242), and no other curl check precedes start_app (grep -n curl scripts/system-orchestrator.sh: L625 require_cmd, the probes in wait_for_runtime, and the `command -v curl` guard in cmd_status). cmd_restart is cmd_down + cmd_up, so it repeats. Not covered by any REVIEW.md finding. Not executed (no real start_app run); established by reading every path.
- Problem: cmd_up (L757-767) runs run_bootstrap_sequence, then start_app (L758-759, the background `nohup bash -lc "npm run dev"`, state file written), and only then verify_runtime -> wait_for_runtime, whose first statement is require_cmd curl (die 10). run_preflight (L719-733) checks node and npm but not curl.
- Impact: On a machine without curl, `npm run system:up` exits 10 with 'Required command not found: curl' while next dev keeps running in the background (port 3000 taken, PID file and state written). The developer must run `system:down`. `--skip-verify` hides the issue, `restart` repeats it.
- Fix: Check before starting anything: in cmd_up before `start_app` add `(( SKIP_VERIFY )) || require_cmd curl` (same for cmd_verify is already fine because nothing was started). Verifier on the fix: Correct and minimal: `(( SKIP_VERIFY )) || require_cmd curl` before start_app (or before run_bootstrap_sequence so a missing curl fails before the install and migration steps). No behaviour risk.
- Fix risk: None beyond the new early exit; test with PATH lacking curl and with --skip-verify.
- Found by: R5-U26 (W34); candidate H-016
- Resolution: FIXED by T-F20 (batch B4, 2026-10-13): `up` checks that curl exists before it starts the dev server, so a missing curl exits fatally with nothing left running (probe cases K5, K5d: no app.pid, no state.env, no 'npm run dev' after the exit 10). `restart` without curl still stops the old app first (K5d: noted, not changed).

### R-759: PwaManager detects iPadOS with the deprecated navigator.platform
- Severity: Nit
- Category: Legacy
- Status: CONFIRMED
- Location: src/components/PwaManager.tsx:L77
- Evidence:
  `const isIOS = /iPad|iPhone|iPod/.test(navigator.userAgent) || (navigator.platform === 'MacIntel' && hasTouch);`
  Independent verifier (W1b): src/components/PwaManager.tsx:76-77 `const hasTouch = 'maxTouchPoints' in navigator ? navigator.maxTouchPoints > 1 : false; const isIOS = /iPad|iPhone|iPod/.test(navigator.userAgent) || (navigator.platform === 'MacIntel' && hasTouch);`. node_modules/typescript/lib/lib.dom.d.ts:21553-21557 (TypeScript 5.9.3): `@deprecated ... readonly platform: string;`; my language-service run reports TS6385 'platform' is deprecated at L77. grep for 'navigator.platform|MacIntel|"platform"' in src and tests: only this line. The candidate's fixRisk is wrong: tests/components/pwa-manager.test.tsx never sets navigator.platform (it sets only navigator.userAgent via IPHONE_USER_AGENT at L161 and L234), so the iPadOS branch (MacIntel + touch) has no test at all. No REVIEW.md hit.
- Problem: TS6385 reports `'platform' is deprecated` here: `navigator.platform === 'MacIntel' && hasTouch` is the iPadOS-13+ detection (desktop-class Safari reports a Macintosh user agent and `MacIntel`). TypeScript 5.9.3's lib.dom.d.ts marks `readonly platform: string` `@deprecated`. The line already computes `hasTouch` from `navigator.maxTouchPoints`.
- Impact: None today: every current browser still returns the value. The only effect is the iOS add-to-home-screen tip; a browser that stops reporting `MacIntel` would stop showing it on iPad.
- Fix: Test the user agent instead: `(/Macintosh/.test(navigator.userAgent) && hasTouch)`, which is the equivalent check without the deprecated property (the user agent of iPadOS desktop-class Safari contains `Macintosh`). Verifier on the fix: `/Macintosh/.test(navigator.userAgent) && hasTouch` is equivalent in practice for iPadOS desktop-class Safari, but it swaps one sniff for another with no benefit while every browser still returns the value. If done, add a test with a Macintosh user agent and maxTouchPoints 5 (none exists); the stated need to adapt pwa-manager.test.tsx is incorrect.
- Fix risk: Low; the component test of the iOS tip (tests/components/pwa-manager.test.tsx) sets `navigator.platform`: it would have to set the user agent instead.
- Found by: lead-W0 (W1b); candidate L-004
- Resolution: DECLINED by decision D13 (2026-10-13, the owner's delegate): Swaps one browser sniff for another with no benefit while every browser still returns the value; consistent with the declined deprecations R-431, R-433 and R-562.

### R-760: Header is-scrolled (border and raised shadow) is missing after a reload or hash load that restores a scroll offset
- Severity: Nit
- Category: Bug
- Status: CONFIRMED
- Location: src/components/shell/SiteHeader.tsx:L43
- Evidence:
  `const { scrolled } = useScroll(24);`
  Independent verifier (W2): src/hooks/useScroll.ts:4 `const [scrolled, setScrolled] = useState(false);` and :24-26 the effect only does `window.addEventListener('scroll', onScroll, { passive: true })` with no initial onScroll(); the only caller is SiteHeader.tsx:43 `const { scrolled } = useScroll(24);` (class at :79 `scrolled && 'is-scrolled'`); shell.css:98 `.site-header.is-scrolled { border-color: var(--color-border); box-shadow: var(--shadow-raised); }`. Executed (W2-VA/d016.cjs, /en/apartment 1440x900, light, reduced motion): y=0 class 'site-header site-header--marketing', border rgba(0,0,0,0); scrollTo(0,700): class '... is-scrolled', border rgba(28,37,40,0.13); page.reload (browser restores y=700): class without is-scrolled, border rgba(0,0,0,0), rest shadow; scrollBy(0,1): is-scrolled returns; hard load /en#contact (y 6508): no is-scrolled; soft navigation to /en/apartment (y 0): correct. W2-VA/d016b.cjs with --disable-features=BackForwardCache: leave at y 900, goBack restores y 900 and the class lacks is-scrolled (in d016.cjs a goBack with bfcache kept the class because the page state was restored, so the back/forward part of the impact holds only for pages that are not bfcached). Unit proof (W2-VA/vt/usescroll.test.tsx, jsdom, renderHook): window.scrollY = 700 at mount gives scrolled=false with the current hook and true with a scratch copy that adds `onScroll();` after addEventListener. R-558 and R-481 (both DECLINED) concern the dead `hidden` state, not this initial state.
- Problem: useScroll (src/hooks/useScroll.ts) starts with `useState(false)` and only recomputes in a scroll listener; it never reads window.scrollY on mount, so a page that opens already scrolled keeps the unscrolled header until the first scroll event. Executed in puppeteer on /en/apartment: scrollTo(0,700) -> class 'is-scrolled', border rgba(242,235,223,0.12); reload (browser restores y 700) -> class 'site-header site-header--marketing' with a transparent border; scrollBy(0,1) -> 'is-scrolled' returns. Also on a hard load of /en#contact (y 7030): class lacks 'is-scrolled'. A soft navigation to a new page clears it correctly (y 0).
- Impact: Cosmetic: after reload, back/forward restore or a #hash load the glass pill has no border and a lighter shadow until the user scrolls by one pixel (visible only as a thin hairline in the screenshots).
- Fix: In useScroll's effect call `onScroll()` once after adding the listener (src/hooks/useScroll.ts, outside this unit), or compute the initial state from window.scrollY. Verifier on the fix: Correct and minimal, verified on a scratch copy: one `onScroll();` after addEventListener makes the hook true at mount; site-shell.test.tsx passes 33/33 with it; `react-hooks/set-state-in-effect` is 'off' in eslint.config.mjs:14 so lint will not flag the setState in the effect. FixRisk 'trivial' is fair. Cosmetic and self-healing on the first scroll, so Nit stands.
- Fix risk: Trivial; one extra setState on mount. Keep the `hidden` branch untouched (R-558 was declined).
- Found by: R5-U11 (W2); candidate D-016
- Resolution: FIXED by T-F23 (batch B4, 2026-10-13): useScroll calls its handler once after adding the scroll listener, so the header's is-scrolled state is right after a reload or a hash load that restores a scroll offset. Evidence: RED 1 failed / 4 passed (fix/logs/T-F23-red.log), GREEN 5/5; lead check in real Chromium on the production build (fix/logs/B4-lead-shell.log): reload at scrollY 600 on /en/moments gives scrollY 610 and the class 'site-header site-header--guide is-scrolled'. Patch R5-T-F23.patch.

### R-761: useGuestSession turns a signed-in guest into 'signed out' on any non-OK status, so a transient 5xx shows 'Sign in' and locked tiles while T08 keeps the portal flags
- Severity: Nit (the finder said Low: The finder's trigger is wrong: a database restart does not give a 5xx here. In production getFeatureFlagsAsync() swallows a failed read and returns the disabled defaults (featureFlags.ts L38-L47), so [...])
- Category: Logic
- Status: CONFIRMED
- Location: src/hooks/useGuestSession.ts:L30-L33
- Evidence:
  ```
  const body = res.ok ? await res.json().catch(() => null) : null;
              const signedIn = body?.data?.authenticated === true;
              if (version === requestVersion.current) {
                  setIsSignedIn(signedIn);
  ```
  Independent verifier (W1a): Read useGuestSession.ts L28-L43: `const body = res.ok ? await res.json().catch(() => null) : null; const signedIn = body?.data?.authenticated === true; if (version === requestVersion.current) { setIsSignedIn(signedIn); ... if (res.ok) {...} else if (res.status === 404) {...} }` -> every non-2xx status sets isSignedIn false while the flags stay; the catch branch preserves state. Executed (scratch jsdom vitest on a copy of src, 3 runs): signed-in guest (200, authenticated true), then a focus event answered with 503 / 502 / 500 / 429 -> {isSignedIn:false, portalEnabled:true, checkinEnabled:true}; answered with a network error -> {isSignedIn:true, ...}. Consumers: SiteHeader.tsx L111 (Sign out only when isSignedIn), MobileMenu.tsx L109-L128, StaySessionTiles.tsx L19-L30. `setIsSignedIn(signedIn)` for every status predates T08 (git diff f7958fa..HEAD shows only the flag lines added); tests/components/guest-session-hook.test.tsx L98-L113 assert the flags only after a 5xx. CORRECTION to the finder's impact (executed): with the repository's route, prisma.operationalSetting.findUnique rejected + NODE_ENV=production -> HTTP 404 (development -> 200). Not covered by an existing finding (R-481, R-482, R-537 mention the hook but not statuses).
- Problem: For every response that is not 2xx, body is null, so signedIn is false and setIsSignedIn(false) runs. T08 added the line below it ('200: the portal is on. 404: it is off. Other statuses say nothing about the flags.') and its tests pin that a 503 or a network error keeps portalEnabled and checkinEnabled. isSignedIn was left out of that contract. The result is an inconsistent state: portalEnabled true, checkinEnabled true, isSignedIn false. Evidence: a scratch test in a copy of the repo (not in the real tree): first fetch answers 200 {authenticated:true,checkinEnabled:true}, then a window 'focus' event with fetch answering 503. Result: AssertionError: expected { signedIn: false, portal: true, …(1) } to deeply equal { signedIn: true, portal: true, …(1) }, with the diff showing only signedIn differing (received false, expected true). The catch branch (network error) does preserve the state, so only HTTP error statuses behave differently. No existing test asserts isSignedIn after a 5xx (guest-session-hook.test.tsx 'keeps the last known portal and check-in flags on $name' checks the flags only).
- Impact: GET /api/portal/sessions reads the feature flags from the database on every call (src/app/api/portal/sessions/route.ts L23), so it answers 5xx when the database restarts during a deploy, and an Nginx 502/504 does the same. A signed-in guest whose /stay tab regains focus during that window sees StaySessionTiles locked, loses the header 'Sign out' button, and (new with T08's gating) the mobile menu shows 'Sign in' instead of 'Check-in'/'Sign out', until the next focus, visibility change or the 5-minute poll. The session cookie is still valid; the state self-heals. Cosmetic and confusing, not a security or data problem.
- Fix: Treat only 200 and 404 as answers about the session: ```diff if (version === requestVersion.current) { - setIsSignedIn(signedIn); + // Only 200 and 404 are answers; any other status keeps the last known state, as the catch does. + if (res.ok || res.status === 404) setIsSignedIn(signedIn); ``` and add to tests/components/guest-session-hook.test.tsx: signed in, then 503 (and a rejected fetch), expect isSignedIn to stay true. Verifier on the fix: Minimal fix is right and tested in the scratch copy: move `setIsSignedIn(signedIn)` into the `res.ok` branch and call `setIsSignedIn(false)` in the 404 branch, so only 200 and 404 are authoritative. All 12 existing tests of guest-session-hook.test.tsx still pass and the probe keeps isSignedIn true on 500/502/503/429. Add a row 'keeps the signed-in state on a 5xx answer' beside L98-L113. Fix risk: a guest who really lost the session during a proxy blip is shown as signed in until the next 200/404 answer; the server still enforces auth, so only labels are affected.
- Fix risk: A 401/403 from an intermediary would no longer sign the UI out; the status route itself never answers those for a signed-out visitor (it answers 200 authenticated:false). Re-run tests/components/guest-session-hook.test.tsx, site-shell.test.tsx and stay-routes.test.tsx.
- Found by: R5-X1, R5-U1 (W1a); candidate C-016; also found independently by R5-U11 (wave 2a, D-012: executed in Chrome at 390 px, a 503, 429 or 500 answer to the session poll on a window focus event turns the menu of a signed-in guest into Sign in; the next 200 restores Check-in and Sign out)
- Resolution: FIXED by T-F24 (batch B4, 2026-10-13): useGuestSession keeps the guest signed in on a transient answer (503, 500, 429 and a network error) instead of turning the UI to 'signed out'; a 404 still signs out (existing test). Evidence: RED 3 failed / 13 passed (the 503, 500 and 429 rows; fix/logs/T-F24-red.log), GREEN 16/16. Accepted risk named by the finding: a 401 or 403 from an intermediary no longer signs the UI out (the status route answers 200 with authenticated:false for a signed-out visitor). Patch R5-T-F24.patch.

### R-764: Nits (grouped, logger configuration): LOG_MAX_METADATA_SIZE below 120 empties every over-limit metadata object and a non-numeric value removes the cap; LOG_STRUCTURED=true prints indented multi-line JSON and an unsanitized circular error cause makes the logger throw
- Severity: Nit
- Category: Maintainability
- Status: CONFIRMED
- Location: src/lib/logger-enterprise.ts:L149-L155
- Evidence:
  ```
  if (serialized.length > this.config.maxMetadataSize) {
        const previewBudget = Math.max(0, this.config.maxMetadataSize - 120);
        return {
          _truncated: true,
          _originalSize: serialized.length,
          _preview: serialized.slice(0, previewBudget),
        };
  ```
  Independent verifier (W1a): Executed with the real logger (fresh module per env, scratch vitest) on a 215-byte metadata object: LOG_MAX_METADATA_SIZE=1000 and 300 -> logged whole; 119, 100 and 0 -> {"_truncated":true,"_originalSize":215,"_preview":""} (previewBudget = Math.max(0, size - 120) is 0 for any size <= 120); 'abc' -> parseInt gives NaN, `serialized.length > NaN` is false, nothing is ever truncated. runtime-env-schema.js L119 `LOG_MAX_METADATA_SIZE: optionalEnv(z.string().regex(/^\d+$/))` accepts 0-119, and the constructor comment (logger-enterprise.ts L77-L78) says the workers do not run the schema. LOG_STRUCTURED=true: output is `JSON.stringify(entry, null, 2)` (L217): 8 lines for a one-field entry; with an Error whose `cause` is { self: <itself> }, logger.error THROWS 'TypeError: Converting circular structure to JSON' (L173 passes `cause` through unsanitised); the non-structured control prints without throwing. grep of REVIEW.md for LOG_MAX_METADATA, LOG_STRUCTURED, maxMetadataSize: nothing.

Executed (scratch logger-config-probe.ts): LOG_MAX_METADATA_SIZE=100 and =0 -> 'probe-metadata { _truncated: true, _originalSize: 217, _preview: "" }' (all metadata lost); =abc -> parseInt gives NaN, `length > NaN` is false and the metadata is never truncated. (b) With LOG_STRUCTURED=true the entry is printed by `JSON.stringify(entry, null, 2)` (L217): one 13-line pretty-printed block per entry in the probe, so a line-oriented collector (docker logs) sees fragments; `entry.error.cause` (L173) is not sanitized, and `JSON.stringify` on a circular cause throws: 'circular cause: THROWS TypeError: Converting circular structure to JSON' (an Error with `cause = { self: <itself> }`).
- Impact: Only when someone sets these knobs: LOG_MAX_METADATA_SIZE=100 to cut log volume removes the content of every larger metadata object; LOG_STRUCTURED=true in production yields logs that cannot be parsed per line, and a circular cause can raise out of logger.error.
- Fix: Clamp the budget (for example `Number.isInteger(n) && n >= 200 ? n : 1000`) and use `z.string().regex(/^\d{3,6}$/)`; print structured entries with `JSON.stringify(entry)` (one line) and pass `cause` through sanitizeMetadata or reduce it to name and message. Verifier on the fix: Parse LOG_MAX_METADATA_SIZE as a strict integer with a floor (ignore non-numeric values and values below about 200 and use 1000, as the constructor already does for LOG_LEVEL); in structured mode print single-line `JSON.stringify(entry)` and run `cause` through the sanitiser or reduce it to name and message. Same file as C-021, one task. Fix risk low: tests/unit/logger-enterprise.test.ts stubs LOG_STRUCTURED=false and LOG_MAX_METADATA_SIZE=1000, so add rows for the new branches; a collector that already parses the pretty-printed form would see a format change. Nit is right: config knobs that [...]
- Fix risk: Tests that assert the structured output format; nobody sets LOG_STRUCTURED today (.env.example sets false).

### R-765: A claim token with less than one second left answers 500 instead of 401
- Severity: Nit
- Category: Error handling
- Status: CONFIRMED
- Location: src/lib/portalClaimExchange.ts:L36-L39
- Evidence:
  ```
  const grantLifetimeSeconds = Math.floor((grantExpiresAt.getTime() - now.getTime()) / 1_000);
    if (grantLifetimeSeconds < 1) {
      throw new Error('Portal claim exchange grant is already expired');
    }
  ```
  Independent verifier (W1a): Read portalClaimExchange.ts L36-L39 (`Math.floor((grantExpiresAt.getTime() - now.getTime()) / 1_000)`; `< 1` throws a plain Error), portalAuthService.ts L173-L177 (prepare accepts every grant with expiresAt > now) and claim-exchange/route.ts L40-L51 (createPortalClaimExchangeCookie is called after the database round trip with a later `now`; the catch maps only PortalAuthError and rethrows the rest). apiErrorHandler.ts L353-L372: an unknown Error becomes 500 INTERNAL_ERROR plus `logger.error('Unexpected API error', ...)`. Executed (real createPortalClaimExchangeCookie, fixed now): 1000, 1001 and 1999 ms left -> maxAge 1; 2000 -> 2; 999, 500 and 1 ms left -> THROWS Error 'Portal claim exchange grant is already expired'. tests/security/claim-token-transport.test.ts L327-L332 pin only the 75-second case. R-604 (cookie lifetime) is adjacent, not the same; grep for 'already expired' in REVIEW.md: nothing.
- Problem: prepareBookingClaimExchange accepts every grant with `expiresAt > now` (portalAuthService.ts L173-L177), then the route calls createPortalClaimExchangeCookie with a later `now`. Any remaining lifetime in (0, 1000) ms floors to 0 and throws a plain Error. The route's catch (claim-exchange/route.ts L51-L56) maps only PortalAuthError, rethrows the rest, and withErrorHandler answers 500 INTERNAL_ERROR and logs 'Unexpected API error' at error level. Executed (scratch cookie-edge.mts): 1000 ms left gives maxAge 1; 999, 500 and 1 ms left throw 'Portal claim exchange grant is already expired'. tests/security/claim-token-transport.test.ts pins the 75-second case only.
- Impact: A guest who submits the token in the last second of its validity gets 'Something went wrong' and an error-level log line instead of the 'token invalid, expired or already used' message. The window is under one second per token, so the practical effect is tiny.
- Fix: Reject it as expired in prepareBookingClaimExchange: replace `grant.expiresAt <= now` by `grant.expiresAt.getTime() - now.getTime() < 1_000`, or catch the expired case in the route and answer 401. Verifier on the fix: Correct and small: in createPortalClaimExchangeCookie keep the throw only for `grantExpiresAt <= now` and use `Math.max(1, Math.floor(...))` for the lifetime, so a grant with under a second left gets a 1-second cookie and the claims route answers its normal 401 (the transaction rejects the expired grant). Fix risk low; add rows for 999 ms (maxAge 1) and an already expired grant (throws) next to L327-L332. Nit is right: window under one second per token.
- Fix risk: tests/security/claim-token-transport.test.ts and tests/unit/claim-grant-issuance.test.ts; a grant with under one second left becomes unusable one second early, which is irrelevant.
- Found by: R5-U1 (W1a); candidate C-028
- Resolution: FIXED by T-F35 (batch B6, 2026-10-13): createPortalClaimExchangeCookie throws 'already expired' only when the remaining lifetime is 0 or negative; a lifetime of less than one second gets maxAge 1 (Math.max(1, floor(ms/1000)), capped at 300), so such a token no longer produces a 500 instead of the 401 path. Evidence: RED 2 failed / 26 passed (999 ms and 1 ms left; fix/logs/T-F35-red.log), GREEN 33/33 (rows for 999, 1, 1000, 1999 and 2000 ms, the 300 s cap and three expired grants); integration suite passed; B6 verifier PASS (the 'no 500' is shown at unit level; no route-level test, none required). Patch R5-T-F35.patch.

### R-766: Nit: prismaPgConfig reads URL parameters with parseInt, so a unit-suffixed value such as statement_timeout=5s becomes 5 milliseconds
- Severity: Nit
- Category: Logic
- Status: CONFIRMED
- Location: src/lib/prismaPgConfig.ts:L26-L30
- Evidence:
  ```
  function parsePositiveInteger(value: string | null): number | undefined {
    if (!value) return undefined;
    const parsed = Number.parseInt(value, 10);
    return Number.isFinite(parsed) && parsed > 0 ? parsed : undefined;
  }
  ```
  Independent verifier (W1a): Read prismaPgConfig.ts L26-L30 and L50-L57 (unchanged since f7958fa except the TimeZone pin). Executed (scratch vitest, real buildPrismaPgAdapterArgs): `?statement_timeout=5s` -> statement_timeout 5; `?statement_timeout=30s` -> 30 (ms); `?statement_timeout=1.5` -> 1; `?statement_timeout=5000ms` -> 5000; `?connect_timeout=10s` -> connectionTimeoutMillis 10000; `?connection_limit=20x` -> max 20; `?statement_timeout=0&lock_timeout=abc&connection_limit=0` -> defaults kept. The three *_timeout parameters are milliseconds (DEFAULT_*_MS constants assigned to pg's statement_timeout/query_timeout/lock_timeout). grep of README.md, scripts/README.md, docs, docker, .env.example and CLAUDE.md for statement_timeout|connection_limit|pool_timeout: no hit, so the levers are undocumented. Related decision, not a conflict: R-582 keeps the nine-parameter shim as the only pool-size lever; this finding asks only for stricter parsing.
- Problem: parseInt accepts trailing text, and the three parameters statement_timeout, query_timeout and lock_timeout are milliseconds (the DEFAULT_* constants) while connect_timeout, pool_timeout and the two lifetime parameters are seconds; nothing documents the parameters (grep in docs, README, scripts/README.md, docker: no hit). Executed (scratch pg-config-probe.ts): `?statement_timeout=5s` -> config.statement_timeout = 5 (ms); `?connection_limit=0&statement_timeout=0&lock_timeout=abc` -> ignored, defaults kept.
- Impact: An operator who writes PostgreSQL's own notation (`statement_timeout=30s`) in DATABASE_URL gets a 30 ms statement timeout and every non-trivial query fails with 'canceling statement due to statement timeout'. Requires someone to use an undocumented lever.
- Fix: Parse strictly: `/^[0-9]+$/.test(value) ? Number(value) : undefined` (and document the units next to PRISMA_URL_PARAMS), or reject the whole URL with a clear error. Verifier on the fix: Correct and one line: accept only /^[0-9]+$/ (`/^[0-9]+$/.test(value) ? Number.parseInt(value, 10) : undefined`) so '5s', '1.5' and '20x' fall back to the default instead of a wrong tiny value. Fix risk very low: a URL with a unit suffix would revert to the default; add one row to tests/unit/prisma-adapter-config.test.ts. Optionally document the parameters in one .env.example comment. Nit is fair: undocumented lever, no known user.
- Fix risk: tests/unit/prisma-adapter-config.test.ts rows; a production DATABASE_URL that currently carries a suffixed value would fall back to the defaults.
- Found by: R5-U3 (W1a); candidate C-023
- Resolution: FIXED by T-F36 (batch B6, 2026-10-13): parsePositiveInteger in prismaPgConfig.ts accepts only plain digits (`/^[0-9]+$/`), so a unit-suffixed or fractional value such as statement_timeout=5s, 1.5 or 20x falls back to the default instead of becoming 5 milliseconds; a comment gives the units (ms for statement, query and lock timeouts, seconds for the rest). Evidence: RED 10 failed / 4 passed (fix/logs/T-F36-red.log), GREEN 14/14 (10 rows over all 8 numeric parameters, each asserting the full default config); integration suite passed; B6 verifier PASS. The optional .env.example note was not made (outside the allowed paths; economy). Patch R5-T-F36.patch.

### R-776: The migration fixture claims to re-create country_origin 'as 000_init defined' it, but makes the column nullable where 000_init has NOT NULL
- Severity: Nit
- Category: Maintainability
- Status: CONFIRMED
- Location: tests/integration/minimise-user-data-migration.test.ts:L64-L66
- Evidence:
  ```
  // Re-creates the pre-migration shape of the two columns as 000_init defined them.
  const ADD_COLUMNS = `CREATE TYPE "CountryOrigin" AS ENUM ('GR', 'ABROAD');
    ALTER TABLE users ADD COLUMN country_origin "CountryOrigin";
  ```
  Independent verifier (W34): tests/integration/minimise-user-data-migration.test.ts L64-L66: comment `// Re-creates the pre-migration shape of the two columns as 000_init defined them.` and `ALTER TABLE users ADD COLUMN country_origin "CountryOrigin";` (nullable). prisma/migrations/000_init/migration.sql L25: `"country_origin" "CountryOrigin" NOT NULL`; grep DROP NOT NULL over prisma/migrations finds only a stay_request_id change (20260714150000), so no migration relaxes users.country_origin. The migration header (20260930120000_minimise_user_data/migration.sql L7) says 'country_origin is NOT NULL, so its guard refuses on any user row at all'. insertUser('NULL', ...) in the cases at L127 ('refuses while a user still holds an email address') and L130+ ('drops leftover columns when no user holds a value and keeps the user') therefore builds a user that cannot exist at the previous migration. Each guard predicate is still exercised in isolation (valid), only the comment overstates fidelity. REVIEW.md R-477 mentions 'a nullable country_origin' once in its Problem text (L8770+), not the misleading comment.
- Problem: prisma/migrations/000_init/migration.sql L25 declares `"country_origin" "CountryOrigin" NOT NULL`, and no later migration relaxes it (grep over prisma/migrations finds only an index, a CASE expression and the minimise migration itself). The fixture adds the column without NOT NULL, so every case may insert a user with country_origin NULL. A database at the previous migration cannot hold such a user: every user row has a country_origin, so the migration's first guard refuses on any user (migration header L7: 'its guard refuses on any user row at all'). The cases 'refuses while a user still holds an email address' and 'drops leftover columns when no user holds a value and keeps the user' therefore run on an unreachable state. They do test each guard predicate in isolation, which is valid, but the comment claims a fidelity the fixture does not have, and the header property (any user row is refused) is never shown against the real NOT NULL shape. R-477 mentions the nullable column only in passing.
- Impact: No wrong result. A reader takes the two cases for reachable upgrade scenarios (a user without a country origin exists and the upgrade passes) and may misjudge what an upgrade of a database with users does: it refuses.
- Fix: Comment only: '// Simplified pre-migration shape: country_origin is nullable here so that each guard can be tested alone; 000_init defines it NOT NULL, so a real user row always trips the first guard.' Verifier on the fix: Comment-only fix is correct and sufficient; no code or test behaviour changes. Suggested wording (nullable here so each guard can be tested alone; 000_init defines NOT NULL, so a real user row always trips the first guard) is accurate. Alternatively make the fixture exact (NOT NULL) and drop the two unreachable cases, but that removes tests (O36/O46 spirit) and is not needed.
- Fix risk: None, comment only.

Case 2 (L195-L209) asserts `privacyRequest.count()` = 1 and the audit count = 1 (L206-L207) without reading them before eraseGuestForRetention. In the skip path (privacyService.ts L122-L129) the request created by the call is deleted and nothing else is written, so the 1/1 are exactly case 1's leftovers. The assertion cannot tell 'the skip left nothing behind' (its claim) from 'the count still equals what case 1 produced'. ### R-778: The integration seeding client is not pinned to a UTC session although the application client is (R-510), so the timestamp seeds of the operations tests are right only while the image defaults to UTC
- Severity: Nit (the finder said Low: Latent only: the image is pinned by exact tag and index digest (postgres-image-policy.ts L112-L116 rejects any other reference) and the integration suite already contains a canary that fails visibly [...])
- Category: Tests
- Status: SUSPECTED
- Location: tests/integration/support/fixtures.ts:L71-L77
- Evidence:
  ```
  const adapter = new PrismaPg({
        connectionString: target.databaseUrl,
        connectionTimeoutMillis: 3_000,
        statement_timeout: 5_000,
        query_timeout: 5_000,
        ssl: false,
      });
  ```
  Independent verifier (W34): tests/integration/support/fixtures.ts L71-L77 builds `new PrismaPg({ connectionString, connectionTimeoutMillis, statement_timeout, query_timeout, ssl: false })` with no `options`; src/lib/prismaPgConfig.ts L43-L45 pins `options: '-c TimeZone=UTC'` for the app pool. Installed @prisma/adapter-pg 7.10.0: formatDateTime (dist/index.js L389-L392) emits getUTC* wall-clock text without offset; normalize_timestamptz (L310-L312) replaces the offset of every read with +00:00, so both are right only in a UTC session. grep -rn 'TimeZone' tests finds only tests/unit/prisma-adapter-config.test.ts; no integration case asserts the zone, and R-510's 'optionally assert SHOW TimeZone' (REVIEW.md L11291) was not done. Docker run args (database-lifecycle.ts L227-L248) pass only POSTGRES_USER/PASSWORD/DB, no TZ. Indirect evidence that the pinned image is UTC today: calendar-sync.test.ts L210-L216 seeds lastSuccessAt = now - 4 h through the unpinned test client and requires the app (pinned UTC) to read >=240 and <245 minutes; .runtime/review5/w0/integration.rc is rc=0 with 'Tests 125 passed (125)', which would fail with any non-zero zone offset. I could not run SHOW TimeZone (Docker).
- Problem: src/lib/prismaPgConfig.ts L43-L45 pins the application pool with `options: '-c TimeZone=UTC'` because adapter-pg 7.10.0 formats Date parameters as UTC wall-clock text without an offset (formatDateTime, node_modules/@prisma/adapter-pg/dist/index.js L389-L392) and replaces the offset of every timestamptz it reads with +00:00 (normalize_timestamptz, L310-L312); both are correct only in a UTC session (R-510, fixed by T41). withTestPrismaClient builds its own PrismaPg without that option, and the operations tests seed and read timestamptz through it while the code under test runs on the pinned client: calendar-sync.test.ts updateState/readState/afterEach (nextAttemptAt, lastSuccessAt), check-in-request-repository.test.ts (exhausted() nextAttemptAt, deliveredAt, claimedAt, the nextAttemptAt read-back at L234), outbox-dead-lifecycle.test.ts (delivered_at parameter), guest-data-retention.test.ts (claimedAt). Both sides agree only while the server's default TimeZone is UTC. I could not check that for the pinned image (no Docker), and no test asserts it (`grep -rn TimeZone tests/integration` finds nothing). The file belongs to unit U24b; reported here because the effect shows in my tests.
- Impact: If the pinned image or its configuration ever defaults to another zone, every seed shifts by the zone offset: with +03 the stale-calendar case writes 'now - 4 h' as 'now - 7 h' and the app reads 420 minutes (the `< 245` check turns red), and a due event can look not due. The failures would point at the application code, not at the harness. Nothing fails today.
- Fix: Add `options: '-c TimeZone=UTC'` to the PrismaPg config in withTestPrismaClient (as prismaPgConfig.ts L45) and, as R-510 suggested, assert `SHOW TimeZone` = 'UTC' once through the application client in an integration case. Verifier on the fix: The one-line `options: '-c TimeZone=UTC'` in withTestPrismaClient is correct (pg sends options in the startup packet, same key the app uses) and a `SHOW TimeZone` assertion makes the premise explicit. Fix risk fair: touches the shared harness, so a full npm run test:integration is needed. Closest existing items: R-510 (FIXED by T41, optional integration assertion never added) and R-605 (ACCEPTED); neither covers the seeding client. Worth doing only if the owner wants harness parity; not urgent.
- Fix risk: Harness change used by every integration file: run the whole npm run test:integration. The session option is already used by the application client, so no new behaviour.
- To confirm: Add a `SHOW TimeZone` query (expect 'UTC') to a verification step through the application client and the harness client and run npm run test:integration; if it returns UTC the finding stays latent. Run request: npm run test:integration with a temporary `SHOW TimeZone` assertion in any integration file (Docker, lead only)
- Found by: R5-U24a (W34); candidate G-018

### R-788: The log-format deny-list is narrower than the template's own comment and misses braced and upper-case spellings
- Severity: Low
- Category: Security
- Status: SUSPECTED
- Location: scripts/lib/release-policy.mjs:L221-L222 (NGINX_FORBIDDEN_LOG_VARIABLE); tests/security/claim-token-transport.test.ts:L334-L336
- Evidence:
  ```
  not denied: $arg_<name>, $request_body, $http_cf_connecting_ip, $verified_client_ip, $origin_proxy_attestation; ${remote_addr} (braced) and $Remote_Addr (upper case)
  ```
- Problem: If nginx accepts the braced and case-folded spellings in log_format, a debugging edit can put the query string or client address into access.log without failing the policy; only `origin_safe` is constrained (a second access_log with the combined format still passes).
- Impact: Possible logging of query strings or client addresses that the claim-token transport contract forbids.
- Fix: Match the braced and case-insensitive forms in both places, add the other variables, constrain every access_log.
- Fix risk: Patterns must stay linear (security/detect-unsafe-regex runs on scripts and tests).
- To confirm (SUSPECTED only): run `nginx -t` and one request in the pinned image with `${remote_addr}` in a log_format.
- Found by: T-F05 implementer; B1 verifier
- Resolution: DEFERRED-OWNER (economy): not scheduled under the owner's instruction of 2026-10-13 to watch the consumption; resumable on request.

### R-789: The worker's private-page guards compare the raw pathname, so a percent-encoded variant may pass
- Severity: Low
- Category: Security

  ```

- Fix: Compare the decoded and normalised pathname.

- To confirm (SUSPECTED only): request the encoded URL in the production build with the worker active and list the cache.

### R-791: `npm run db:studio` and `db:generate` never reach the DIRECT_URL guard of the orchestrator
- Severity: Low
- Category: Bug

  ```
- Problem: prisma.config.ts prefers DIRECT_URL, and Prisma Studio started this way does not pass through the guard added for `migrate`; `-- --allow-remote-db` appended to the npm script goes to the Prisma command, not to the orchestrator.

- Fix risk: Low.

### R-795: `toSafeLocalPath` returns a protocol-relative `//host` string for dot-segment input (latent open redirect in a shared helper)
- Severity: Low
- Category: Security
- Status: CONFIRMED
- Location: src/lib/safeLocalPath.ts:L12-L31
- Evidence:
  ```
  "/.//evil.example" -> "//evil.example" | second pass: null
  "/en/..//evil.example" -> "//evil.example" | second pass: null
  "/a/..//evil.example/x?y=1#z" -> "//evil.example/x?y=1#z" | second pass: null
  ```
  Lead run with tsx and the base https://guest.test/start.
- Problem: The function returns `target.pathname + search + hash` of the parsed URL; the WHATWG parser keeps the empty segment of a dot-segment path, so the returned string reads as another origin when used on its own (`location.assign`, `href`).
- Impact: No reachable open redirect today: the portal refresh flow validates twice (the second pass rejects the already normalised value) and OfflineActions refuses a result that starts with `//` (T-F09). Any new single-pass caller would be exposed.
- Fix: Return null when the canonical pathname starts with `//`; add the three inputs to tests/unit/core-utilities.test.ts (strengthen only, O36/O46).
- Fix risk: Low; callers already treat null as unsafe.
- Found by: T-F09 implementer; reproduced by the lead (batch B2)
- Resolution: DEFERRED-OWNER (economy): not scheduled under the owner's instruction of 2026-10-13 to watch the consumption; a one-line fix plus tests, resumable on request (recommended first, because it is the only security item among the new findings).
